# Transaction management

# [&lt;start transaction command&gt;](#_bookmark1088)

**Function**

Start a new GQL-transaction and set its characteristics.

# Format

&lt;start transaction command&gt; ::=

START TRANSACTION \[ [&lt;transaction characteristics&gt;](#_bookmark1096) \]

# Syntax Rules

1. Let _TS_ be the [&lt;start transaction command&gt;](#_bookmark1088).
2. If _TS_ does not simply contain [&lt;transaction characteristics&gt;](#_bookmark1096), then an implementation-defined [(ID006)](#_bookmark6121) default transaction characteristics that simply contains a [&lt;transaction mode&gt;](#_bookmark1098) READ WRITE is

implicit.

# General Rules

1. If a GQL-transaction is currently active, then an exception condition is raised: _invalid transaction state — active GQL-transaction (25G01)_.
2. Let _TC_ be the explicit or implicit [&lt;transaction characteristics&gt;](#_bookmark1096) simply contained in _TS_.
3. A new GQL-transaction _TX_ with the transaction characteristics specified by _TC_ as its transaction characteristics is initiated.

NOTE 170 — Every transaction records its transaction characteristics.

1. The current transaction is set to _TX_.

NOTE 171 — This determines _TX_ as the currently active GQL-transaction associated with the GQL-session of the currently executing GQL-request.

# Conformance Rules

1. Without Feature GT02, “Specified transaction characteristics”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [&lt;start transaction command&gt;](#_bookmark1088) that contains [&lt;transaction characteristics&gt;](#_bookmark1096).
    1. [**&lt;transaction characteristics&gt;**](#_bookmark1096)

# [&lt;transaction characteristics&gt;](#_bookmark1096) Function

Specify GQL-transaction characteristics.

# Format

&lt;transaction characteristics&gt; ::=

[&lt;transaction mode&gt;](#_bookmark1098) \[ { [&lt;comma&gt;](#_bookmark5022) [&lt;transaction mode&gt;](#_bookmark1098) }... \]

&lt;transaction mode&gt; ::=

[&lt;transaction access mode&gt;](#_bookmark1099)

| [&lt;implementation-defined access mode&gt;](#_bookmark1101)

&lt;transaction access mode&gt; ::= READ ONLY

| READ WRITE

&lt;implementation-defined access mode&gt; ::=

!! _See the Syntax Rules._

# Syntax Rules

1. Let _TC_ be the [&lt;transaction characteristics&gt;](#_bookmark1096).
2. _TC_ shall contain exactly one [&lt;transaction access mode&gt;](#_bookmark1099).
3. The Format and Syntax Rules for [&lt;implementation-defined access mode&gt;](#_bookmark1101) are implementation- defined [(IE002)](#_bookmark6159).

# General Rules

_None._

# Conformance Rules

_None._

- 1. [**&lt;rollback command&gt;**](#_bookmark1105)

# [&lt;rollback command&gt;](#_bookmark1105)

**Function**

Terminate the currently active GQL-transaction with rollback.

# Format

&lt;rollback command&gt; ::= ROLLBACK

# Syntax Rules

_None._

# General Rules

1. If the currently active GQL-transaction is part of an encompassing transaction that is controlled by an agent other than the GQL-agent and the [&lt;rollback command&gt;](#_bookmark1105) is not being implicitly executed, then an exception condition is raised: _invalid transaction termination (2D000)_.
2. All changes to GQL-data or the GQL-catalog that were made by the currently active GQL-transaction are canceled.
3. The currently active GQL-transaction is terminated and the current transaction is set to “not set”.

# Conformance Rules

_None._

- 1. [**&lt;commit command&gt;**](#_bookmark1109)

# [&lt;commit command&gt;](#_bookmark1109) Function

Terminate the currently active GQL-transaction with commit.

# Format

&lt;commit command&gt; ::= COMMIT

# Syntax Rules

_None._

# General Rules

1. Case:
    1. If the currently active GQL-transaction is part of an encompassing transaction that is controlled by an agent other than the GQL-agent, then an exception condition is raised: _invalid transaction_ _termination (2D000)_.
    2. If any other error preventing commitment of the GQL-transaction has occurred, then any changes to GQL-data or the GQL-catalog that were made by the currently active GQL-transaction are canceled and an exception condition is raised: _transaction rollback (40000)_ with an

implementation-defined [(IE008)](#_bookmark6166) subclass value.

- 1. Otherwise, any changes to GQL-data or the GQL-catalog that were made by the currently active GQL-transaction are eligible to be perceived by all subsequent GQL-transactions.

1. The currently active GQL-transaction is terminated and the current transaction is set to “not set”.

# Conformance Rules

_None._

1. If a [&lt;procedure specification&gt;](#_bookmark1118) _PS_ is specified that is immediately contained in a [<transaction](#_bookmark971) [activity>](#_bookmark971), then:

    3. Let _BVDSEQ_ be the sequence of [&lt;binding variable definition&gt;](#_bookmark1140)s immediately contained in

_BVDBLK_, let _N_ be the number of elements of _BVDSEQ_.

  3. For _j_, 2 (two) ≤ _j_ ≤ _N_, the declared type of the incoming working record of _BVDj_ is the declared type of the outgoing working record of _BVDj_\-1.
  4. The declared type of the outgoing working record of _BVDBLK_ is the declared type of the out- going working record of _BVDN_.
  5. The declared type of the outgoing working table of _BVDBLK_ is the declared type of the incoming working table of _BVDBLK_.
  6. [**&lt;procedure body&gt;**](#_bookmark1137)

1. Let _SBLK_ be the [&lt;statement block&gt;](#_bookmark1144).
2. If _SBLK_ directly contains a [&lt;linear catalog-modifying statement&gt;](#_bookmark1265), then _SBLK_ shall directly contain at most one [&lt;statement&gt;](#_bookmark1145).
3. If _SBLK_ directly contains a [&lt;focused linear query statement&gt;](#_bookmark1585) or a [<focused linear data-modifying](#_bookmark1383) [statement>](#_bookmark1383), then _SBLK_ shall not directly contain an [&lt;ambient linear query statement&gt;](#_bookmark1594) or an

[&lt;ambient linear data-modifying statement&gt;](#_bookmark1389).

NOTE 173 — As a consequence of this rule, focused statements and ambient statement are mutually exclusive within a [&lt;statement block&gt;](#_bookmark1144), so that the following is true as well: If _SBLK_ directly contains an

[&lt;ambient linear query statement&gt;](#_bookmark1594) or an [&lt;ambient linear data-modifying statement&gt;](#_bookmark1389), then _SBLK_ does not directly contain a [&lt;focused linear query statement&gt;](#_bookmark1585) or a [&lt;focused linear data-modifying statement&gt;](#_bookmark1383).

1. If _SBLK_ directly contains a [&lt;linear query statement&gt;](#_bookmark1584) that is a [&lt;select statement&gt;](#_bookmark1758), then every [<linear](#_bookmark1584) [query statement>](#_bookmark1584) directly contained in _SBLK_ shall be a [&lt;select statement&gt;](#_bookmark1758).
2. If _SBLK_ directly contains a [&lt;linear query statement&gt;](#_bookmark1584) that contains a [&lt;primitive result statement&gt;](#_bookmark1690), then every [&lt;linear query statement&gt;](#_bookmark1584) directly contained in _SBLK_ shall contain a [<primitive result](#_bookmark1690) [statement>](#_bookmark1690).
3. Let _TSTMSEQ_ be the sequence of [&lt;next statement&gt;](#_bookmark1149)s immediately contained in _SBLK_, let _M_ be the number of elements of _TSTMSEQ_.
4. For _j_, 0 (zero) ≤ _j_ ≤ _M_, let the [&lt;statement&gt;](#_bookmark1145)s _STMj_ directly contained in _SBLK_ be defined as follows:
    1. _STM_0 is the [&lt;statement&gt;](#_bookmark1145) immediately contained in _SBLK_.

5. The declared type of incoming working record of _STM_0 is defined as follows. Case:
    1. If the [&lt;binding variable definition block&gt;](#_bookmark1139) _BVDBLK_ was specified, then the declared type of the incoming working record of _STM_0 is the declared type of the outgoing working record of _BVDBLK_.
    2. Otherwise, the declared type of incoming working record of _STM_0 is the declared type of the incoming working record of _PB_.
6. The declared type of the incoming working table of _STM_0 is the declared type of the incoming working table of _PB_.
7. For _j_, 1 (one) ≤ _j_ ≤ _M_:
    1. The declared type of the incoming working record of _STMj_ is the declared type of the outgoing working record of _STMj_\-1.
    2. The declared type of the incoming working table of _STM__j_ is defined as follows. Case:

            1. If the [&lt;next statement&gt;](#_bookmark1149) that directly contains _STMj_ also directly contains a [<yield](#_bookmark2500) [clause>](#_bookmark2500) _YC_, then:
                1. The declared type of the incoming working table of _YC_ is _BTT_.
    3. [**&lt;procedure body&gt;**](#_bookmark1137)

        - - 1. The declared type of the incoming working table of _STMj_ is the declared type of _YC_.

            1. Otherwise, the declared type of the incoming working table of _STMj_ is _BTT_.

        1. Otherwise, the declared type of the incoming working table of _STMj_ is the material unit binding table type.
    4. The record type of the declared type of the incoming working table of _STMj_ and the declared type of the incoming working record of _STMj_ shall be field name-disjoint.
8. The declared type of _PB_ is the declared type of _STMM_.

# General Rules

1. If the [&lt;binding variable definition block&gt;](#_bookmark1139) _BVDBLK_ is specified, then:
    1. Let _CONTEXT_ be a new child execution context.
    2. For _j_, 1 (one) ≤ _j_ ≤ _N_, Case:
        1. If _BVDj_ is a [&lt;graph variable definition&gt;](#_bookmark1185), then the General Rules of [Subclause 10.1,](#_bookmark1184) [“](#_bookmark1184)[<gr](#_bookmark1185)[aph variable definition>”](#_bookmark1184) are applied in _CONTEXT_.
        2. If _BVDj_ is a [&lt;binding table variable definition&gt;](#_bookmark1198), then the General Rules of [Subclause 10.2,](#_bookmark1197) [“](#_bookmark1197)[<binding](#_bookmark1198) [table variable definition>”](#_bookmark1197) are applied in _CONTEXT_.
        3. Otherwise, _BVDj_ is a [&lt;value variable definition&gt;](#_bookmark1211) and the General Rules of [Subclause 10.3,](#_bookmark1210) [“](#_bookmark1210)[<v](#_bookmark1211)[alue variable definition>”](#_bookmark1210) are applied in _CONTEXT_.
    3. The current working record is set to the working record of _CONTEXT_.
2. The General Rules of _STM_0 are applied.

NOTE 174 — Not all statements set a result; instead they possibly modify the current execution context. A result is set by [&lt;primitive result statement&gt;](#_bookmark1690)s and by [&lt;simple data-modifying statement&gt;](#_bookmark1393)s to determine the execution outcome of a GQL-procedure or a top-level [&lt;statement&gt;](#_bookmark1145).

NOTE 175 — Not all statements set a result; instead they possibly modify the current execution context. A result is set by [&lt;primitive result statement&gt;](#_bookmark1690)s and by [&lt;simple data-modifying statement&gt;](#_bookmark1393)s to determine the execution outcome of a GQL-procedure or a top-level [&lt;statement&gt;](#_bookmark1145).

1. Without Feature GP16, “AT schema clause”, in conforming GQL language, a [&lt;procedure body&gt;](#_bookmark1137) shall not contain an [&lt;at schema clause&gt;](#_bookmark1910).
2. Without Feature GP17, “Binding variable definition block”, in conforming GQL language, a [<procedure](#_bookmark1137) [body>](#_bookmark1137) shall not contain a [&lt;binding variable definition block&gt;](#_bookmark1139).
3. Without Feature GP11, “Procedure-local graph variable definitions”, in conforming GQL language, a [&lt;binding variable definition&gt;](#_bookmark1140) shall not contain a [&lt;graph variable definition&gt;](#_bookmark1185).
4. Without Feature GP08, “Procedure-local binding table variable definitions”, in conforming GQL language, a [&lt;binding variable definition&gt;](#_bookmark1140) shall not contain a [&lt;binding table variable definition&gt;](#_bookmark1198).
5. Without Feature GP05, “Procedure-local value variable definitions”, in conforming GQL language, a [&lt;binding variable definition&gt;](#_bookmark1140) shall not contain a [&lt;value variable definition&gt;](#_bookmark1211).

[&lt;procedure body&gt;](#_bookmark1137) shall not contain a [&lt;next statement&gt;](#_bookmark1149).

# [&lt;graph variable definition&gt;](#_bookmark1185)

**Function**

Define graph variables.

# Format

&lt;graph variable definition&gt; ::=

\[ PROPERTY \] GRAPH [&lt;binding variable&gt;](#_bookmark4447) [&lt;opt typed graph initializer&gt;](#_bookmark1187)

&lt;opt typed graph initializer&gt; ::=

\[ \[ [&lt;typed&gt;](#_bookmark2881) \] [&lt;graph reference value type&gt;](#_bookmark2980) \] [&lt;graph initializer&gt;](#_bookmark1189)

&lt;graph initializer&gt; ::=

[&lt;equals operator&gt;](#_bookmark5026) [&lt;graph expression&gt;](#_bookmark1223)

# Syntax Rules

1. Let _GVD_ be the [&lt;graph variable definition&gt;](#_bookmark1185).
2. Let _GN_ be the name of the [&lt;binding variable&gt;](#_bookmark4447) simply contained in _GVD_.
3. Let _OTGI_ be the [&lt;opt typed graph initializer&gt;](#_bookmark1187) immediately contained in _GVD_.
4. Let _GI_ be the [&lt;graph initializer&gt;](#_bookmark1189) immediately contained in _OTGI_.
5. The declared type of _GI_ is the declared type of the [&lt;graph expression&gt;](#_bookmark1223) immediately contained in

_GI_.

1. Let _WRT_ be the declared type of the incoming working record of _GVD_.
2. _WRT_ shall not have a field type whose name is _GN_.
3. Let the graph reference value type _GT_ be defined as follows.
    1. Let _GIT_ be the declared type of _GI_.
    2. Case:
        1. If _GVD_ simply contains a [&lt;graph reference value type&gt;](#_bookmark2980) _OGT_ without an intervening instance of [&lt;graph initializer&gt;](#_bookmark1189), then:
            1. _GIT_ shall be assignable to the graph reference value type specified by _OGT_.
            2. _GT_ is the graph reference value type specified by _OGT_.
        2. Otherwise, _GT_ is _GIT_.
4. The declared type of the outgoing working record of _GVD_ is a record type comprising all the field types of _WRT_ and one additional field type with name _GN_ and value type _GT_.
    1. [**&lt;graph variable definition&gt;**](#_bookmark1185)

# General Rules

1. The result of _GI_ is the result of the [&lt;graph expression&gt;](#_bookmark1223) immediately contained in _GI_.
2. Let _ROGI_ be the result of _GI_.
3. A field with name _GN_ and value assigned from _ROGI_ is added to the current working record.

# Conformance Rules

1. Without Feature GP12, “Procedure-local graph variable definitions: graph variables based on simple expressions or references”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [&lt;graph variable definition&gt;](#_bookmark1185) that contains a [&lt;procedure body&gt;](#_bookmark1137).
2. Without Feature GP13, “Procedure-local graph variable definitions: graph variables based on sub- queries”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [&lt;graph variable definition&gt;](#_bookmark1185) that simply

contains a [&lt;graph expression&gt;](#_bookmark1223) that does not conform to [&lt;value specification&gt;](#_bookmark3529) or is a [<graph refer-](#_bookmark2600) [ence>](#_bookmark2600).

_OBTT_.

- - - 1. _BTT_ is the binding table reference value type specified by _OBTT_.

      1. Otherwise, _BTT_ is _BTIT_.

1. The declared type of the outgoing working record of _BTVD_ is a record type comprising all the field types of _WRT_ and one additional field type with name _BTN_ and value type _BTT_.

1. The result of _BTI_ is the result of the [&lt;binding table expression&gt;](#_bookmark1240) immediately contained in _BTI_.

# [&lt;create schema statement&gt;](#_bookmark1278) Function

Create a GQL-schema.

# Format

&lt;create schema statement&gt; ::=

CREATE SCHEMA \[ IF NOT EXISTS \] [&lt;catalog schema parent and name&gt;](#_bookmark2578)

# Syntax Rules

1. Let _CSPN_ be the [&lt;catalog schema parent and name&gt;](#_bookmark2578).
2. Let _ADP_ be the [&lt;absolute directory path&gt;](#_bookmark2582) immediately contained in _CSPN_. _ADP_ shall identify a GQL- directory.
3. Let _PARENT_ be the GQL-directory identified by _ADP_.
4. Let _SN_ be the [&lt;schema name&gt;](#_bookmark4425) immediately contained in _CSPN_.
5. If IF NOT EXISTS is not specified, then _SN_ shall not identify an existing GQL-schema descriptor in

_PARENT_.

# General Rules

1. If IF NOT EXISTS is specified and _SN_ identifies an existing GQL-schema descriptor in _PARENT_, then no further General Rules of this Subclause are applied.
2. Let _S_ be a new GQL-schema.
3. The associated GQL-schema descriptor _SD_ of _S_ is created that comprises:
    1. The session authorization identifier as the owner of _S_.
    2. An empty set as the set of named subobjects of _S_.
4. _SD_ is inserted into _PARENT_ with the name _SN_.

# Conformance Rules

1. Without Feature GC01, “Graph schema management”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [&lt;create schema statement&gt;](#_bookmark1278).
2. Without Feature GC02, “Graph schema management: IF \[ NOT \] EXISTS”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [&lt;create schema statement&gt;](#_bookmark1278) that includes IF NOT EXISTS.
    1. [**&lt;drop schema statement&gt;**](#_bookmark1285)

# [&lt;drop schema statement&gt;](#_bookmark1285) Function

Destroy a GQL-schema.

# Format

&lt;drop schema statement&gt; ::=

DROP SCHEMA \[ IF EXISTS \] [&lt;catalog schema parent and name&gt;](#_bookmark2578)

# Syntax Rules

1. Let _DSS_ be [&lt;drop schema statement&gt;](#_bookmark1285).
2. Let _CSPN_ be the [&lt;catalog schema parent and name&gt;](#_bookmark2578).
3. Let _ADP_ be the [&lt;absolute directory path&gt;](#_bookmark2582) immediately contained in _CSPN_. _ADP_ shall identify a GQL- directory.
4. Let _PARENT_ be the GQL-directory identified by _ADP_.
5. Let _SN_ be the [&lt;schema name&gt;](#_bookmark4425) immediately contained in _CSPN_.
6. If IF EXISTS is not specified, then _SN_ shall identify an existing GQL-schema descriptor in _PARENT_.
7. If _SN_ identifies an existing GQL-schema descriptor _SD_ in _PARENT_, then:
    1. If the current working schema of _DSS_ is defined, then _SD_ shall not be the descriptor of the current working schema of _DSS_.
    2. _SD_ shall not contain any catalog object descriptors.

# General Rules

1. If IF EXISTS is specified and _SN_ does not identify an existing GQL-schema descriptor in _PARENT_, then no further General Rules of this Subclause are applied.
2. _SD_ is removed from _PARENT_ under the name _SN_ and _SD_ is destroyed.

# Conformance Rules

1. Without Feature GC01, “Graph schema management”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [&lt;drop schema statement&gt;](#_bookmark1285).
2. Without Feature GC02, “Graph schema management: IF \[ NOT \] EXISTS”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [&lt;drop schema statement&gt;](#_bookmark1285) that includes IF EXISTS.
    1. [**&lt;create graph statement&gt;**](#_bookmark1292)

- 1. If _GT_ is not “omitted”, then the constraining graph type of _GD_ is _GT_.

Without Feature GG03, “Graph type inline specification”, in conforming GQL language, a [<create](#_bookmark1292) [graph statement>](#_bookmark1292) shall not contain an [&lt;of graph type&gt;](#_bookmark1297) that contains a [<nested graph type specific-](#_bookmark2657) [ation>](#_bookmark2657).
6. Without Feature GG04, “Graph type like a graph”, in conforming GQL language, a [<create graph](#_bookmark1292) [statement>](#_bookmark1292) shall not contain an [&lt;of graph type&gt;](#_bookmark1297) that contains a [&lt;graph type like graph&gt;](#_bookmark1300).

# [&lt;drop graph statement&gt;](#_bookmark1335) Function

Destroy a graph.

# Format

&lt;drop graph statement&gt; ::=

DROP \[ PROPERTY \] GRAPH \[ IF EXISTS \] [&lt;catalog graph parent and name&gt;](#_bookmark2604)

# Syntax Rules

1. Let _DGS_ be the [&lt;drop graph statement&gt;](#_bookmark1335) and let _CGPN_ be the [&lt;catalog graph parent and name&gt;](#_bookmark2604).
2. Let _COPR_ be the explicit or implicit [&lt;catalog object parent reference&gt;](#_bookmark2631) immediately contained in

_CGPN_. _COPR_ shall identify a GQL-schema.

1. Let _SCHEMA_ be the GQL-schema identified by _COPR_.
2. Let _GN_ be the [&lt;graph name&gt;](#_bookmark4426) immediately contained in _CGPN_.
3. If _DGS_ does not immediately contain IF EXISTS, then _CGPN_ shall identify an existing graph.

# General Rules

1. If _DGS_ immediately contains IF EXISTS and _CGPN_ does not identify an existing graph, then a comple- tion condition is raised: _warning — graph does not exist (01G03)_ and no further General Rules of

this Subclause are applied.

1. Let _G_ be the graph identified by _CGPN_ and let _GD_ be the graph descriptor of _G_.
2. Let _GT_ be the graph type of _G_.
3. _GD_ is removed from _SCHEMA_ under the name _GN_ and _GD_ is destroyed.
4. If the name of _GT_ is a system-generated name and _GT_ is not the graph type of any other graph in the GQL-catalog, then the graph type descriptor of _GT_ is destroyed.

NOTE 184 — See [Syntax Rule 23)](#_bookmark4958) of [Subclause 21.3, “](#_bookmark4737)[<t](#_bookmark4738)[oken>,](#_bookmark4737) [<separ](#_bookmark4906)[ator>, and](#_bookmark4737) [&lt;identifier&gt;](#_bookmark4744)[”](#_bookmark4737) for detailed provisions regarding the construction of system-generated regular identifiers.

# [&lt;delete statement&gt;](#_bookmark1525) Function

Delete graph elements.

&lt;delete statement&gt; ::=

\[ DETACH | NODETACH \] DELETE [&lt;delete item list&gt;](#_bookmark1527)

&lt;delete item list&gt; ::=

[&lt;delete item&gt;](#_bookmark1529) \[ { [&lt;comma&gt;](#_bookmark5022) [&lt;delete item&gt;](#_bookmark1529) }... \]

# Syntax Rules

1. Let _DS_ be the [&lt;delete statement&gt;](#_bookmark1525).
2. Let _DIL_ be the [&lt;delete item list&gt;](#_bookmark1527) immediately contained in _DS_.
3. The current working graph site of _DS_ shall not be “omitted”.
4. Let _CWGS_ be the current working graph site of _DS_.
5. The declared type for every [&lt;value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3470) simply contained in _DIL_ shall be a graph element reference value type.
6. If _DS_ does not specify DETACH or NODETACH, then NODETACH is implicit.
7. The declared type of the outgoing working table of _DS_ is the declared type of the incoming working table of _DS_.
8. The declared type of the outgoing working record of _DS_ is the declared type of the incoming working record of _DS_.
9. The declared type of _DS_ is the empty type.

# General Rules

1. Let _TABLE_ be the current working table.
2. Let _CG_ be the graph referenced by _CWGS_.
3. Let _NODES_ be an empty set. Let _EDGES_ be an empty set.
4. For each record _R_ of _TABLE_ in a new child execution context amended with _R_:
    1. For each [&lt;delete item&gt;](#_bookmark1529) _DI_ immediately contained in _DIL_:
        1. Let the value _V_ be the result of the [&lt;value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3470) immediately contained in _DI_.
        2. Case:
            1. If _V_ is a reference value to an edge _E_ and _V_ is not invalidated, then _E_ is added to

_EDGES_.

- 1. [**&lt;delete statement&gt;**](#_bookmark1525)
        - 1. If _V_ is a reference value to a node _N_ and _V_ is not invalidated, then:
                1. _N_ is added to _NODES_.
                2. If DETACH is specified, then all edges connected to _N_ are added to _EDGES_.
          2. Otherwise, _V_ is the null value.

1. For every node _N_ in _NODES_, if any edge connected to _N_ is not in _EDGES_, then an exception condition is raised: _dependent object error — edges still exist (G1001)_.
2. Let _CG1_ be a copy of _CG_ with all members of _EDGES_ and all members of _NODES_ deleted. If _CG_ has a graph type _GT_ and _CG1_ is not of graph type _GT_, then an exception condition is raised: _graph type violation (G2000)_.

NOTE 195 — This document does not currently specify a situation in which the above exception would be triggered. However, it is included as it is expected that implementation-defined extensions and/or future editions of this document will define such situations.

1. All members of _EDGES_ and all members of _NODES_ are deleted from _CG_.

NOTE 196 — The effect of this is that all graph elements referenced by the results of evaluating the

[&lt;delete statement&gt;](#_bookmark1525), for all records in the current working table, are deleted atomically. If any such graph element cannot be deleted, then no other graph element will be deleted.

1. The current execution outcome is set to a successful outcome with an omitted result.

1. Without Feature GD03, “DELETE statement: subquery support”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [&lt;delete item&gt;](#_bookmark1529) that contains a [&lt;procedure body&gt;](#_bookmark1137).
2. Without Feature GD04, “DELETE statement: simple expression support”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [&lt;delete item&gt;](#_bookmark1529) that simply contains a [&lt;value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3470) that is not a [<binding](#_bookmark3823) [variable reference>](#_bookmark3823).

# [&lt;composite query statement&gt;](#_bookmark1549)

**Function**

&lt;composite query statement&gt; ::=

[&lt;composite query expression&gt;](#_bookmark1551)

1. Let _CQS_ be the [&lt;composite query statement&gt;](#_bookmark1549) and let _CQE_ be the [&lt;composite query expression&gt;](#_bookmark1551) immediately contained in _CQS_.
2. The declared type of the outgoing working record of _CQS_ is the declared type of the incoming working record of _CQS_.
3. The declared type of the outgoing working table of _CQS_ is the declared type of _CQE_.

# [&lt;composite query expression&gt;](#_bookmark1551) Function

Specify binding table compositions.

# Format

&lt;composite query expression&gt; ::=

[&lt;composite query expression&gt;](#_bookmark1551) [&lt;query conjunction&gt;](#_bookmark1552) [&lt;composite query primary&gt;](#_bookmark1558)

| [&lt;composite query primary&gt;](#_bookmark1558)

&lt;query conjunction&gt; ::=

[&lt;set operator&gt;](#_bookmark1554)

| OTHERWISE

&lt;set operator&gt; ::=

UNION \[ [&lt;set quantifier&gt;](#_bookmark3745) \]

| EXCEPT \[ [&lt;set quantifier&gt;](#_bookmark3745) \]

| INTERSECT \[ [&lt;set quantifier&gt;](#_bookmark3745) \]

&lt;composite query primary&gt; ::=

[&lt;linear query statement&gt;](#_bookmark1584)

# Syntax Rules

1. If [&lt;set operator&gt;](#_bookmark1554) is specified and [&lt;set quantifier&gt;](#_bookmark3745) is not specified, then DISTINCT is implicit.
2. Let _CQE_ be the [&lt;composite query expression&gt;](#_bookmark1551).
3. If a [&lt;query conjunction&gt;](#_bookmark1552) _QC_ is immediately contained in _CQE_, then every [&lt;query conjunction&gt;](#_bookmark1552) directly contained in _CQE_ shall be _QC_.
4. If _CQE_ directly contains a [&lt;focused linear query statement&gt;](#_bookmark1585), then _CQE_ shall not directly contain an

[&lt;ambient linear query statement&gt;](#_bookmark1594).

NOTE 197 — As a consequence of this rule, focused statements and ambient statement are mutually exclusive within a [&lt;composite query expression&gt;](#_bookmark1551), so that the following is true as well: If _CQE_ directly contains an [&lt;ambient linear query statement&gt;](#_bookmark1594), then _CQE_ does not directly contain a [<focused linear query](#_bookmark1585) [statement>](#_bookmark1585).

1. If _CQE_ directly contains a [&lt;primitive result statement&gt;](#_bookmark1690) that is FINISH, then _CQE_ shall directly contain at most one [&lt;composite query primary&gt;](#_bookmark1558).
2. Let _CQP_ be the [&lt;composite query primary&gt;](#_bookmark1558) immediately contained in _CQE_.
3. Let _LQS_ be the [&lt;linear query statement&gt;](#_bookmark1584) immediately contained in _CQP_.
4. The declared type of the incoming working record of _LQS_ is the declared type of the incoming working record of _CQE_.
5. The declared type of the incoming working table of _LQS_ is the declared type of the incoming working table of _CQE_.
6. Case:
    1. If [&lt;query conjunction&gt;](#_bookmark1552) is specified, then:
        1. Let _ICQE_ be the [&lt;composite query expression&gt;](#_bookmark1551) immediately contained in _CQE_.
    2. [**&lt;composite query expression&gt;**](#_bookmark1551)
        1. The declared type of the incoming working record of _ICQE_ is the declared type of the incoming working record of _CQE_.
        2. The declared type of the incoming working table of _ICQE_ is the declared type of the incoming working table of _CQE_.
        3. Let _FCQE_ be the set of the columns of the declared type of the outgoing working table of _ICQE_ and let _FLQE_ be the set of the columns of the declared type of the outgoing working table of _CQP_.
        4. _FCQE_ and _FLQE_ shall be column name-equal and column-combinable.
        5. Let _COLS_ be the combined columns of _FCQE_ and _FLQE_.
        6. If [&lt;set operator&gt;](#_bookmark1554) is UNION DISTINCT, EXCEPT ALL, EXCEPT DISTINCT, INTERSECT ALL, or INTERSECT DISTINCT, then:
            1. There shall be no column _COL_ in _COLS_ such that all of the following is true:
                1. The value type of _COL_ is a dynamic union type _DUT_.
                2. There exists a pair of different component types _CT1_ and _CT2_ of _DUT_ such that _CT1_ and _CT2_ are not comparable value types.
            2. Each column in _COLS_ is an operand of a grouping operation. The Syntax Rules and Conformance Rules of [Subclause 22.15, “Grouping operations”](#_bookmark5273), apply.
        7. The declared type of _CQE_ is the material binding table whose set of columns is _COLS_.
    3. Otherwise, the declared type of _CQE_ is the declared type of the outgoing working table of _CQP_.

# General Rules

1. The result of _CQP_ is the result of _LQS_.
2. Case:
    1. If [&lt;query conjunction&gt;](#_bookmark1552) is specified, then:
        1. Let _ICQER_ be the binding table that is the result of _ICQE_.
        2. Let _CQPR_ be the binding table that is the result of _CQP_.
        3. Let _FCQER_ be a binding table determined as follows. Case:
            1. If UNION DISTINCT, EXCEPT ALL, EXCEPT DISTINCT, INTERSECT ALL, or

INTERSECT DISTINCT is specified, and there exists a record _R1_ of _ICQER_ and a record _R2_ of _CQPR_ such that _R1_ and _R2_ are not comparable values, then an exception condition is raised: _data exception — values not comparable (22G04)_.

- - - 1. If [&lt;set operator&gt;](#_bookmark1554) is specified, then _FCQER_ is new binding table whose columns are _COLS_ and whose records are determined by considering each record _R_ that is a duplicate of some record in _ICQER_ or of some record in _CQPR_ or both:
                1.  Let _M_ be the number of duplicates of _R_ in _ICQER_ and let _N_ be the number of duplicates of _R_ in _CQPR_, where _M_ ≥ 0 (zero) and _N_ ≥ 0 (zero).
                2.  If DISTINCT is specified or implicit, then Case:

    1. [**&lt;composite query expression&gt;**](#_bookmark1551)

If UNION is specified, then _FCQER_ contains exactly one duplicate of

_R_.

NOTE 198 — _R_ exists as a result of [General Rule 2)a)iii)2)](#_bookmark1566), guaranteeing that _FCQER_ always contains a duplicate of _R_.

If EXCEPT is specified, then Case:

If _M_ \> 0 (zero) and _N_ \= 0 (zero), then _FCQER_ contains exactly one duplicate of _R_.

Otherwise, _FCQER_ contains no duplicate of _R_.

If INTERSECT is specified, then Case:

If _M_ \> 0 (zero) and _N_ \> 0 (zero), then _FCQER_ contains exactly one duplicate of _R_.

Otherwise, _FCQER_ contains no duplicates of _R_.

- - - - 1. If ALL is specified, then Case:

If UNION is specified, then the number of duplicates of _R_ that _FCQER_

contains is (_M_ \+ _N_).

If EXCEPT is specified, then the number of duplicates of _R_ that _FCQER_

contains is the maximum of (_M_ − _N_) and 0 (zero).

If INTERSECT is specified, then the number of duplicates of _R_ that

_FCQER_ contains is the minimum of _M_ and _N_.

- - - 1. If OTHERWISE is specified, then Case:
                1.  If _ICQER_ contains at least one record, then _FCQER_ is _ICQER_.
                2.  Otherwise, _FCQER_ is _CQPR_.

      1. The result of _CQE_ is _FCQER_.

    1. Otherwise, the result of _CQE_ is the result of _CQP_.

# Conformance Rules

1. Without Feature GQ02, “Composite query: OTHERWISE”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [&lt;composite query expression&gt;](#_bookmark1551) that immediately contains a [&lt;query conjunction&gt;](#_bookmark1552) OTHERWISE.

[&lt;composite query expression&gt;](#_bookmark1551) that immediately contains a [&lt;query conjunction&gt;](#_bookmark1552) UNION.

1. Without Feature GQ04, “Composite query: EXCEPT DISTINCT”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [&lt;composite query expression&gt;](#_bookmark1551) that immediately contains a [&lt;query conjunction&gt;](#_bookmark1552) EXCEPT.
2. Without Feature GQ05, “Composite query: EXCEPT ALL”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [&lt;composite query expression&gt;](#_bookmark1551) that immediately contains a [&lt;query conjunction&gt;](#_bookmark1552) EXCEPT ALL.
    1. [**&lt;composite query expression&gt;**](#_bookmark1551)
3. Without Feature GQ06, “Composite query: INTERSECT DISTINCT”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [&lt;composite query expression&gt;](#_bookmark1551) that immediately contains a [&lt;query conjunction&gt;](#_bookmark1552)

INTERSECT.

NOTE 199 — This is a recursive definition. An [&lt;exists predicate&gt;](#_bookmark3394) contained in _S_ provides an example of a [&lt;graph pattern binding table&gt;](#_bookmark1933) that does not supply output bindings to _S_.

- 1. [**&lt;match statement&gt;**](#_bookmark1606)
  2. Let _OBVRL_ be a comma-separated list of [&lt;binding variable reference&gt;](#_bookmark3823)s corresponding to

[&lt;binding variable&gt;](#_bookmark4447)s whose names are column names of the declared type of any [<graph pattern](#_bookmark1933) [binding table>](#_bookmark1933) that supplies output bindings to _MS_ that are not included in _IFNS_.

- 1. Let _RETURN_ be defined as follows. Case:
        1. If _OBVRL_ is the empty list, then _RETURN_ is:

RETURN NO BINDINGS

- - 1. Otherwise, _OBVRL_ is non-empty and _RETURN_ is:

RETURN _OBVRL_

- 1. Let _OO_ be the [&lt;optional operand&gt;](#_bookmark1611) simply contained in _MS_. Case:
        1. If _OO_ immediately contains a [&lt;simple match statement&gt;](#_bookmark1607) _SMS_, then _MS_ is effectively replaced by:

_SMS RETURN_

}

- - 1. If _OO_ immediately contains a [&lt;match statement block&gt;](#_bookmark1614) _MSB_, then _MS_ is effectively replaced by:

_MSB RETURN_

}

[&lt;optional match statement&gt;](#_bookmark1609)s. _IBVRL_ and _OBVRL_ are computed separately for each trans- formation.

1. If _MS_ is a [&lt;simple match statement&gt;](#_bookmark1607), then:

type of the incoming working table at certain sites.

[&lt;limit clause&gt;](#_bookmark2561) immediately contained in _OPS_ is _DTIWR_.

# [&lt;select statement&gt;](#_bookmark1758) Function

Provide an SQL-style query over graph data, which produces a binding table result.

# Format

&lt;select statement&gt; ::=

SELECT \[ [&lt;set quantifier&gt;](#_bookmark3745) \] { [&lt;asterisk&gt;](#_bookmark5020) | [&lt;select item list&gt;](#_bookmark1763) } \[ [&lt;select statement body&gt;](#_bookmark1770)

\[ [&lt;where clause&gt;](#_bookmark2497) \]

\[ [&lt;group by clause&gt;](#_bookmark2513) \] \[ [&lt;having clause&gt;](#_bookmark1771) \] \[ [&lt;order by clause&gt;](#_bookmark2526) \]

\[ [&lt;offset clause&gt;](#_bookmark2566) \] \[ [&lt;limit clause&gt;](#_bookmark2561) \] \]

&lt;select item list&gt; ::=

[&lt;select item&gt;](#_bookmark1766) \[ { [&lt;comma&gt;](#_bookmark5022) [&lt;select item&gt;](#_bookmark1766) }... \]

&lt;select item&gt; ::=

[&lt;aggregating value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3488) \[ [&lt;select item alias&gt;](#_bookmark1768) \]

&lt;select item alias&gt; ::= AS [&lt;identifier&gt;](#_bookmark4744)

&lt;having clause&gt; ::=

HAVING [&lt;search condition&gt;](#_bookmark3337)

&lt;select statement body&gt; ::=

FROM { [&lt;select graph match list&gt;](#_bookmark1774) | [&lt;select query specification&gt;](#_bookmark1776) }

&lt;select graph match list&gt; ::=

[&lt;select graph match&gt;](#_bookmark1775) \[ { [&lt;comma&gt;](#_bookmark5022) [&lt;select graph match&gt;](#_bookmark1775) }... \]

&lt;select graph match&gt; ::=

[&lt;graph expression&gt;](#_bookmark1223) [&lt;match statement&gt;](#_bookmark1606)

&lt;select query specification&gt; ::=

[&lt;nested query specification&gt;](#_bookmark1123)

| [&lt;graph expression&gt;](#_bookmark1223) [&lt;nested query specification&gt;](#_bookmark1123)

# Procedure calling

# [&lt;call procedure statement&gt;](#_bookmark1875) and [&lt;procedure call&gt;](#_bookmark1877)

**Function**

Execute a procedure.

# Format

&lt;call procedure statement&gt; ::=

\[ OPTIONAL \] CALL [&lt;procedure call&gt;](#_bookmark1877)

&lt;procedure call&gt; ::=

[&lt;inline procedure call&gt;](#_bookmark1884)

| [&lt;named procedure call&gt;](#_bookmark1895)

# Syntax Rules

1. Let _CPS_ be the [&lt;call procedure statement&gt;](#_bookmark1875).
2. Let _PC_ be the [&lt;procedure call&gt;](#_bookmark1877) immediately contained in _CPS_.
3. Let the record type _IREDT_ be the declared type of the incoming working record of _CPS_.
4. Let _ITART_ be the record type of the declared type of the incoming working table of _CPS_.
5. Let _IREDTPC_ be _IREDT_ amended by _ITART_.
6. The declared type of the incoming working record of _PC_ is _IREDTPC_.
7. The declared type of the incoming working table of _PC_ is the material unit binding table type.
8. Let _OTARTPC_ be defined as follows. Case:
    1. If _PC_ is the [&lt;named procedure call&gt;](#_bookmark1895) _NPC_ and _NPC_ has a declared type, then _OTARTPC_ is the record type of the declared type of _NPC_.
    2. If _PC_ is the [&lt;inline procedure call&gt;](#_bookmark1884) _IPC_ and _IPC_ has a declared type, then _OTARTPC_ is the record type of the declared type of _IPC_.
    3. Otherwise, _OTARTPC_ is the material unit record type.
9. _ITART_ and _OTARTPC_ shall be field name-disjoint.
10. Let _OTART_ be _ITART_ amended with _OTARTPC_.
11. The declared type of the outgoing working record of _CPS_ is _IREDT_.
12. The declared type of the outgoing working table of _CPS_ is the binding table type whose record type is _OTART_.
13. The declared type of _CPS_ is the empty type.
    1. [**&lt;call procedure statement&gt;**](#_bookmark1875) **and** [**&lt;procedure call&gt;**](#_bookmark1877)

# General Rules

1. Let _TABLE_ be the current working table.
2. Let _NEW_TABLE_ be a new empty binding table whose columns are the field types of _OTART_.
3. For each record _R_ of _TABLE_ in a new child execution context amended with _R_:
    1. Case:
        1. If _PC_ is an [&lt;inline procedure call&gt;](#_bookmark1884), then the General Rules of [Subclause 15.2, “](#_bookmark1883)[<inline](#_bookmark1884) [pr](#_bookmark1884)[ocedure call>”](#_bookmark1883) are applied.
        2. Otherwise, _PC_ is a [&lt;named procedure call&gt;](#_bookmark1895) and the General Rules of [Subclause 15.3,](#_bookmark1894) [“](#_bookmark1894)[<named](#_bookmark1895) [procedure call>”](#_bookmark1894) are applied.
    2. Let _RESULT_ be a new binding table defined as follows. Case:
        1. If the current execution result is a binding table _RESULT_TABLE_, then _RESULT_ is _RES- ULT_TABLE_ and the columns of _RESULT_ are the field types of _OTARTPC_.
        2. Otherwise, the current execution result is omitted and _RESULT_ is a unit binding table.
    3. Let _OPTIONAL_RESULT_ be a new binding table defined as follows. Case:
        1. If _CPS_ immediately contains OPTIONAL and _RESULT_ is an empty binding table result, then _OPTIONAL_RESULT_ comprises a new record of type _OTARTPC_ in which every field value is the null value.
        2. Otherwise, _OPTIONAL_RESULT_ is _RESULT_.
    4. The Cartesian product of _R_ and _OPTIONAL_RESULT_ is appended to _NEW_TABLE_.
4. The current working table is set to _NEW_TABLE_.
5. The current execution outcome is set to a successful outcome with an omitted result.

# Conformance Rules

_None._

- 1. [**&lt;inline procedure call&gt;**](#_bookmark1884)

# [&lt;inline procedure call&gt;](#_bookmark1884) Function

Execute a procedure that is specified inline.

# Format

&lt;inline procedure call&gt; ::=

\[ [&lt;variable scope clause&gt;](#_bookmark1886) \] [&lt;nested procedure specification&gt;](#_bookmark1116)

&lt;variable scope clause&gt; ::=

[&lt;left paren&gt;](#_bookmark5032) \[ [&lt;binding variable reference list&gt;](#_bookmark1888) \] [&lt;right paren&gt;](#_bookmark5043)

&lt;binding variable reference list&gt; ::=

[&lt;binding variable reference&gt;](#_bookmark3823) \[ { [&lt;comma&gt;](#_bookmark5022) [&lt;binding variable reference&gt;](#_bookmark3823) }... \]

# Syntax Rules

1. Let _IPC_ be the [&lt;inline procedure call&gt;](#_bookmark1884).
2. Let _PROC_ be the [&lt;nested procedure specification&gt;](#_bookmark1116) immediately contained in _IPC_.
3. If [&lt;variable scope clause&gt;](#_bookmark1886) is not specified, then:
    1. Let _FNL_ be a comma-separated list of all the field type names of the declared type of the incoming working record of _IPC_.
    2. _IPC_ is effectively replaced by:

(_FNL_) _PROC_

1. Let _VSC_ be the implicit or explicit [&lt;variable scope clause&gt;](#_bookmark1886) immediately contained in _IPC_.
2. For every [&lt;binding variable reference&gt;](#_bookmark3823) _BVR_ simply contained in _VSC_:
    1. The declared type of the incoming working record of _BVR_ is the declared type of the incoming working record of _IPC_.
    2. The declared type of the incoming working table of _BVR_ is the declared type of the incoming working table of _IPC_.
3. Let _BVRLN_ be defined as follows:
    1. If _VSC_ immediately contains a [&lt;binding variable reference list&gt;](#_bookmark1888) _BVRL_, then:
        1. _BVRLN_ is the sequence of names of the binding variables referenced by the [<binding](#_bookmark3823) [variable reference>](#_bookmark3823)s immediately contained in _BVRL_.
        2. _BVRLN_ shall not contain two equal names at different positions.
    2. Otherwise, _BVRLN_ is the empty sequence.
4. The declared type of the incoming working record of _PROC_ is the declared type of the incoming working record of _IPC_ comprising the field types identified by _BVRLN_.
5. The declared type of the incoming working table of _PROC_ is the declared type of the incoming working table of _IPC_.
    1. [**&lt;inline procedure call&gt;**](#_bookmark1884)
6. The declared type of the outgoing working record of _IPC_ is the declared type of the outgoing working record of _PROC_.
7. The declared type of the outgoing working table of _IPC_ is the declared type of the outgoing working table of _PROC_.
8. The declared type of _IPC_ is the declared type of _PROC_.

# General Rules

1. Let _R_ be the current working record comprising the fields identified by _BVRLN_.
2. The current working record is set to _R_.
3. The General Rules of _PROC_ are applied.
4. The outcome of _IPC_ is the outcome of _PROC_.

# Conformance Rules

1. Without Feature GP01, “Inline procedure”, conforming GQL language shall not contain an [<inline](#_bookmark1884) [procedure call>](#_bookmark1884).
2. Without Feature GP02, “Inline procedure with implicit nested variable scope”, in conforming GQL language, an [&lt;inline procedure call&gt;](#_bookmark1884) shall contain a [&lt;variable scope clause&gt;](#_bookmark1886).
3. Without Feature GP03, “Inline procedure with explicit nested variable scope”, in conforming GQL language, an [&lt;inline procedure call&gt;](#_bookmark1884) shall not contain a [&lt;variable scope clause&gt;](#_bookmark1886).
    1. [**&lt;named procedure call&gt;**](#_bookmark1895)

# [&lt;named procedure call&gt;](#_bookmark1895) Function

Execute a named procedure.

# Format

&lt;named procedure call&gt; ::=

[&lt;procedure reference&gt;](#_bookmark2625) [&lt;left paren&gt;](#_bookmark5032) \[ [&lt;procedure argument list&gt;](#_bookmark1898) \] [&lt;right paren&gt;](#_bookmark5043) \[ [&lt;yield clause&gt;](#_bookmark2500) \]

&lt;procedure argument list&gt; ::=

[&lt;procedure argument&gt;](#_bookmark1900) \[ { [&lt;comma&gt;](#_bookmark5022) [&lt;procedure argument&gt;](#_bookmark1900) }... \]

&lt;procedure argument&gt; ::=

[&lt;value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3470)

# Syntax Rules

1. Let _NPC_ be the [&lt;named procedure call&gt;](#_bookmark1895) and let _PROC_ be the procedure identified by the [<procedure](#_bookmark2625) [reference>](#_bookmark2625) immediately contained in _NPC_.
2. Let _PROCDESC_ be the named procedure descriptor of _PROC_.
3. Let _PARAMS_ be the list of procedure parameters of _PROCDESC_, let _PARAMSMIN_ be the number of procedure parameters required by _PROCDESC_ and let _PARAMSMAX_ be the maximum number of procedure parameters allowed by _PROCDESC_.
4. Let _ARGEXPS_ be the sequence of all [&lt;value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3470)s that are simply contained in _NPC_ in the order of their occurrence in _NPC_ from left to right and let _NUMARGS_ be the number of such elements in _ARGEXPS_.
5. _NUMARGS_ shall be greater than or equal to _PARAMSMIN_.
6. _NUMARGS_ shall be less than or equal to _PARAMSMAX_.
7. For _i_, 1 (one) ≤ _i_ ≤ _NUMARGS_:
    1. Let _ARGEXPi_ be the _i_\-th element of _ARGEXPS_.
    2. Let _PTi_ be the declared type of the _i_\-th element of _PARAMS_.
    3. The Syntax Rules of [Subclause 22.10, “Store assignment”](#_bookmark5227), are applied with a transient site of type _PTi_ as [_TARGET_](#_bookmark5229) and _ARGEXPi_ as [_VALUE_](#_bookmark5229).
8. If _NPC_ immediately contains a [&lt;yield clause&gt;](#_bookmark2500), then the procedure result type of _PROCDESC_ shall be a binding table type.
9. Let the declared type of _NPC_ be defined as follows. Case:
    1. If _NPC_ immediately contains a [&lt;yield clause&gt;](#_bookmark2500) _YC_, then the declared type of _NPC_ is the declared type of _YC_.
    2. Otherwise, the declared type of _NPC_ is the procedure result type of _PROCDESC_.
    3. [**&lt;named procedure call&gt;**](#_bookmark1895)

# General Rules

1. For _i_, 1 (one) ≤ _i_ ≤ _PARAMSMAX_, let _ARGVALi_ be defined as follows. Case:
    1. If _i_ ≤ _NUMARGS_, then _ARGVALi_ is the result of _ARGEXPi_.
    2. Otherwise, _ARGVALi_ is the default value of the _i_\-th element of _PARAMS_.
2. For _i_, 1 (one) ≤ _i_ ≤ _PARAMSMAX_, let _R_ be a new record comprising fields _Fi_ defined as follows:
    1. Let _Ti_ be the declared type of the _i_\-th element of _PARAMS_.
    2. Let _TS_ be a transient site of type _Ti_. The General Rules of [Subclause 22.10, “Store assignment”](#_bookmark5227), are applied with _TS_ as [_TARGET_](#_bookmark5229) and _ARGVALi_ as [_VALUE_](#_bookmark5229). Let _TSVi_ be the value of _TS_.
    3. The name of _Fi_ is the procedure parameter name of the _i_\-th element of _PARAMS_ and the value of _Fi_ is _TSVi_.
3. The following steps are performed in a new child execution context with _R_ as its working record:
    1. Execute _PROC_.
    2. Let _RESULT_ be the result returned from the successful execution of _PROC_.
    3. The current execution outcome is set as follows. Case:
        1. If a [&lt;yield clause&gt;](#_bookmark2500) _YC_ is specified, then:
            1. The General Rules of _YC_ are applied; let _YIELD_ be the result returned from the application of these General Rules.
            2. The current execution outcome is set to a successful outcome with _YIELD_ as its result.
        2. Otherwise, set the current execution outcome to a successful outcome with _RESULT_ as its result.

# Conformance Rules

1. Without Feature GP04, “Named procedure calls”, conforming GQL Language shall not contain a

[&lt;named procedure call&gt;](#_bookmark1895).

1. Without Feature GP15, “Graphs as procedure arguments”, in conforming GQL language, the declared type of a [&lt;value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3470) immediately contained in a [&lt;procedure argument&gt;](#_bookmark1900) shall not be a

supertype of a graph reference value type.

1. Without Feature GP14, “Binding tables as procedure arguments”, in conforming GQL language, the declared type of a [&lt;value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3470) immediately contained in a [&lt;procedure argument&gt;](#_bookmark1900) shall not be a supertype of a binding table reference value type.

**Function**

Declare a working schema and its scope.

# Format

&lt;at schema clause&gt; ::= AT [&lt;schema reference&gt;](#_bookmark2574)

# Syntax Rules

1. Let _ASC_ be the [&lt;at schema clause&gt;](#_bookmark1910).
2. Let _ACSR_ be an [&lt;absolute catalog schema reference&gt;](#_bookmark2576) that identifies the GQL-schema identified by the [&lt;schema reference&gt;](#_bookmark2574) immediately contained in _ASC_.

NOTE 209 — If the [&lt;schema reference&gt;](#_bookmark2574) _SR_ that is immediately contained in _ASC_ is a [<relative catalog](#_bookmark2579) [schema reference>](#_bookmark2579) or a [&lt;reference parameter specification&gt;](#_bookmark2634), then the Syntax Rules of [Subclause 17.1,](#_bookmark2573) [“](#_bookmark2573)[<schema](#_bookmark2574) [reference> and](#_bookmark2573) [<catalog](#_bookmark2578) [schema parent and name>”](#_bookmark2573) are applied to determine the GQL-schema identified by _SR_.

1. Let _PB_ be the [&lt;procedure body&gt;](#_bookmark1137) immediately containing _ASC_.
2. The scope clause of _ASC_ is _PB_.
3. The scope of _ACSR_ comprises _PB_.
4. _ASC_ identifies _ACSR_ as a working schema reference.

# General Rules

_None._

# Conformance Rules

_None._

# [&lt;use graph clause&gt;](#_bookmark1917) Function

Declare a working graph and its scope.

# Format

&lt;use graph clause&gt; ::= USE [&lt;graph expression&gt;](#_bookmark1223)

# Syntax Rules

1. Let _UGC_ be the [&lt;use graph clause&gt;](#_bookmark1917).
2. Let _GE_ be the [&lt;graph expression&gt;](#_bookmark1223) simply contained in _UGC_.
3. The declared type of the incoming working record of _GE_ is the declared type of the incoming working record of _UGC_.
4. The declared type of the incoming working table of _GE_ is the material unit binding table type.
5. Let _PART_ be the instance of the BNF non-terminal that immediately contains _UGC_.
6. The scope clause of _UGC_ is defined as follows. Case:
    1. If _PART_ is simply contained in a [&lt;focused linear query statement&gt;](#_bookmark1585) _FLQS_, then the scope clause of _UGC_ is _FLQS_.
    2. Otherwise, _PART_ is simply contained in a [&lt;focused linear data-modifying statement&gt;](#_bookmark1383) _FLDMS_, and the scope clause of _UGC_ is _FLDMS_.
7. The scope of _GE_ is defined as follows. Case:
    1. If _PART_ is a [&lt;focused linear query statement part&gt;](#_bookmark1587), then the scope of _GE_ comprises the [<simple](#_bookmark1595) [linear query statement>](#_bookmark1595) immediately contained in _PART_.
    2. If _PART_ is a [&lt;focused linear query and primitive result statement part&gt;](#_bookmark1589), then the scope of _GE_ comprises the [&lt;simple linear query statement&gt;](#_bookmark1595) and the [&lt;primitive result statement&gt;](#_bookmark1690) imme- diately contained in _PART_.
    3. If _PART_ is a [&lt;focused primitive result statement&gt;](#_bookmark1591), then the scope of _GE_ comprises the [<prim-](#_bookmark1690) [itive result statement>](#_bookmark1690) immediately contained in _PART_.
    4. If _PART_ is a [&lt;focused nested query specification&gt;](#_bookmark1592), then the scope of _GE_ comprises the [<nested](#_bookmark1123) [query specification>](#_bookmark1123) immediately contained in _PART_.
    5. If _PART_ is a [&lt;focused linear data-modifying statement body&gt;](#_bookmark1384), then the scope of _GE_ comprises the [&lt;simple linear query statement&gt;](#_bookmark1595), the [&lt;simple data-modifying statement&gt;](#_bookmark1393), the [<simple](#_bookmark1391) [linear data-accessing statement>](#_bookmark1391), and the [&lt;primitive result statement&gt;](#_bookmark1690) immediately contained in _PART_.
    6. [**&lt;use graph clause&gt;**](#_bookmark1917)
    7. Otherwise, _PART_ is a [&lt;focused nested data-modifying procedure specification&gt;](#_bookmark1387) and the scope of _GE_ comprises the [&lt;nested data-modifying procedure specification&gt;](#_bookmark1121) immediately contained in _PART_.
8. _UGC_ identifies _GE_ as a working graph site.

# General Rules

1. The working graph site that is _GE_ is set to the result of evaluating _GE_ in a new child execution context.

# Conformance Rules

1. Without Feature GQ01, “USE graph clause”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [<use graph](#_bookmark1917) [clause>](#_bookmark1917).

# Format

[&lt;graph pattern&gt;](#_bookmark1977) \[ [&lt;graph pattern yield clause&gt;](#_bookmark1934) \]

YIELD [&lt;graph pattern yield item list&gt;](#_bookmark1936)

&lt;graph pattern yield item list&gt; ::=

[&lt;graph pattern yield item&gt;](#_bookmark1938) \[ { [&lt;comma&gt;](#_bookmark5022) [&lt;graph pattern yield item&gt;](#_bookmark1938) }... \]

| NO BINDINGS

[&lt;element variable reference&gt;](#_bookmark2381)

1. Let _GPBT_ be the [&lt;graph pattern binding table&gt;](#_bookmark1933) and let _GP_ be the [&lt;graph pattern&gt;](#_bookmark1977) simply contained in _GPBT_.
2. Every variable in the scope of _GP_ is also in the scope of the [&lt;graph pattern yield clause&gt;](#_bookmark1934) simply contained in _GPBT_.
3. Let _EVSET_ be the set of names of element variable declared by _GP_, let _PVSET_ be the set of names of path variables declared by _GP_, and let _GPVARS_ be a permutation of _EVSET_ ∪ _PVSET_ in the order of their first occurrence as an [&lt;element variable declaration&gt;](#_bookmark2193) or a [&lt;path variable declaration&gt;](#_bookmark1995), respectively, that is simply contained in _GP_. 4. Each graph pattern variable name in _GPVARS_ shall identify exactly one graph pattern variable in

_GP_ at the same depth of graph pattern matching.

1. Let _GLOBALS_ be _GPVARS_ restricted to the names of graph pattern variables in the scope of _GP_.
2. Let _IREDT_ be the declared type of the incoming working record of _GPBT_.
3. _IREDT_ shall not contain a field whose name is in _SPVSET_.
4. Let _ITART_ be the record type of the declared type of the incoming working table of _GPBT_.
5. _ITART_ shall not contain a field whose name is in _SPVSET_.
6. Let _RECORD_OVERLAP_ be _GLOBALS_ restricted to the names of fields of _IREDT_, let _TABLE_OVERLAP_ be _GLOBALS_ restricted to the names of fields of _ITART_, and let _OVERLAP_ be the concatenation of _RECORD_OVERLAP_ with _TABLE_OVERLAP_.
7. The sequence of variable names _XGPYCVARS_ is defined as follows. Case:
    1. [**&lt;graph pattern binding table&gt;**](#_bookmark1933)
    2. If an explicit [&lt;graph pattern yield clause&gt;](#_bookmark1934) _XGPYC_ is specified, then _XGPYCVARS_ is the sequence of names of variables identified by instances of [&lt;binding variable reference&gt;](#_bookmark3823)s simply contained in _XGPYC_.
    3. Otherwise, _XGPYCVARS_ is the empty sequence.
8. Case:
    1. If the length of _XGPYCVARS_ is at least 1 (one), then:
        1. _XGPYCVARS_ shall not contain two equal names at different positions.
        2. Every name in _XGPYCVARS_ shall be contained in _GLOBALS_.
        3. Let _OGPYCVARS_ be _OVERLAP_ without the names contained in _XGPYCVARS_.
        4. Let _GPYIL_ be the comma-separated list of the elements of the concatenation of

_OGPYCVARS_ with _XGPYCVARS_.

- - 1. _XGPYC_ is equivalent to:

YIELD _GPYIL_

- 1. Otherwise, _XGPYCVARS_ is the empty sequence. Case:

# [&lt;graph pattern&gt;](#_bookmark1977)

**Function**

Specify a pattern to be matched in a graph.

# Subclause Signature

“[&lt;graph pattern&gt;](#_bookmark1977)” \[General Rules\] ( Parameter: “PROPERTY GRAPH”, Parameter: “GRAPH PATTERN”, Parameter: “PATH PATTERN LIST”,

Parameter: “MACHINERY”

) Returns: “SET OF REDUCED MATCHES”

PROPERTY GRAPH — a property graph GRAPH PATTERN — a [&lt;graph pattern&gt;](#_bookmark1977). PATH PATTERN LIST — a [&lt;path pattern list&gt;](#_bookmark1990).

MACHINERY — the machinery for graph pattern matching.

SET OF REDUCED MATCHES — the resulting set of reduced matches.

# Format

&lt;graph pattern&gt; ::=

\[ [&lt;match mode&gt;](#_bookmark1980) \] [&lt;path pattern list&gt;](#_bookmark1990) \[ [&lt;keep clause&gt;](#_bookmark1997) \]

\[ [&lt;graph pattern where clause&gt;](#_bookmark1999) \]

&lt;match mode&gt; ::=

[&lt;repeatable elements match mode&gt;](#_bookmark1981)

| [&lt;different edges match mode&gt;](#_bookmark1983)

&lt;repeatable elements match mode&gt; ::= REPEATABLE [&lt;element bindings or elements&gt;](#_bookmark1985)

&lt;different edges match mode&gt; ::= DIFFERENT [&lt;edge bindings or edges&gt;](#_bookmark1987)

&lt;element bindings or elements&gt; ::= ELEMENT \[ BINDINGS \]

| ELEMENTS

&lt;edge bindings or edges&gt; ::=

[&lt;edge synonym&gt;](#_bookmark4920) \[ BINDINGS \]

| [&lt;edges synonym&gt;](#_bookmark4922)

&lt;path pattern list&gt; ::=

[&lt;path pattern&gt;](#_bookmark1993) \[ { [&lt;comma&gt;](#_bookmark5022) [&lt;path pattern&gt;](#_bookmark1993) }... \]

&lt;path pattern&gt; ::=

\[ [&lt;path variable declaration&gt;](#_bookmark1995) \] \[ [&lt;path pattern prefix&gt;](#_bookmark2098) \] [&lt;path pattern expression&gt;](#_bookmark2171)

&lt;path variable declaration&gt; ::=

[&lt;path variable&gt;](#_bookmark4444) [&lt;equals operator&gt;](#_bookmark5026)

- 1. [**&lt;graph pattern&gt;**](#_bookmark1977)

&lt;keep clause&gt; ::=

KEEP [&lt;path pattern prefix&gt;](#_bookmark2098)

&lt;graph pattern where clause&gt; ::= WHERE [&lt;search condition&gt;](#_bookmark3337)

For every binding _BPPPE_ of _PPPE_ contained in _PBj_, all of the following are true:

- - 1. For every [&lt;element variable&gt;](#_bookmark4443) _EV_ that is exposed as an unconditional singleton by _PPPE_, _EV_ is bound to a unique graph element by the element variable bindings contained in _BPPPE_.

NOTE 229 — Anonymous symbols are not [&lt;element variable&gt;](#_bookmark4443)s; there is no requirement that two anonymous symbols bind to the same graph element.

- - 1. If _PPPE_ contains a [&lt;parenthesized path pattern where clause&gt;](#_bookmark2238) _PPPWC_, then _True_ is the

[_VALUE_](#_bookmark5199) returned as _V1_ when the General Rules of [Subclause 22.6, “Application of](#_bookmark5194)

[bindings to evaluate an expression”](#_bookmark5194), with _GPT_ as [_GRAPH PATTERN_](#_bookmark5197), the [<search condi-](#_bookmark3337) [tion>](#_bookmark3337) simply contained in _PPPWC_ as [_EXPRESSION_](#_bookmark5197), _MACH_ as [_MACHINERY_](#_bookmark5197), _M_ as [_MULTI-_](#_bookmark5198) [_PATH BINDING_](#_bookmark5198), and a reference to _BPPPE_ as [_REFERENCE TO LOCAL CONTEXT_](#_bookmark5198).

- 1. If _GPT_ contains a [&lt;graph pattern where clause&gt;](#_bookmark1999) _GPWC_, then _True_ is the [_VALUE_](#_bookmark5199) returned as _V2_ when the General Rules of [Subclause 22.6, “Application of bindings to evaluate an expression”](#_bookmark5194), with _GPT_ as [_GRAPH PATTERN_](#_bookmark5197), _GPWC_ as [_EXPRESSION_](#_bookmark5197), _MACH_ as [_MACHINERY_](#_bookmark5197), _M_ as [_MULTI-PATH_](#_bookmark5198)

[_BINDING_](#_bookmark5198), and a reference to _M_ as [_REFERENCE TO LOCAL CONTEXT_](#_bookmark5198).

1. A _reduced match RM_ \= ( _RPB_1, ..., _RPBNP_ ) is obtained from a match _M_ \= ( _PB_1, ..., _PBNP_ ) as _RM_ \=

_REDUCE_(_M_).

NOTE 230 — Set-theoretic deduplication will occur here. That is, two or more matches can reduce to the same reduced match; this scenario is regarded as contributing only a single reduced match to the result set.

1. Let _SRM_ be the set of reduced matches.
2. Evaluation of the General Rules is terminated and control is returned to the invoking Subclause, which receives _SRM_ as _SET OF REDUCED MATCHES_.

# Conformance Rules

1. Without Feature G002, “Different-edges match mode”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [&lt;different edges match mode&gt;](#_bookmark1983).
2. Without Feature G003, “Explicit REPEATABLE ELEMENTS keyword”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [&lt;match mode&gt;](#_bookmark1980) that specifies REPEATABLE ELEMENTS or REPEATABLE ELEMENT BINDINGS.
3. Without Feature G004, “Path variables”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [&lt;path pattern&gt;](#_bookmark1993) that simply contains a [&lt;path variable declaration&gt;](#_bookmark1995).
4. Without Feature G005, “Path search prefix in a path pattern”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [&lt;path pattern&gt;](#_bookmark1993) that simply contains a [&lt;path pattern prefix&gt;](#_bookmark2098) that is a [&lt;path search prefix&gt;](#_bookmark2105).
5. Without Feature G006, “Graph pattern KEEP clause: path mode prefix”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [&lt;keep clause&gt;](#_bookmark1997) that simply contains a [&lt;path mode prefix&gt;](#_bookmark2099).
6. Without Feature G007, “Graph pattern KEEP clause: path search prefix”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [&lt;keep clause&gt;](#_bookmark1997) that simply contains a [&lt;path search prefix&gt;](#_bookmark2105).

# Syntax Rules

1. Let _IGP_ be the [&lt;insert graph pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2064).
2. For every [&lt;insert element pattern filler&gt;](#_bookmark2077) _IEPF_ simply contained in _IGP_ that does not immediately contain an [&lt;element variable declaration&gt;](#_bookmark2193):
    1. Let _IDN_ be the name of a new system-generated regular identifier.
    2. _IEPF_ is effectively replaced by:

_IDN IEPF_

1. The system-generated variable names of _IGP_ are the names of all [&lt;element variable declaration&gt;](#_bookmark2193)s that are system-generated regular identifiers immediately contained in an [<insert element pattern](#_bookmark2077) [filler>](#_bookmark2077) simply contained in _IGP_.
2. Let _IS_ be the [&lt;insert statement&gt;](#_bookmark1411) that immediately contains _IGP_.
    1. [**&lt;insert graph pattern&gt;**](#_bookmark2064)
3. An [&lt;element variable&gt;](#_bookmark4443) _EV_ contained in an [&lt;element variable declaration&gt;](#_bookmark2193) _EVD_ is said to be declared by _EVD_, and by the [&lt;insert node pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2068) or [&lt;insert edge pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2070) _EP_ that simply contains _EVD_.

The [&lt;element variable&gt;](#_bookmark4443) specifies the name of an element variable, which is also declared by _EVD_

and _EP_.

1. For every [&lt;value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3470) _VE_ immediately contained in a [&lt;property key value pair&gt;](#_bookmark2207) immediately contained in an [&lt;element property specification&gt;](#_bookmark2203) simply contained in _IGP_:
    1. The declared type of the incoming working record of _VE_ is the declared type of the incoming working record of _IS_ amended with the record type of the declared type of the incoming working table of _IS_.
    2. The declared type of the incoming working table of _VE_ is the material unit binding table type.
    3. The declared type of _VE_ shall be a supported property value type.
2. An _insert element pattern_ is either an [&lt;insert node pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2068) or an [&lt;insert edge pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2070) that is simply contained in _IGP_.
3. A _bound insert element pattern_ is an insert element pattern _IEP_ that declares an [&lt;element variable&gt;](#_bookmark4443) _EV_ whose name is either the name of a column _COL_ of the declared type of the incoming working table of _IS_ or is the name of a field type _FT_ of the declared type of the incoming working record of _IS_. The declared type of _IEP_ is the column type of _COL_ or the value type of _FT_.
4. No [&lt;property key value pair list&gt;](#_bookmark2205) simply contained in a bound insert element pattern shall simply contain two equivalent [&lt;property name&gt;](#_bookmark4436)s that are each immediately contained in a different

[&lt;property key value pair&gt;](#_bookmark2207).

1. For every [&lt;element variable&gt;](#_bookmark4443) _EV_ simply contained in _IGP_:
    1. For every bound insert element pattern _EP_ that declares _EV_:
        1. _EP_ shall be an [&lt;insert node pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2068).
        2. The declared type of _EP_ shall be a node reference value type.
        3. _EP_ shall not simply contain a [&lt;label and property set specification&gt;](#_bookmark2079).
    2. The _defining insert element pattern_ of _EV_ is the first insert element pattern that declares _EV_. Every insert element pattern that declares _EV_ and is not the defining insert element pattern of _EV_ shall not simply contain a [&lt;label and property set specification&gt;](#_bookmark2079).
2. If an [&lt;insert edge pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2070) _EP1_ declares an [&lt;element variable&gt;](#_bookmark4443) _EV1_, then there shall not be an

[&lt;insert node pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2068) or [&lt;insert edge pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2070) _EP2_ that declares an [&lt;element variable&gt;](#_bookmark4443) _EV2_ equi- valent to _EV1_.

NOTE 231 — This rule has two consequences.

- If an [&lt;insert node pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2068) declares an [&lt;element variable&gt;](#_bookmark4443) _EV_, then there is not an [<insert edge](#_bookmark2070) [pattern>](#_bookmark2070) that declares an [&lt;element variable&gt;](#_bookmark4443) with the same name as _EV_.
- Every [&lt;insert edge pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2070) is the defining insert element pattern of the element variable it declares.

# General Rules

_None._

# Syntax Rules

1. If a [&lt;parenthesized path pattern expression&gt;](#_bookmark2231) does not specify a [&lt;path mode prefix&gt;](#_bookmark2099), then WALK PATHS is implicit.
2. If a [&lt;path pattern prefix&gt;](#_bookmark2098) _PPP_ does not specify [&lt;all path search&gt;](#_bookmark2106), then:
    1. Case:
        1. If _PPP_ does not simply contain a [&lt;path mode&gt;](#_bookmark2100), then let _PM_ be WALK.
        2. Otherwise, let _PM_ be the [&lt;path mode&gt;](#_bookmark2100) simply contained in _PPP_.
    2. Case:
        1. If _PPP_ does not simply contain a [&lt;number of paths&gt;](#_bookmark2111) or [&lt;number of groups&gt;](#_bookmark2121), then let

_N_ be an [&lt;unsigned integer&gt;](#_bookmark4545) whose value is 1 (one).

- - 1. Otherwise, let _N_ be the [&lt;number of paths&gt;](#_bookmark2111) or [&lt;number of groups&gt;](#_bookmark2121) simply contained in _PPP_. The declared type of _N_ shall be exact numeric with scale 0 (zero). If _N_ is a [<lit-](#_bookmark4475) [eral>](#_bookmark4475), then the value of _N_ shall be positive.

    1. Case:
        1. If _PPP_ is an [&lt;any path search&gt;](#_bookmark2110), then _PPP_ is equivalent to:

ANY _N PM_ PATHS

- - 1. If _PPP_ is a [&lt;shortest path search&gt;](#_bookmark2113), then Case:
            1.  If _PPP_ is [&lt;all shortest path search&gt;](#_bookmark2115), then _PPP_ is equivalent to:

SHORTEST 1 _PM_ GROUP

- - - 1. If _PPP_ is [&lt;any shortest path search&gt;](#_bookmark2117), then _PPP_ is equivalent to:

SHORTEST 1 _PM_ PATH

- - - 1. If _PPP_ is [&lt;counted shortest path search&gt;](#_bookmark2118), then _PPP_ is equivalent to:

SHORTEST _N PM_ PATHS

- - - 1. If _PPP_ is [&lt;counted shortest group search&gt;](#_bookmark2119), then _PPP_ is equivalent to:

SHORTEST _N PM_ GROUPS

1. A [&lt;path pattern prefix&gt;](#_bookmark2098) that specifies a [&lt;path mode&gt;](#_bookmark2100) other than WALK is _restrictive_. A [<parenthesized](#_bookmark2231) [path pattern expression>](#_bookmark2231) that immediately contains a restrictive [&lt;path mode prefix&gt;](#_bookmark2099) is _restrictive_.
2. A [&lt;path search prefix&gt;](#_bookmark2105) other than [&lt;all path search&gt;](#_bookmark2106) is _selective_. A [&lt;path pattern&gt;](#_bookmark1993) that simply contains a selective [&lt;path search prefix&gt;](#_bookmark2105) is _selective_.
3. Let _PPPE_ be a selective [&lt;path pattern&gt;](#_bookmark1993).
    1. An element variable exposed by _PPPE_ is an _interior variable_ of _PPPE_.
    2. A node variable _LVV_ is the _left boundary variable_ of _PPPE_ if all of the following conditions are true:
        1. _PPPE_ exposes _LVV_ as an unconditional singleton variable.
    3. [**&lt;path pattern prefix&gt;**](#_bookmark2098)
        1. _LVV_ is declared in the first explicit or implicit [&lt;node pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2188) _LVP_ contained in _PPPE_.
        2. _LVP_ is not contained in a [&lt;path pattern union&gt;](#_bookmark2174) or [&lt;path multiset alternation&gt;](#_bookmark2172) that is contained in _PPPE_.
    4. A node variable _RVV_ is the _right boundary variable_ of _PPPE_ if all of the following conditions are true:
        1. _PPPE_ exposes _RVV_ as an unconditional singleton variable.
        2. _RVV_ is declared in the last explicit or implicit [&lt;node pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2188) _RVP_ contained in _PPPE_.
        3. _RVP_ is not contained in a [&lt;path pattern union&gt;](#_bookmark2174) or [&lt;path multiset alternation&gt;](#_bookmark2172) that is contained in _PPPE_.
    5. An element variable that is exposed by _PPPE_ that is neither a left boundary variable of _PPPE_

nor a right boundary variable of _PPPE_ is a _strict interior variable_ of _PPPE_.

1. An element variable that is not declared in a selective [&lt;path pattern&gt;](#_bookmark1993) is an _exterior variable_.
2. A strict interior variable of one selective [&lt;path pattern&gt;](#_bookmark1993) shall not be equivalent to an exterior variable, or to an interior variable of another selective [&lt;path pattern&gt;](#_bookmark1993).

NOTE 232 — This does not prohibit implicit joins of boundary variables of selective [&lt;path pattern&gt;](#_bookmark1993)s with exterior variables or boundary variables of other selective [&lt;path pattern&gt;](#_bookmark1993)s.

1. A selective [&lt;path pattern&gt;](#_bookmark1993) _SPP_ shall not contain a reference to a graph pattern variable that is not declared by _SPP_.

NOTE 233 — This rule, and the prohibition of implicit joins to exterior variables and interior variables of other selective [&lt;path pattern&gt;](#_bookmark1993)s, insure that each selective [&lt;path pattern&gt;](#_bookmark1993) can be evaluated in isolation from any other [&lt;path pattern&gt;](#_bookmark1993).

_None._

# Syntax Rules

1. Let _GP_ be the outermost [&lt;graph pattern&gt;](#_bookmark1977) that contains the [&lt;path pattern expression&gt;](#_bookmark2171).
2. Let _RIGHTMINUS_ be the following collection of [&lt;token&gt;](#_bookmark4738)s: [&lt;right bracket minus&gt;](#_bookmark4895), [&lt;left arrow&gt;](#_bookmark4881), [<slash](#_bookmark4898) [minus>](#_bookmark4898), and [&lt;minus sign&gt;](#_bookmark5034).

NOTE 236 — These are the tokens (“\]-”, “<-”, “/-”, and “-”) that expose a minus sign on the right.

1. Let _LEFTMINUS_ be the following collection of [&lt;token&gt;](#_bookmark4738)s: [&lt;minus left bracket&gt;](#_bookmark4891), [&lt;right arrow&gt;](#_bookmark4894), [<minus](#_bookmark4892) [slash>](#_bookmark4892), and [&lt;minus sign&gt;](#_bookmark5034).

NOTE 237 — These are the tokens (“-\[”, “->”, “-/”, and “-”) that expose a minus sign on the left. [<minus](#_bookmark5034) [sign>](#_bookmark5034) itself is in both _RIGHTMINUS_ and _LEFTMINUS_.

1. A [&lt;path pattern expression&gt;](#_bookmark2171) shall not juxtapose a [&lt;token&gt;](#_bookmark4738) from _RIGHTMINUS_ followed by a [&lt;token&gt;](#_bookmark4738) from _LEFTMINUS_ without a [&lt;separator&gt;](#_bookmark4906) between them.

NOTE 238 — Otherwise, the concatenation of the two tokens would include the sequence of two [<minus](#_bookmark5034) [sign>](#_bookmark5034)s, which is a [&lt;simple comment introducer&gt;](#_bookmark4912).

1. A [&lt;path pattern expression&gt;](#_bookmark2171) that contains at the same depth of graph pattern matching a variable quantifier, a [&lt;questioned path primary&gt;](#_bookmark2181), a [&lt;path multiset alternation&gt;](#_bookmark2172), or a [&lt;path pattern union&gt;](#_bookmark2174) is a _possibly variable length path pattern_.
2. A [&lt;path pattern expression&gt;](#_bookmark2171) that is not a possibly variable length path pattern is a _fixed length path_ _pattern_.
3. The _minimum path length_ of certain BNF non-terminal instances defined in this Subclause is defined recursively as follows:
    1. The minimum path length of a [&lt;node pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2188) is 0 (zero).
    2. The minimum path length of an [&lt;edge pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2209) is 1 (one).
    3. The minimum path length of a [&lt;path concatenation&gt;](#_bookmark2177) is the sum of the minimum path lengths of its operands.
    4. The minimum path length of a [&lt;path pattern union&gt;](#_bookmark2174) or [&lt;path multiset alternation&gt;](#_bookmark2172) is the minimum of the minimum path length of its operands.
    5. The minimum path length of a [&lt;quantified path primary&gt;](#_bookmark2179) is the product of the minimum path length of the simply contained [&lt;path primary&gt;](#_bookmark2183) and the value of the [&lt;lower bound&gt;](#_bookmark2392).
    6. The minimum path length of a [&lt;questioned path primary&gt;](#_bookmark2181) is 0 (zero).
    7. [**&lt;path pattern expression&gt;**](#_bookmark2171)
    8. The minimum path length of a [&lt;parenthesized path pattern expression&gt;](#_bookmark2231) is the minimum path length of the simply contained [&lt;path pattern expression&gt;](#_bookmark2171).
    9. If _BNT1_ and _BNT2_ are two BNF non-terminal instances such that _BNT1_ ::= _BNT2_ and the minimum path length of _BNT2_ is defined, then the minimum path length of _BNT1_ is also defined and is the same as the minimum path length of _BNT2_.
4. The [&lt;path primary&gt;](#_bookmark2183) immediately contained in a [&lt;quantified path primary&gt;](#_bookmark2179) or [<questioned path](#_bookmark2181) [primary>](#_bookmark2181) shall have minimum path length that is greater than 0 (zero).
5. The [&lt;path primary&gt;](#_bookmark2183) simply contained in a [&lt;quantified path primary&gt;](#_bookmark2179) shall not contain a [<quantified](#_bookmark2179) [path primary>](#_bookmark2179) at the same depth of graph pattern matching.
6. Let _PMA_ be a [&lt;path multiset alternation&gt;](#_bookmark2172).
    1. A [&lt;path term&gt;](#_bookmark2176) simply contained in _PMA_ is a _multiset alternation operand_ of _PMA_.
    2. Let _NOPMA_ be the number of multiset alternation operands of _PMA_. Let _OPMA_1, ..., _OPMANOPMA_

be an enumeration of the operands of _PMA_.

- 1. Any [&lt;subpath variable&gt;](#_bookmark4445)s declared by [&lt;subpath variable declaration&gt;](#_bookmark2236)s simply contained in the multiset alternation operands of _PMA_ shall be mutually distinct.
  2. Let _SOPMA_1, ..., _SOPMANOPMA_ be new system-generated regular identifiers.
  3. For _i_, 1 (one) ≤ _i_ ≤ _NOPMA_, Case:
        1. If _OPMAi_ is a [&lt;parenthesized path pattern expression&gt;](#_bookmark2231) that simply contains a [<subpath](#_bookmark2236) [variable declaration>](#_bookmark2236), then let _OPMAXi_ be _OPMAi_.
        2. Otherwise, let _OPMAXi_ be the [&lt;parenthesized path pattern expression&gt;](#_bookmark2231)

(_SOPMAi_ \= _OPMAi_)

- 1. _PMA_ is equivalent to:

_OPMAX_1 | ... | _OPMAXNOPMA_

1. A [&lt;path term&gt;](#_bookmark2176) _PPUOP_ simply contained in a [&lt;path pattern union&gt;](#_bookmark2174) _PSD_ is a _path pattern union operand_ of _PSD_.

_PPUOP_ shall not contain a reference to an element variable that is not declared in _PPUOP_ or outside of _PSD_.

1. An [&lt;element pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2184) _EP_ that contains an [&lt;element pattern where clause&gt;](#_bookmark2201) _EPWC_ is transformed as follows:
    1. Let _EPF_ be the [&lt;element pattern filler&gt;](#_bookmark2190) simply contained in _EP_.
    2. Let _PREFIX_ be the [&lt;delimiter token&gt;](#_bookmark4838) contained in _EP_ before _EPF_ and let _SUFFIX_ be the

[&lt;delimiter token&gt;](#_bookmark4838) contained in _EP_ after _EPF_.

- 1. Let _EV_ be the [&lt;element variable&gt;](#_bookmark4443) simply contained in _EPF_.
  2. Let _ILE_ be defined as follows. If _EPF_ simply contains the [&lt;is label expression&gt;](#_bookmark2194) _ILE_CAND_, then

_ILE_ is _ILE_CAND_; otherwise, _ILE_ is the zero-length character string.

- 1. _EP_ is effectively replaced by

( _PREFIX EV ILE SUFFIX EPWC_ )

1. An [&lt;element pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2184) that does not contain an [&lt;element variable declaration&gt;](#_bookmark2193), an [<is label](#_bookmark2194) [expression>](#_bookmark2194), or an [&lt;element pattern predicate&gt;](#_bookmark2200) is said to be _empty_.

( _EP_ )

inserted between them.

- 1. If an edge pattern _EP_ contained in a [&lt;path term&gt;](#_bookmark2176) _PST_ at the same depth of graph pattern matching is not preceded by a [&lt;node pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2188) contained in _PST_ at the same depth of graph

pattern matching, then an implicit empty [&lt;node pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2188) is inserted in _PST_ immediately prior to _EP_.

- 1. If an edge pattern _EP_ contained in a [&lt;path term&gt;](#_bookmark2176) _PST_ at the same depth of graph pattern matching is not followed by a [&lt;node pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2188) contained in _PST_ at the same depth of graph

pattern matching, than an implicit empty [&lt;node pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2188) is inserted in _PST_ immediately after

_EP_.

NOTE 240 — As a result of the preceding transformations, a fixed length path pattern has an odd number of [&lt;element pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2184)s, beginning and ending with [&lt;node pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2188)s, and alternating between

[&lt;node pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2188)s and [&lt;edge pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2209)s.
