1. The _minimum node count_ of certain BNF non-terminal instances defined in this Subclause is defined recursively as follows:
    1. The minimum node count of a [&lt;node pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2188) is 1 (one).
    2. The minimum node count of an [&lt;edge pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2209) is 0 (zero).
    3. The minimum node count of a [&lt;path concatenation&gt;](#_bookmark2177) _PC_ is: Case:
        1. If two successive [&lt;element pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2184)s contained in _PC_ at the same depth of graph pattern matching are [&lt;node pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2188)s, then 1 (one) less than the sum of the minimum node counts of its operands.
        2. Otherwise, the sum of the minimum node counts of its operands.
    4. The minimum node count of a [&lt;path pattern union&gt;](#_bookmark2174) or [&lt;path multiset alternation&gt;](#_bookmark2172) is the minimum of the minimum node count of its operands.
    5. The minimum node count of a [&lt;quantified path primary&gt;](#_bookmark2179) is the product of the minimum node count of the simply contained [&lt;path primary&gt;](#_bookmark2183) and the value of the [&lt;lower bound&gt;](#_bookmark2392) of the simply contained [&lt;graph pattern quantifier&gt;](#_bookmark2385).
    6. The minimum node count of a [&lt;questioned path primary&gt;](#_bookmark2181) is 0 (zero).
    7. The minimum node count of a [&lt;parenthesized path pattern expression&gt;](#_bookmark2231) is the minimum node count of the simply contained [&lt;path pattern expression&gt;](#_bookmark2171).
    8. If _BNF1_ and _BNF2_ are two BNF non-terminal instances such that _BNF1_ ::= _BNF2_ and the min- imum node count of _BNF2_ is defined, then the minimum node count of _BNF1_ is also defined and is the same as the minimum node count of _BNF2_.
2. The [&lt;path pattern expression&gt;](#_bookmark2171) simply contained in a [&lt;path pattern&gt;](#_bookmark1993) shall have a minimum node count that is greater than 0 (zero).

NOTE 241 — The minimum node count is computed after the syntactic transform that adds implicit node patterns. Thus a single [&lt;edge pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2209) is a permitted [&lt;path pattern&gt;](#_bookmark1993) because it implies two [<node pat-](#_bookmark2188) [tern>](#_bookmark2188)s.

NOTE 242 — A later Syntax Rule makes the same requirement of a [<parenthesized path pattern expres-](#_bookmark2231) [sion>](#_bookmark2231) that simply contains a [&lt;subpath variable declaration&gt;](#_bookmark2236).

1. An [&lt;element variable&gt;](#_bookmark4443) _EV_ contained in an [&lt;element variable declaration&gt;](#_bookmark2193) _GPVD_ is said to be _declared_

by _GPVD_, and by the [&lt;element pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2184) _EP_ that simply contains _GPVD_. The [&lt;element variable&gt;](#_bookmark4443) is the name of an element variable, which is also declared by _GPVD_ and _EP_. If _GPVD_ simply contains TEMP, then _EV_ is a temporary element variable.

If _EV_ is a temporary element variable, then the scope of _EV_ is the innermost [&lt;path term&gt;](#_bookmark2176) containing _EP_; otherwise, the scope of _EV_ is the innermost [&lt;graph pattern binding table&gt;](#_bookmark1933) containing _EP_.
3. If a [&lt;parenthesized path pattern expression&gt;](#_bookmark2231) _PPPE_ simply contains a [&lt;subpath variable declaration&gt;](#_bookmark2236), then the minimum node count of _PPPE_ shall be greater than 0 (zero).
4. If an [&lt;element pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2184) _EP_ that contains an [&lt;element pattern where clause&gt;](#_bookmark2201) _EPWC_, then _EP_ shall simply contain an [&lt;element variable declaration&gt;](#_bookmark2193) _GPVD_.
5. If _EV_ is an element variable or subpath variable, and _BNT_ is an instance of a BNF non-terminal, then the terminology “_BNT_ exposes _EV_” is defined as follows. The full terminology is one of the following: “_BNT_ exposes _EV_ as an unconditional singleton variable”, “_BNT_ exposes _EV_ as a conditional singleton variable”, “_BNT_ exposes _EV_ as an effectively bounded group variable” or “_BNT_ exposes _EV_ as an effectively unbounded group variable”. The terms “unconditional singleton variable”, “conditional singleton variable”, “effectively bounded group variable”, and “effectively unbounded group variable” are called the _degree of exposure_.
    1. An [&lt;element pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2184) _EP_ that declares an element variable _EV_ exposes _EV_ as an unconditional singleton.
    2. A [&lt;parenthesized path pattern expression&gt;](#_bookmark2231) _PPPE_ that simply contains a [<subpath variable](#_bookmark2236) [declaration>](#_bookmark2236) that declares _EV_ exposes _EV_ as an unconditional singleton variable. _PPPE_ shall not contain another [&lt;parenthesized path pattern expression&gt;](#_bookmark2231) that declares _EV_.
    3. If a [&lt;path concatenation&gt;](#_bookmark2177) _PPC_ declares _EV_ then let _PT_ be the [&lt;path term&gt;](#_bookmark2176) and let _PF_ be the

[&lt;path factor&gt;](#_bookmark2178) simply contained in _PPC_. Case:

- - 1. If _EV_ is exposed as an unconditional singleton by both _PT_ and _PF_, then _EV_ is exposed as an unconditional singleton by _PPC_. _EV_ shall not be a subpath variable.

NOTE 244 — This case expresses an implicit join on _EV_ within _PPC_. Implicit joins between conditional singleton variables, group variables, or subpath variables are forbidden.

- - 1. Otherwise, _EV_ shall only be exposed by one of _PT_ or _PF_. In this case _EV_ is exposed by

_PPC_ in the same degree that it is exposed by _PT_ or _PF_.

exposes _EV_ as an unconditional singleton variable.

        2.  If at least one operand of _PA_ exposes _EV_ as an effectively bounded group variable, then

_PA_ exposes _EV_ as an effectively bounded group variable.

- - 1. Otherwise, _PA_ exposes _EV_ as a conditional singleton variable.

# Conformance Rules

1. Conforming GQL language shall not contain an [&lt;element variable declaration&gt;](#_bookmark2193) that immediately contains TEMP.

NOTE 249 — An [&lt;element variable declaration&gt;](#_bookmark2193) containing TEMP is a specification device and is not syntax available to the user.

1. Without Feature G030, “Path multiset alternation”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a

[&lt;path multiset alternation&gt;](#_bookmark2172).

1. Without Feature G031, “Path multiset alternation: variable length path operands”, in conforming GQL language, an operand of a [&lt;path multiset alternation&gt;](#_bookmark2172) shall be a fixed length path pattern.
2. Without Feature G032, “Path pattern union”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [<path](#_bookmark2174) [pattern union>](#_bookmark2174).
3. Without Feature G033, “Path pattern union: variable length path operands”, in conforming GQL language, an operand of a [&lt;path pattern union&gt;](#_bookmark2174) shall be a fixed length path pattern.
4. Without Feature G035, “Quantified paths”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [<quantified](#_bookmark2179) [path primary>](#_bookmark2179) that does not immediately contain a [&lt;path primary&gt;](#_bookmark2183) that is an [&lt;edge pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2209).
5. Without Feature G036, “Quantified edges”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [<quantified](#_bookmark2179) [path primary>](#_bookmark2179) that immediately contains a [&lt;path primary&gt;](#_bookmark2183) that is an [&lt;edge pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2209).
6. Without Feature G037, “Questioned paths”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [<questioned](#_bookmark2181) [path primary>](#_bookmark2181).
7. Without Feature G038, “Parenthesized path pattern expression”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [&lt;parenthesized path pattern expression&gt;](#_bookmark2231).
8. Without Feature G041, “Non-local element pattern predicates”, in conforming GQL language, the

3. Without Feature G045, “Complete abbreviated edge patterns”, conforming GQL language shall not contain an [&lt;abbreviated edge pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2223) that is not a [&lt;minus sign&gt;](#_bookmark5034), a [&lt;left arrow&gt;](#_bookmark4881), or a [&lt;right arrow&gt;](#_bookmark4894).

Without Feature G046, “Relaxed topological consistency: adjacent vertex patterns”, in conforming GQL language, between any two [&lt;node pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2188)s contained in a [&lt;path pattern expression&gt;](#_bookmark2171) there shall be at least one [&lt;edge pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2209), [&lt;left paren&gt;](#_bookmark5032), or [&lt;right paren&gt;](#_bookmark5043).
5. Without Feature G047, “Relaxed topological consistency: concise edge patterns”, in conforming GQL language, an [&lt;edge pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2209) shall be immediately preceded and followed by a [&lt;node pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2188).

# [&lt;label expression&gt;](#_bookmark2355) Function

Specify an expression that matches one or more labels of a graph.

# Format

&lt;label expression&gt; ::=

[&lt;label term&gt;](#_bookmark2358)

| [&lt;label disjunction&gt;](#_bookmark2356)

&lt;label disjunction&gt; ::=

[&lt;label expression&gt;](#_bookmark2355) [&lt;vertical bar&gt;](#_bookmark5047) [&lt;label term&gt;](#_bookmark2358)

&lt;label term&gt; ::=

[&lt;label factor&gt;](#_bookmark2361)

| [&lt;label conjunction&gt;](#_bookmark2359)

&lt;label conjunction&gt; ::=

[&lt;label term&gt;](#_bookmark2358) [&lt;ampersand&gt;](#_bookmark5019) [&lt;label factor&gt;](#_bookmark2361)

&lt;label factor&gt; ::=

[&lt;label primary&gt;](#_bookmark2364)

| [&lt;label negation&gt;](#_bookmark2362)

&lt;label negation&gt; ::=

[&lt;exclamation mark&gt;](#_bookmark5027) [&lt;label primary&gt;](#_bookmark2364)

&lt;label primary&gt; ::=

[&lt;label name&gt;](#_bookmark4435)

| [&lt;wildcard label&gt;](#_bookmark2366)

| [&lt;parenthesized label expression&gt;](#_bookmark2368)

&lt;wildcard label&gt; ::=

[&lt;percent&gt;](#_bookmark5035)

&lt;parenthesized label expression&gt; ::=

[&lt;left paren&gt;](#_bookmark5032) [&lt;label expression&gt;](#_bookmark2355) [&lt;right paren&gt;](#_bookmark5043)

# Syntax Rules

1. Let _LE_ be the [&lt;label expression&gt;](#_bookmark2355).
2. The current working graph site of _LE_ shall not be “omitted”.
3. Let _CWGS_ be the current working graph site of _LE_.
4. Case:
    1. If _LE_ is simply contained in an [&lt;is label expression&gt;](#_bookmark2194), then:
        1. Let _GRVT_ be the graph reference value type that is the declared type of _CWGS_.
        2. If _GRVT_ is a closed graph reference value type with constraining GQL-object type _COT_

then:

- - - 1. If _LE_ is simply contained in a [&lt;node pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2188), then _LE_ is a _node_ [_&lt;label expression&gt;_](#_bookmark2355). Every [&lt;label name&gt;](#_bookmark4435) contained in _LE_ shall identify a node label of _COT_.

    1. [**&lt;label expression&gt;**](#_bookmark2355)
        - 1. Otherwise, _LE_ is an _edge_ [_&lt;label expression&gt;_](#_bookmark2355). Every [&lt;label name&gt;](#_bookmark4435) contained in _LE_

shall identify an edge label of _COT_.

- 1. Otherwise, _LE_ is simply contained in a [&lt;labeled predicate&gt;](#_bookmark3427) _LP_ and then:
        1. Let _EVR_ be the [&lt;element variable reference&gt;](#_bookmark2381) in _LP_.
        2. If the declared type of _EVR_ is a closed graph reference value type with constraining

GQL-object type _COT_, then every [&lt;label name&gt;](#_bookmark4435) contained in _LE_ shall identify a label in the label set of _COT_.

NOTE 250 — _COT_ is either a node type or an edge type. [Subclause 19.9, “](#_bookmark3425)[<labeled](#_bookmark3427) [predicate>”](#_bookmark3425), [Syntax Rule 2)](#_bookmark3433), requires that _EVR_ has singleton degree of reference and in this case,

[Subclause 16.10, “](#_bookmark2380)[<element](#_bookmark2381) [variable reference>”](#_bookmark2380), [Syntax Rule 3)a)](#_bookmark2383) requires that _EVR_ is a node reference value or an edge reference value type, whose constraining GQL-object type is a node type or an edge type, respectively.

# General Rules

_None._

# Conformance Rules

1) Without Feature G074, “Label expression: wildcard label”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [&lt;wildcard label&gt;](#_bookmark2366).

Specify element variable references.

# Format

&lt;element variable reference&gt; ::=

[&lt;binding variable reference&gt;](#_bookmark3823)

# Syntax Rules

1. Let _EVR_ be the [&lt;element variable reference&gt;](#_bookmark2381).
2. Let _EVRDT_ be the declared type of _EVR_.

    1. If the degree of reference of _EVR_ is singleton, then _EVRDT_ shall be a node reference value type or an edge reference value type.

However the actual element variable reference value is originally constructed and bound in the General Rules of [Subclause 22.6, “Application](#_bookmark5194) [of bindings to evaluate an expression”](#_bookmark5194).

_None._

# [&lt;graph pattern quantifier&gt;](#_bookmark2385) Function

Specify a graph pattern quantifier.

# Format

&lt;graph pattern quantifier&gt; ::=

[&lt;asterisk&gt;](#_bookmark5020)

| [&lt;plus sign&gt;](#_bookmark5037)

| [&lt;fixed quantifier&gt;](#_bookmark2388)

| [&lt;general quantifier&gt;](#_bookmark2390)

&lt;fixed quantifier&gt; ::=

[&lt;left brace&gt;](#_bookmark5030) [&lt;unsigned integer&gt;](#_bookmark4545) [&lt;right brace&gt;](#_bookmark5041)

&lt;general quantifier&gt; ::=

[&lt;left brace&gt;](#_bookmark5030) \[ [&lt;lower bound&gt;](#_bookmark2392) \] [&lt;comma&gt;](#_bookmark5022) \[ [&lt;upper bound&gt;](#_bookmark2393) \] [&lt;right brace&gt;](#_bookmark5041)

&lt;lower bound&gt; ::=

[&lt;unsigned integer&gt;](#_bookmark4545)

&lt;upper bound&gt; ::=

[&lt;unsigned integer&gt;](#_bookmark4545)

# Syntax Rules

1. The maximum value of [&lt;upper bound&gt;](#_bookmark2393) is implementation-defined [(IL018)](#_bookmark6177). [&lt;upper bound&gt;](#_bookmark2393), if spe- cified, shall not be greater than this value.
2. Every [&lt;graph pattern quantifier&gt;](#_bookmark2385) is normalized, as follows:
    1. [&lt;asterisk&gt;](#_bookmark5020) is equivalent to:

{0,}

- 1. [&lt;plus sign&gt;](#_bookmark5037) is equivalent to:

{1,}

- 1. If [&lt;fixed quantifier&gt;](#_bookmark2388) _FQ_ is specified, then let _UI_ be the [&lt;unsigned integer&gt;](#_bookmark4545) contained in _FQ_. _FQ_

is equivalent to:

{_UI_,_UI_}

- 1. If [&lt;general quantifier&gt;](#_bookmark2390) _GQ_ is specified, and if [&lt;lower bound&gt;](#_bookmark2392) is not specified, then the [<unsigned](#_bookmark4545) [integer>](#_bookmark4545) 0 (zero) is supplied as the [&lt;lower bound&gt;](#_bookmark2392).

1. If [&lt;general quantifier&gt;](#_bookmark2390) _GQ_ is specified or implied by the preceding normalizations, then Case:
    1. If [&lt;upper bound&gt;](#_bookmark2393) is specified, then:
        1. The value of [&lt;upper bound&gt;](#_bookmark2393) _VUP_ shall be greater than 0 (zero).
        2. The value of [&lt;lower bound&gt;](#_bookmark2392) _LUP_ shall be less than or equal to _VUP_.
    2. [**&lt;graph pattern quantifier&gt;**](#_bookmark2385)
        1. If _LUP_ equals _VUP_, then _GQ_ is a _fixed quantifier_.
        2. _GQ_ is a _bounded quantifier_.
    3. Otherwise, _GQ_ is an _unbounded quantifier_.
2. A [&lt;graph pattern quantifier&gt;](#_bookmark2385) that is not a fixed quantifier is a _variable quantifier_.

# General Rules

_None._

# Conformance Rules

1. Without Feature G060, “Bounded graph pattern quantifiers”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [&lt;fixed quantifier&gt;](#_bookmark2388) or a [&lt;general quantifier&gt;](#_bookmark2390) that immediately contains an [&lt;upper bound&gt;](#_bookmark2393).
2. Without Feature G061, “Unbounded graph pattern quantifiers”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [&lt;graph pattern quantifier&gt;](#_bookmark2385) that immediately contains an [&lt;asterisk&gt;](#_bookmark5020), a [&lt;plus sign&gt;](#_bookmark5037), or a

[&lt;general quantifier&gt;](#_bookmark2390) that does not immediately contain an [&lt;upper bound&gt;](#_bookmark2393).

( _SPPE_ )

1. The following rules are recursively applied until no [&lt;simplified path pattern expression&gt;](#_bookmark2403)s remain.

NOTE 254 — The rules work from the root of the parse tree of a [&lt;simplified path pattern expression&gt;](#_bookmark2403). At each step, the coarsest analysis of a [&lt;simplified path pattern expression&gt;](#_bookmark2403) is replaced, eliminating at least one level of the parse tree, measured from the root. Note that each replacement can create more

[&lt;simplified path pattern expression&gt;](#_bookmark2403)s than before, but these replacements have less depth. Eventually the recursion replaces [&lt;simplified path pattern expression&gt;](#_bookmark2403) with [&lt;edge pattern&gt;](#_bookmark2209).

- 1. Let _SPPE_ be a [&lt;simplified path pattern expression&gt;](#_bookmark2403).
        1. Let _SC_ be the [&lt;simplified contents&gt;](#_bookmark2416) contained in _SPPE_.
        2. Let _PREFIX_ be the [&lt;minus slash&gt;](#_bookmark4892), [&lt;left minus slash&gt;](#_bookmark4886), [&lt;tilde slash&gt;](#_bookmark4904), [&lt;left tilde slash&gt;](#_bookmark4887), or [&lt;left minus slash&gt;](#_bookmark4886) contained in _SPPE_.
        3. Let _SUFFIX_ be the [&lt;slash minus right&gt;](#_bookmark4899), [&lt;slash minus&gt;](#_bookmark4898), [&lt;slash tilde&gt;](#_bookmark4900), or [<slash tilde](#_bookmark4901) [right>](#_bookmark4901) contained in _SPPE_.
        4. Let _EDGEPRE_ and _EDGESUF_ be determined by [Table 3, “Conversion of simplified syntax](#_bookmark2464) [delimiters to default edge delimiters”](#_bookmark2464), from the row containing the values of _PREFIX_ and _SUFFIX_.

**Table 3 — Conversion of simplified syntax delimiters to default edge delimiters**

| **_PREFIX_** | **_SUFFIX_** | **_EDGEPRE_** | **_EDGESUF_** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| \-/ | /-> | \-\[ | \]-> |
| <-/ | /-  | <-\[ | \]- |
| ~/  | /~  | ~\[ | \]~ |
| ~/  | /~> | ~\[ | \]~> |
| <~/ | /~  | <~\[ | \]~ |
| <-/ | /-> | <-\[ | \]-> |
| \-/ | /-  | \-\[ | \]- |

- 1. Case:

**16.12** [**&lt;simplified path pattern expression&gt;**](#_bookmark2403)

- - 1. If _SC_ is a [&lt;simplified path union&gt;](#_bookmark2417) _SPU_, then let _N_ be the number of [&lt;simplified term&gt;](#_bookmark2421)s simply contained in _SPU_, and let _ST_1, ..., _STN_ be those [&lt;simplified term&gt;](#_bookmark2421)s; _SPPE_ is effectively replaced by:

_PREFIX ST_1 _SUFFIX_ | _PREFIX ST_2 _SUFFIX_ | ... | _PREFIX STN SUFFIX_

- - 1. If _SC_ is a [&lt;simplified multiset alternation&gt;](#_bookmark2419) _SMA_, then let _N_ be the number of [<simplified](#_bookmark2421) [term>](#_bookmark2421)s simply contained in _SMA_, and let _ST_1, ..., _STN_ be those [&lt;simplified term&gt;](#_bookmark2421)s; _SPPE_ is effectively replaced by:

_PREFIX ST_1 _SUFFIX_ |+| _PREFIX ST_2 _SUFFIX_ |+| ... |+| _PREFIX STN SUFFIX_

- - 1. If _SC_ is a [&lt;simplified concatenation&gt;](#_bookmark2422) _SCAT_, then let _ST_ be the [&lt;simplified term&gt;](#_bookmark2421) and let _SFL_ be the [&lt;simplified factor low&gt;](#_bookmark2423) simply contained in _SCAT_; _SPPE_ is effectively replaced by:

_PREFIX ST SUFFIX PREFIX SFL SUFFIX_

- - 1. If _SC_ is a [&lt;simplified conjunction&gt;](#_bookmark2426) _SAND_, then _SPPE_ is effectively replaced by:

_EDGEPRE_ IS _SAND EDGESUF_

# [&lt;where clause&gt;](#_bookmark2497)

**Function**

Compute a new binding table by selecting records from the current working table fulfilling the specified

[&lt;search condition&gt;](#_bookmark3337).

# Format

&lt;where clause&gt; ::=

WHERE [&lt;search condition&gt;](#_bookmark3337)

# Syntax Rules

1. Let _WC_ be the [&lt;where clause&gt;](#_bookmark2497) and let _SC_ be the [&lt;search condition&gt;](#_bookmark3337) immediately contained in _WC_.
2. The declared type of the incoming working record of _SC_ is the declared type of the incoming

working record of _WC_ amended with the record type of the declared type of the incoming working table of _WC_.

1. The declared type of the incoming working table of _SC_ is the material unit binding table type.
2. The declared type of _WC_ is the declared type of incoming working table of _WC_.

# General Rules

1. Let _WHERE_ be a new empty binding table.
2. For each record _R_ of the current working table:
    1. Let _INCLUDE_ be the result of _SC_ in a new child execution context amended with _R_.
    2. If _INCLUDE_ is _True_, then _R_ is added to _WHERE_.
3. The result of _WC_ is _WHERE_.

# Conformance Rules

_None._

# [&lt;yield clause&gt;](#_bookmark2500) Function

Select and rename columns of a binding table.

# Format

&lt;yield clause&gt; ::=

YIELD [&lt;yield item list&gt;](#_bookmark2502)

&lt;yield item list&gt; ::=

[&lt;yield item&gt;](#_bookmark2504) \[ { [&lt;comma&gt;](#_bookmark5022) [&lt;yield item&gt;](#_bookmark2504) }... \]

&lt;yield item&gt; ::=

{ [&lt;yield item name&gt;](#_bookmark2505) \[ [&lt;yield item alias&gt;](#_bookmark2507) \] }

&lt;yield item name&gt; ::=

[&lt;field name&gt;](#_bookmark4437)

&lt;yield item alias&gt; ::= AS [&lt;binding variable&gt;](#_bookmark4447)

# Syntax Rules

1. Let _YC_ be the [&lt;yield clause&gt;](#_bookmark2500).
2. Let _COYI_ be the collection of [&lt;yield item&gt;](#_bookmark2504)s simply contained in _YC_.
3. Let _N_ be the number of [&lt;yield item&gt;](#_bookmark2504)s in _COYI_.
4. For each [&lt;yield item&gt;](#_bookmark2504) _YIi_, 1 (one) ≤ _i_ ≤ _N_, in _COYI_:
    1. Let _YINi_ be the [&lt;yield item name&gt;](#_bookmark2505) specified by _YIi_.
    2. If _YIi_ does not immediately contain a [&lt;yield item alias&gt;](#_bookmark2507), then:
        1. _YINi_ shall be a [&lt;binding variable&gt;](#_bookmark4447).
        2. _YIi_ is effectively replaced by:

_YINi_ AS _YINi_

1. Let _YCT_ be the [&lt;yield clause&gt;](#_bookmark2500) after the preceding transformation and let _COYIT_ be the collection of

_N_ [&lt;yield item&gt;](#_bookmark2504)s simply contained in _YCT_.

1. If _COYIT_ simply contains a [&lt;yield item alias&gt;](#_bookmark2507) that simply contains a [&lt;binding variable&gt;](#_bookmark4447) _YIABV1_, then _COYIT_ shall not simply contain another [&lt;yield item alias&gt;](#_bookmark2507) that simply contains a [<binding](#_bookmark4447) [variable>](#_bookmark4447) _YIABV2_ such that _YIABV1_ and _YIABV2_ are equivalent.
2. The declared type of _YCT_ is a binding table type _BTT_ defined as follows:
    1. _BTT_ has _N_ columns.
    2. For each [&lt;yield item&gt;](#_bookmark2504) _YIi_, 1 (one) ≤ _i_ ≤ _N_ in _COYIT_:
        1. Let _YINi_ be the [&lt;yield item name&gt;](#_bookmark2505) specified by _YIi_.
    3. [**&lt;yield clause&gt;**](#_bookmark2500)
        1. Let _YIAi_ be the [&lt;binding variable&gt;](#_bookmark4447) simply contained in the [&lt;yield item alias&gt;](#_bookmark2507) specified by _YIi_.
        2. The declared type of the incoming working table of _YC_ shall have a column _SC_ with column name _YINi_.
        3. _BTT_ has a column _TC_.
        4. The column type of _TC_ is the column type of _SC_.

# General Rules

1. Let _YIELD_ be a new empty binding table.
2. For each record _R_ of the current working table in a new child execution context amended with _R_:
    1. Let _T_ be a new empty record.
    2. For each [&lt;yield item&gt;](#_bookmark2504) _YIi_, 1 (one) ≤ _i_ ≤ _N_, from _COYIT_:
        1. Let _YINi_ be the [&lt;yield item name&gt;](#_bookmark2505) specified by _YIi_.
        2. Let _Fi_ be the field of the current working record whose name is _YINi_.
        3. Let _YIVi_ be the value of _Fi_.

NOTE 258 — As opposed to the General Rules for [&lt;binding variable&gt;](#_bookmark4447), [&lt;yield item&gt;](#_bookmark2504)s only consider the current working record and ignore the working records of any parent execution contexts that precede the current execution context in the current execution stack.

- - 1. Let _YIAi_ be the [&lt;binding variable&gt;](#_bookmark4447) simply contained in the [&lt;yield item alias&gt;](#_bookmark2507) specified by _YIi_.
        2.  A new field with name _YIAi_ and with value _YIVi_ is added to _T_.

    1. _T_ is added to _YIELD_.

1. The result of _YCT_ is _YIELD_.

# Conformance Rules

_None._

# [&lt;group by clause&gt;](#_bookmark2513) Function

Define a [&lt;group by clause&gt;](#_bookmark2513) for specifying the set of grouping keys to be used during grouping.

# Format

&lt;group by clause&gt; ::=

GROUP BY [&lt;grouping element list&gt;](#_bookmark2515)

&lt;grouping element list&gt; ::=

[&lt;grouping element&gt;](#_bookmark2517) \[ { [&lt;comma&gt;](#_bookmark5022) [&lt;grouping element&gt;](#_bookmark2517) }... \]

| [&lt;empty grouping set&gt;](#_bookmark2519)

&lt;grouping element&gt; ::=

[&lt;binding variable reference&gt;](#_bookmark3823)

&lt;empty grouping set&gt; ::=

[&lt;left paren&gt;](#_bookmark5032) [&lt;right paren&gt;](#_bookmark5043)

# Syntax Rules

1. Let _GBC_ be the [&lt;group by clause&gt;](#_bookmark2513) and let _GEL_ be the [&lt;grouping element list&gt;](#_bookmark2515).
2. Let _COLS_ be the sequence of columns defined as follows. Case:
    1. If _GEL_ is the [&lt;empty grouping set&gt;](#_bookmark2519), then _COLS_ is the empty sequence.
    2. Otherwise:
        1. Let _GESEQ_ be the sequence of [&lt;grouping element&gt;](#_bookmark2517)s immediately contained in _GEL_ and let _NGESEQ_ be the number of such [&lt;grouping element&gt;](#_bookmark2517)s in _GESEQ_.
        2. For every _i_\-th element _GEi_ of _GESEQ_, 1 (one) ≤ _i_ ≤ _NGESEQ_:
            1. Let _BVRi_ be the [&lt;binding variable reference&gt;](#_bookmark3823) immediately contained in _GEi_.
            2. The declared type of the incoming working record of _BVRi_ is the declared type of the incoming working record of _GBC_ amended with the record type of the declared type of the incoming working table of _GBC_.
            3. The declared type of the incoming working table of _BVRi_ is the unit binding table type.
            4. _BVRi_ is an operand of a grouping operation. The Syntax Rules and Conformance Rules of [Subclause 22.15, “Grouping operations”](#_bookmark5273), apply.
            5. Let _GEBVi_ be the name of the binding variable referenced by _BVRi_.
            6. Let _COL_i be the column whose name is _GEBVi_ and whose type is the declared type of _BVRi_.
            7. Append _COL_ to _COLS_.
    3. [**&lt;group by clause&gt;**](#_bookmark2513)
3. The declared type of the outgoing working table of _GBC_ is a material binding table whose set of columns is _COLS_.
4. The declared type of the outgoing working record of _GBC_ is the declared type of the incoming working record of _GBC_.
5. The declared type of _GBC_ is the declared type of the outgoing working table of _GBC_.

# General Rules

| 1)  | Case: a)<br><br>b) | If _GEL_ is the [&lt;empty grouping set&gt;](#_bookmark2519), then let _GROUP_BY_ be a unit binding table. Otherwise: |
| --- | --- | --- |
|     |     | i) For _i_, 1 (one) ≤ _i_ ≤ _NGESEQ_, let _GEi_be the _i_\-th element of _GESEQ_ and let _GEBVi_ be the<br><br>[&lt;binding variable reference&gt;](#_bookmark3823) simply contained in _GEBVi_. |
| ii) Let _GROUP_BY_ be a new empty binding table with the column set _COLS_. |
| iii) For each record _R_ of the current working table in a new child execution context amended with _R_: |
| 1) Let _T_ be a new record comprising fields _Fi_, 1 (one) ≤ _i_ ≤ _NGESEQ_, such that the name of _Fi_ is the name of _COLSi_ and the value of _Fi_ is the value of _GEBVi_ in _R_. |
| 2) If _T_ is distinct from every record in _GROUP_BY_, then _T_ is added to _GROUP_BY_. |

2) The result of _GBC_ is _GROUP_BY_.

# Conformance Rules

1) Without Feature GQ15, “GROUP BY clause”, conforming GQL language shall not contain [<group by](#_bookmark2513) [clause>](#_bookmark2513).

# [&lt;sort specification list&gt;](#_bookmark2529) Function

Obtaining an ordered binding table from the current working table.

# Format

&lt;sort specification list&gt; ::=

[&lt;sort specification&gt;](#_bookmark2531) \[ { [&lt;comma&gt;](#_bookmark5022) [&lt;sort specification&gt;](#_bookmark2531) }... \]

&lt;sort specification&gt; ::=

[&lt;sort key&gt;](#_bookmark2532) \[ [&lt;ordering specification&gt;](#_bookmark2534) \] \[ [&lt;null ordering&gt;](#_bookmark2539) \]

&lt;sort key&gt; ::=

[&lt;aggregating value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3488)

&lt;ordering specification&gt; ::= ASC

| ASCENDING

| DESC

| DESCENDING

&lt;null ordering&gt; ::= NULLS FIRST

| NULLS LAST

# Syntax Rules

1. Each [&lt;value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3470) immediately contained in the [&lt;sort key&gt;](#_bookmark2532) contained in a [&lt;sort specification&gt;](#_bookmark2531) is an operand of an ordering operation. The Syntax Rules and Conformance Rules of [Subclause 22.14,](#_bookmark5263) [“Ordering operations”](#_bookmark5263), apply.
2. Let _SSL_ be the [&lt;sort specification list&gt;](#_bookmark2529)
3. Let _NSS_ be the number of [&lt;sort specification&gt;](#_bookmark2531)s immediately contained in _SSL_.
4. For _i_, 1 (one) ≤ _i_ ≤ _NSS_, let _SSi_ be the _i_\-th [&lt;sort specification&gt;](#_bookmark2531) immediately contained in _SSL_.
5. For each _SSi_, 1 (one) ≤ _i_ ≤ _NSS_:
    1. Let _SKi_ be the [&lt;sort key&gt;](#_bookmark2532) immediately contained in _SSi_.
    2. If _SSi_ does not immediately contain an [&lt;ordering specification&gt;](#_bookmark2534), then _SSi_ is effectively replaced by:

_SKi_ ASC

- 1. The declared type of the incoming working record of _SKi_ is the declared type of the incoming working record of _SSL_ amended with the record type of the declared type of the incoming working table of _SSL_.
  2. The declared type of the incoming working table of _SKi_ is the material unit binding table type.
  3. The declared type of _SKi_ is the declared type of the [&lt;aggregating value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3488) immediately contained in _SKi_.

**16.17** [**&lt;sort specification list&gt;**](#_bookmark2529)

1. If [&lt;null ordering&gt;](#_bookmark2539) is not specified, then an implementation-defined [(IS001)](#_bookmark6181) [&lt;null ordering&gt;](#_bookmark2539) is

implicit. The implementation-defined default for [&lt;null ordering&gt;](#_bookmark2539) shall not depend on the context outside of [&lt;sort specification list&gt;](#_bookmark2529).

1. The declared type of _SSL_ is the declared type of the incoming working table of _SSL_.

# General Rules

1. Let _SORTED_ be a new ordered binding table created from the collection of records of the current working table by ordering the records, as follows:
    1. Let _N_ be the number of [&lt;sort specification&gt;](#_bookmark2531)s.
    2. For _i_, 1 (one) ≤ _i_ ≤ _N_, let _Ki_ be the [&lt;sort key&gt;](#_bookmark2532) contained in the _i_\-th [&lt;sort specification&gt;](#_bookmark2531).
    3. Each [&lt;sort specification&gt;](#_bookmark2531) specifies the _sort direction_ for the corresponding sort key _Ki_. If neither DESC nor DESCENDING is specified in the _i_\-th [&lt;sort specification&gt;](#_bookmark2531), then the sort dir- ection for _Ki_ is ascending and the applicable [&lt;comp op&gt;](#_bookmark3355) is the [&lt;less than operator&gt;](#_bookmark4888); otherwise, the sort direction for _Ki_ is descending and the applicable [&lt;comp op&gt;](#_bookmark3355) is the [<greater than](#_bookmark4878) [operator>](#_bookmark4878).
    4. Let _P_ be any record of the collection of records to be ordered, and let _Q_ be any other record of the same collection of records.
    5. Let _PVi_ be the result of _Ki_ in a new child execution context amended with _P_.
    6. Let _QVi_ be the result of _Ki_ in a new child execution context amended with _Q_.
    7. The relative position of records _P_ and _Q_ in the result is determined by comparing _PVi_ and _QVi_

as follows:

- - 1. The comparison is performed according to the General Rules of [Subclause 19.3,](#_bookmark3352) [“](#_bookmark3352)[<comparison](#_bookmark3353) [predicate>”](#_bookmark3352), where the [&lt;comp op&gt;](#_bookmark3355) is the applicable [&lt;comp op&gt;](#_bookmark3355) for _Ki_.
        2.  The comparison is performed with the following special treatment of null values. Case:
            1.  If _PVi_ and _QVi_ are both the null value, then they are considered equal to each other.
            2.  If _PV__i_ is the null value and _QVi_ is not the null value, then Case:
                1.  If NULLS FIRST is specified or implied, then _PVi_ [&lt;comp op&gt;](#_bookmark3355) _QVi_ is considered to be _True_.
                2.  If NULLS LAST is specified or implied, then _PVi_ [&lt;comp op&gt;](#_bookmark3355) _QVi_ is considered to be _False_.
            3.  If _PVi_ is not the null value and _QVi_ is the null value, then Case:
                1.  If NULLS FIRST is specified or implied, then _PVi_ [&lt;comp op&gt;](#_bookmark3355) _QVi_ is considered to be _False_.
                2.  If NULLS LAST is specified or implied, then _PVi_ [&lt;comp op&gt;](#_bookmark3355) _QVi_ is considered to be _True_.

    1. [**&lt;sort specification list&gt;**](#_bookmark2529)
    2. _PVi_ is said to _precede QVi_ if the result of the [&lt;comparison predicate&gt;](#_bookmark3353) “_PVi_ [&lt;comp op&gt;](#_bookmark3355) _QVi_” is

_True_ for the applicable [&lt;comp op&gt;](#_bookmark3355).

- 1. If _PVi_ and _QVi_ are not the null value and the result of “_PVi_ [&lt;comp op&gt;](#_bookmark3355) _QVi_” is _Unknown_, then the relative ordering of _PVi_ and _QVi_ is implementation-dependent [(US007)](#_bookmark6225).
  2. The relative position of record _P_ is before record _Q_ if for some _n_, 1 (one) ≤ _n_ ≤ _N_, _PVn_ precedes

_QVn_ and _PVi_ is not distinct from _QVi_ for all _i_ < _n_.

- 1. Two records that are not distinct with respect to the [&lt;sort specification&gt;](#_bookmark2531)s are said to be _peers_

of each other. The relative ordering of peers is implementation-dependent [(US006)](#_bookmark6224).

- 1. The result of _SSL_ is _SORTED_.

# Conformance Rules

1) Without Feature GA03, “Explicit ordering of nulls”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a

[&lt;null ordering&gt;](#_bookmark2539).

# [&lt;limit clause&gt;](#_bookmark2561) Function

Obtain a new binding table that retains only a limited number of records of the current working table.

# Format

&lt;limit clause&gt; ::=

LIMIT [&lt;non-negative integer specification&gt;](#_bookmark3533)

# Syntax Rules

1. Let _LC_ be the [&lt;limit clause&gt;](#_bookmark2561).
2. The declared type of _LC_ is the declared type of the incoming working table of _LC_.

# General Rules

1. Let _TABLE_ be the current working table.
2. If _TABLE_ is not ordered, then let _ORDERED_TABLE_ be a new ordered binding table created from the result of sorting the collection of all records of _TABLE_ according to an [implementation-dependent](#_bookmark6222) [(US001)](#_bookmark6222) order; otherwise, let _ORDERED_TABLE_ be _TABLE_.
3. Let _V_ be the result of the [&lt;non-negative integer specification&gt;](#_bookmark3533).
4. Let _LIMIT_ be a new ordered binding table obtained by selecting only the first _V_ records of

_ORDERED_TABLE_ and discarding all subsequent records.

NOTE 259 — If the order of the result of _LC_ has no effect on the outcome of a [&lt;GQL-program&gt;](#_bookmark965), there is no need for _LIMIT_ to be indicated as ordered.

1. The result of _LC_ is _LIMIT_.

# Conformance Rules

_None._

NOTE 260 — If the order of the result of _OC_ has no effect on the outcome of a [&lt;GQL-program&gt;](#_bookmark965), there is no need for _OFFSET_ to be indicated as ordered.

1. Let _V_ be the result of the [&lt;non-negative integer specification&gt;](#_bookmark3533).
2. Let _OFFSET_ be a new ordered binding table obtained from all but the first _V_ records of

_ORDERED_TABLE_.

    1. If _COPR_ simply contains a [&lt;schema reference&gt;](#_bookmark2574) that is a [&lt;solidus&gt;](#_bookmark5044), then _COPR_ shall not imme- diately contain a [&lt;solidus&gt;](#_bookmark5044).
    2. Otherwise, _COPR_ shall immediately contain a [&lt;solidus&gt;](#_bookmark5044).

NOTE 261 — // is not a valid [&lt;catalog object parent reference&gt;](#_bookmark2631).

1. Let the GQL-schema _SCHEMA_ be defined as follows. Case:
    1. If _COPR_ immediately contains a [&lt;schema reference&gt;](#_bookmark2574) _CSR_, then _SCHEMA_ is the GQL-schema identified by _CSR_.
    2. Otherwise:
        1. The current working schema of _COPR_ shall not be “omitted”.
        2. _SCHEMA_ is the current working schema of _COPR_.
2. Let _ONSEQ_ be the sequence of all [&lt;object name&gt;](#_bookmark4421)s that are immediately contained in _COPR_. Let _N_ be the number of elements of _ONSEQ_.
3. For _i_, 1 (one) ≤ _i_ ≤ _N_, let _ONi_ be the _i_\-th element of _ONSEQ_.
4. The GQL-schema or catalog object identified by _COPR_ is defined as follows. Case:
    1. If _N_ is 0 (zero), then _COPR_ identifies the GQL-schema _SCHEMA_.
    2. Otherwise,
        1. The GQL-schema _SCHEMA_ shall contain a catalog object with name _ON_1.
        2. Let _CO_1 be the catalog object with name _ON_1 contained in _SCHEMA_.
        3. For _j_, 2 (two) ≤ _j_ ≤ _N_, the catalog object _COj_ is defined as follows:
            1. The catalog object _COj_\-1 shall contain a catalog object with name _ONj_.
    3. [**&lt;catalog object parent reference&gt;**](#_bookmark2631)
        - 1. _COj_ is the catalog object with name _ONj_ contained in _COj_\-1.

# [&lt;nested graph type specification&gt;](#_bookmark2657)

**Function**

Specify a graph type.

# Format

&lt;nested graph type specification&gt; ::=

[&lt;left brace&gt;](#_bookmark5030) [&lt;graph type specification body&gt;](#_bookmark2659) [&lt;right brace&gt;](#_bookmark5041)

&lt;graph type specification body&gt; ::=

[&lt;element type list&gt;](#_bookmark2660)

&lt;element type list&gt; ::=

[&lt;element type specification&gt;](#_bookmark2662) \[ { [&lt;comma&gt;](#_bookmark5022) [&lt;element type specification&gt;](#_bookmark2662) }... \]

&lt;element type specification&gt; ::=

[&lt;node type specification&gt;](#_bookmark2689)

| [&lt;edge type specification&gt;](#_bookmark2736)

# Syntax Rules

1. Let _NGTS_ be the [&lt;nested graph type specification&gt;](#_bookmark2657).
2. Let _GTSB_ be the [&lt;graph type specification body&gt;](#_bookmark2659) simply contained in _NGTS_.
3. An _element type specification_ of _GTSB_ is a [&lt;node type specification&gt;](#_bookmark2689) or an [&lt;edge type specification&gt;](#_bookmark2736) simply contained in _GTSB_.
4. The _property names_ of an element type specification _AETS_ are given by the set of names of all property types of _AETS_.
5. For two element type specifications _ET1_ and _ET2_ of a [&lt;graph type specification body&gt;](#_bookmark2659), whether

_ET1_ and _ET2_ are _property name-sharing_ is defined as follows:

Case:

1. _ETS_ specifies an edge type as follows. Case:
    1. If _ETS_ simply contains an [&lt;edge type pattern directed&gt;](#_bookmark2749), then _ETS_ specifies the directed edge type with:
        1. The edge type label set that is the label set of _ETS_.
        2. The edge type property type set that is the property type set of _ETS_.
        3. The source node type that is the source node type of _ETS_.
        4. The destination node type that is the destination node type of _ETS_.
    2. [**&lt;edge type specification&gt;**](#_bookmark2736)
    3. Otherwise, _ETS_ simply contains an [&lt;edge type pattern undirected&gt;](#_bookmark2753) and _ETS_ specifies the undirected edge type with:
        1. The edge type label set that is the label set of _ETS_.
        2. The edge type property type set that is the property type set of _ETS_.
        3. The set of endpoint node types that is the set comprising the source node type of _ETS_

and the destination node type of _ETS_.

1. For each edge type _ET_, there is an implementation-defined [(IV003)](#_bookmark6184) edge type, _ETNF_(_ET_), known as the _normal form_ of _ET_ (which can be _ET_ itself), such that:
    1. If _ET1_ and _ET2_ are two directed edge types that have the same label sets, the same property names _PNS_, respective source node types with the same normal form, and respective destin- ation node types with the same normal form, and for each property name _PN_ from _PNS_ it holds that the value types of the respective property types of _ET1_ and _ET2_ whose name is _PN_ have the same normal form, then _ETNF_(_ET1_) = _ETNF_(_ET2_).
    2. If _ET1_ and _ET2_ are two undirected edge types that have the same label sets, the same property names _PNS_, and the same sets of normal forms of their respective endpoint node types, and for each property name _PN_ from _PNS_ it holds that the value types of the respective property types of _ET1_ and _ET2_ whose name is _PN_ have the same normal form, then then _ETNF_(_ET1_) = _ETNF_(_ET2_).
    3. _ETNF_(_ETNF_(_ET_)) = _ETNF_(_ET_).
    4. The results of all invocations of _ETNF_(_ET_) are the same.

NOTE 269 — This ensures that all invocations of the implementation-defined [(IV003)](#_bookmark6184) choice of the normal form of an edge type from amongst the equivalent edge types are deterministic.

# General Rules

1. An edge type descriptor is created for the edge type _ET_ specified by _ETS_ that describes _ET_ and comprises:
    1. The declared name of the primary base type of all edge types (EDGE DATA).

NOTE 270 — See [Subclause 4.13.1, “Introduction to GQL-object types and related base types”](#_bookmark541).

- 1. The preferred name of _ET_.
  2. The edge type label set of _ET_.
  3. The edge type property type set of _ET_.
  4. Case:
        1. If _ET_ is directed, then:
            1. The indication that the edge type is directed.
            2. The source node type of _ET_.
            3. The destination node type of _ET_.
        2. Otherwise:
            1. The indication that the edge type is undirected.
            2. The set of endpoint node types of _ET_.
  5. [**&lt;edge type specification&gt;**](#_bookmark2736)

# Conformance Rules

1. Without Feature GH02, “Undirected edge patterns”, conforming GQL language shall not contain an

[&lt;edge type specification&gt;](#_bookmark2736) that simply contains an [&lt;edge kind&gt;](#_bookmark2764) that is UNDIRECTED, an [<endpoint](#_bookmark2769) [pair>](#_bookmark2769) that is an [&lt;endpoint pair undirected&gt;](#_bookmark2774), or an [&lt;edge type pattern undirected&gt;](#_bookmark2753).

1. Without Feature GG20, “Explicit element type names”, in conforming GQL language, an [<edge type](#_bookmark2736) [specification>](#_bookmark2736) shall not simply contain an [&lt;edge type name&gt;](#_bookmark4431).
2. Without Feature GG21, “Explicit element type key label sets”, in conforming GQL language, an [<edge](#_bookmark2736) [type specification>](#_bookmark2736) shall not simply contain an [&lt;edge type key label set&gt;](#_bookmark2744) or a [<node type key label](#_bookmark2700) [set>](#_bookmark2700).

[&lt;label name&gt;](#_bookmark4435) \[ { [&lt;ampersand&gt;](#_bookmark5019) [&lt;label name&gt;](#_bookmark4435) }... \]

# Syntax Rules

1. If a [&lt;label set phrase&gt;](#_bookmark2850) _LSP_ simply contains LABEL and the [&lt;label name&gt;](#_bookmark4435) _LN_, then _LSP_ is equivalent to:

:_LN_

1. Every [&lt;label set phrase&gt;](#_bookmark2850) _LSP_ specifies the label set specified by the implicit or explicit [<label set](#_bookmark2854) [specification>](#_bookmark2854) immediately contained in _LSP_.
2. Every [&lt;label set specification&gt;](#_bookmark2854) _LSS_ specifies the set of distinct label names specified by the [<label](#_bookmark4435) [name>](#_bookmark4435)s simply contained in _LSS_.

- 1. [**&lt;property type&gt;**](#_bookmark2862)

# [&lt;property type&gt;](#_bookmark2862) Function

Define a property type.

# Format

&lt;property type&gt; ::=

[&lt;property name&gt;](#_bookmark4436) \[ [&lt;typed&gt;](#_bookmark2881) \] [&lt;property value type&gt;](#_bookmark2869)

# Syntax Rules

1. The _name_ of a [&lt;property type&gt;](#_bookmark2862) _APT_ is the name specified by the [&lt;property name&gt;](#_bookmark4436) simply contained in _APT_.
2. The _value type_ of a [&lt;property type&gt;](#_bookmark2862) _APT_ is the value type specified by the [&lt;property value type&gt;](#_bookmark2869) simply contained in _APT_.
3. The property type specified by the [&lt;property type&gt;](#_bookmark2862) _TPT_ is the pair comprising the name of _TPT_

and the value type of _TPT_.

1. The value type of the property type specified by a [&lt;property type&gt;](#_bookmark2862) shall be a supported property value type.

NOTE 271 — See [Subclause 4.3.4, “Properties and supported property value types”](#_bookmark199).

# General Rules

1. A data type descriptor is created that describes the value type of the property type being defined.
2. A property type descriptor is created that describes the property type being defined. The property type descriptor includes the following:
    1. The name of the property type.
    2. The value type of the property type.

# Conformance Rules

1) Without Feature GV48, “Nested record types”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a

[&lt;property type&gt;](#_bookmark2862) that simply contains a [&lt;record type&gt;](#_bookmark3009).

- 1. [**&lt;binding table type&gt;**](#_bookmark2872)

# [&lt;binding table type&gt;](#_bookmark2872) Function

Define a binding table type.

# Format

&lt;binding table type&gt; ::=

\[ BINDING \] TABLE [&lt;field types specification&gt;](#_bookmark3011)

# Syntax Rules

1. Every [&lt;binding table type&gt;](#_bookmark2872) _BTT_ specifies a material binding table type whose record type is the closed material record type whose field types are specified by the [&lt;field types specification&gt;](#_bookmark3011)

immediately contained in _BTT_.

1. For each binding table type _BTT_, there is an implementation-defined [(IV003)](#_bookmark6184) binding table type,

_BTNF_(_BTT_), known as the _normal form_ of _BTT_ (which can be _BTT_ itself), such that:

- 1. If _BTT1_ and _BTT2_ are two binding table types whose record types have the same normal form and whose indications regarding the inclusion of the null value are the same, then _BTNF_(_BTT1_)

\= _BTNF_(_BTT2_).

- 1. _BTNF_(_BTNF_(_BTT_)) = _BTNF_(_BTT_).
  2. The results of all invocations of _BTNF_(_BTT_) are the same.

NOTE 273 — This ensures that all invocations of the implementation-defined [(IV003)](#_bookmark6184) choice of the normal form of a binding table type from amongst the equivalent binding table types are

deterministic.

# General Rules

1. Let _BTT_ be the binding table type specified by [&lt;binding table type&gt;](#_bookmark2872).
2. A record data type descriptor for the record type _RT_ of _BTT_ is created that comprises:
    1. The base type name of all record types (RECORD DATA).
    2. The indication that _RT_ is closed.
    3. A field type descriptor for every [&lt;field type&gt;](#_bookmark3328) simply contained in [&lt;binding table type&gt;](#_bookmark2872), according to the Syntax Rules and General Rules of [Subclause 18.10, “](#_bookmark3327)[<field](#_bookmark3328) [type>”](#_bookmark3327), applied to the [&lt;field type&gt;](#_bookmark3328)s in the order in which they were specified.
    4. The indication that _RT_ excludes the null value.
3. A binding table data type descriptor is created that comprises:
    1. The base type name of all binding table types (BINDING TABLE DATA).
    2. The record data type descriptor _RT_.

# Conformance Rules

_None._

# Syntax Rules

1. Every [&lt;value type&gt;](#_bookmark2878) specifies the value type that is the data type specified by the immediately con- tained BNF non-terminal instance.
2. Every [&lt;predefined type&gt;](#_bookmark2883) specifies the data type specified by the immediately contained BNF non- terminal instance.
3. Every [&lt;reference value type&gt;](#_bookmark2974) specifies the reference value type that is the data type specified by the immediately contained [&lt;graph reference value type&gt;](#_bookmark2980), [&lt;binding table reference value type&gt;](#_bookmark2986),

[&lt;node reference value type&gt;](#_bookmark2988), or [&lt;edge reference value type&gt;](#_bookmark2994).

1. The nullability specified by a BNF non-terminal instance _NT_ that is a [&lt;value type&gt;](#_bookmark2878) but not a [<closed](#_bookmark3020) [d](#_bookmark3020)ynamic union type> is defined as follows.

Case:

- 1. If _NT_ contains [&lt;not null&gt;](#_bookmark3024) without an intervening instance of [&lt;value type&gt;](#_bookmark2878), then _NT_ specifies known not nullable.
  2. If _NT_ is NOTHING, then _NT_ specifies known not nullable.
  3. Otherwise, _NT_ specifies possibly nullable.

NOTE 274 — See [Subclause 4.17.4, “Nullability”](#_bookmark901).

1. Every [&lt;boolean type&gt;](#_bookmark2887) _BT_ specifies the _Boolean type_ with the nullability specified by _BT_.
2. For each Boolean type _BT_, there is an implementation-defined [(IV008)](#_bookmark6185) Boolean type _BNF_(_BT_), known as the _normal form_ of _BT_ (which can be _BT_ itself), such that:
    1. The nullability of _BNF_(_BT_) is the nullability of _BT_.
    2. The declared name of _BNF_(_BT_) is the preferred name of Boolean types.
    3. All invocations of _BNF_(_BT_) are the same.

NOTE 275 — This ensures that all invocations of the implementation-defined [(IV003)](#_bookmark6184) choice of

the normal form of a Boolean type from amongst the equivalent Boolean types are deterministic.

1. The value of every [&lt;max length&gt;](#_bookmark2899) shall be greater than or equal to 1 (one).
2. The value of every [&lt;min length&gt;](#_bookmark2897) shall be greater than or equal to 0 (zero).
3. If [&lt;min length&gt;](#_bookmark2897) is omitted, then a [&lt;min length&gt;](#_bookmark2897) of 0 (zero) is implicit.
4. The value of every [&lt;fixed length&gt;](#_bookmark2900) shall be greater than or equal to 1 (one).
5. If [&lt;fixed length&gt;](#_bookmark2900) is omitted, then a [&lt;fixed length&gt;](#_bookmark2900) of 1 (one) is implicit.
6. Every [&lt;character string type&gt;](#_bookmark2889) _CST_ specifies the _character string type_ with the nullability specified by _CST_.
7. If both [&lt;min length&gt;](#_bookmark2897) _MINL_ and [&lt;max length&gt;](#_bookmark2899) _MAXL_ are specified or implicit in a [<character string](#_bookmark2889) [type>](#_bookmark2889), then _MINL_ shall be less than or equal to _MAXL_.
8. If [&lt;min length&gt;](#_bookmark2897) _CSMINL_ is specified or implicit in a [&lt;character string type&gt;](#_bookmark2889) _CST_, then the minimum length of the character string type specified by _CST_ is the value of _CSMINL_.
9. If [&lt;max length&gt;](#_bookmark2899) _CSMAL_ is specified in a [&lt;character string type&gt;](#_bookmark2889) _CST_, then the maximum length of the character string type specified by _CST_ is the value of _CSMAXL_.

**18.9** [**&lt;value type&gt;**](#_bookmark2878)

1. If [&lt;fixed length&gt;](#_bookmark2900) _CSFIXL_ is specified or implicit in a [&lt;character string type&gt;](#_bookmark2889) _CST_, then the minimum length of the character string type specified by _CST_ is the value of _CSFIXL_ and the maximum length of the character string type specified by _CST_ is the value of _CSFIXL_.
2. If neither [&lt;max length&gt;](#_bookmark2899) nor [&lt;fixed length&gt;](#_bookmark2900) are specified or implicit in a [&lt;character string type&gt;](#_bookmark2889) _CST_, then the maximum length of the character string type specified by _CST_ is implementation- defined [(IL013)](#_bookmark6175) but shall be greater than or equal to 214−1 = 16383 characters.
3. For each character string type _CST_, there is an implementation-defined [(IV008)](#_bookmark6185) character string type _CSNF_(_CST_), known as the _normal form_ of _CST_ (which can be _CST_ itself), such that _CSNF_(_CST_) and _CST_ have the same minimum length and the same maximum length and the nullability of _CSNF_(_CST_) is the nullability of _CST_ and

Case:

- 1. If _CST_ is a fixed-length character string type, then:
        1. The declared name of _CSNF_(_CST_) is the preferred name of fixed-length character string types.
        2. All invocations of _CSNF_(_CST_) are the same.

NOTE 276 — This ensures that all invocations of the implementation-defined [(IV003)](#_bookmark6184) choice of the normal form of a fixed-length character string type from amongst the equivalent fixed-length character string types are deterministic.

- 1. If _CST_ is a variable-length character string type, then:
        1. The declared name of _CSNF_(_CST_) is the preferred name of variable-length character string types.
        2. All invocations of _CSNF_(_CST_) are the same.

NOTE 277 — This ensures that all invocations of the implementation-defined [(IV003)](#_bookmark6184) choice of the normal form of a variable-length character string type from amongst the equivalent variable-length character string types are deterministic.

1. The material values of a character string type with minimum length _CSMINL_ and maximum length _CSMAXL_ are the character strings whose length is both greater than or equal to _CSMINL_ and less than or equal to _CSMAXL_.
2. Every [&lt;byte string type&gt;](#_bookmark2893) _BST_ specifies the _byte string type_ with the nullability specified by _BST_.
3. If both [&lt;min length&gt;](#_bookmark2897) _MINL_ and [&lt;max length&gt;](#_bookmark2899) _MAXL_ are specified or implicit in a [&lt;byte string type&gt;](#_bookmark2893), then _MINL_ shall be less than or equal to _MAXL_.
4. If [&lt;min length&gt;](#_bookmark2897) _BSMINL_ is specified or implicit in a [&lt;byte string type&gt;](#_bookmark2893) _BST_, then the minimum length of the byte string type specified by _BST_ is the value of _BSMINL_.
5. If [&lt;max length&gt;](#_bookmark2899) _BSMAXL_ is specified in a [&lt;byte string type&gt;](#_bookmark2893) _BST_, then the maximum length of the byte string type specified by _BST_ is the value of _BSMAXL_.
6. If [&lt;fixed length&gt;](#_bookmark2900) _BSFIXL_ is specified or implicit in a [&lt;byte string type&gt;](#_bookmark2893) _BST_, then the minimum length of the byte string type specified by _BST_ is the value of _BSFIXL_ and the maximum length of the byte string type specified by _BST_ is the value of _BSFIXL_.
7. If neither [&lt;max length&gt;](#_bookmark2899) nor [&lt;fixed length&gt;](#_bookmark2900) are specified or implicit in a [&lt;byte string type&gt;](#_bookmark2893) _BST_, then the maximum length of the byte string type specified by _BST_ is implementation-defined [(IL013)](#_bookmark6175)

but shall be greater than or equal to 216-2 = 65534 bytes.

1. For each byte string type _BST_, there is an implementation-defined [(IV008)](#_bookmark6185) byte string type

_BSNF_(_BST_), known as the _normal form_ of _BST_ (which can be _BST_ itself), such that _BSNF_(_BST_) and

**18.9** [**&lt;value type&gt;**](#_bookmark2878)

_BST_ have the same minimum length and the same maximum length and the nullability of _BSNF_(_BST_) is the nullability of _BST_.

Case:

- 1. If _BST_ is a fixed-length byte string type, then:
        1. The declared name of _BSNF_(_BST_) is the preferred name of fixed-length byte string types.
        2. All invocations of _BSNF_(_BST_) are the same.

NOTE 278 — This ensures that all invocations of the implementation-defined [(IV003)](#_bookmark6184) choice of the normal form of a fixed-length byte string type from amongst the equivalent fixed-

length byte string types are deterministic.

- 1. If _BST_ is a variable-length byte string type, then:
        1. The declared name of _BSNF_(_BST_) is the preferred name of variable-length byte string types.
        2. All invocations of _BSNF_(_BST_) are the same.

NOTE 279 — This ensures that all invocations of the implementation-defined [(IV003)](#_bookmark6184) choice of the normal form of a variable-length byte string type from amongst the equivalent vari- able-length byte string types are deterministic.

1. The material values of a byte string type with minimum length _BSMINL_ and maximum length _BSMAXL_ are the byte strings whose length is both greater than or equal to _BSMINL_ and less than or equal to _BSMAXL_.
2. The minimum length of every byte string type _BST_ shall be less than or equal to the maximum length of _BST_.
3. The value of every [&lt;precision&gt;](#_bookmark2941) shall be greater than or equal to 1 (one).
4. Every [&lt;numeric type&gt;](#_bookmark2901) specifies the _numeric type_ specified by the immediately contained [<exact](#_bookmark2903) [numeric type>](#_bookmark2903) or the immediately contained [&lt;approximate numeric type&gt;](#_bookmark2944).
5. For each exact numeric type _ENT_, there is an implementation-defined [(IV008)](#_bookmark6185) exact numeric type,

NOTE 293 — This ensures that all invocations of the implementation-defined [(IV008)](#_bookmark6185) choice of the normal form of a record type from amongst the equivalent exact numeric types are deterministic.

1. Every [&lt;field types specification&gt;](#_bookmark3011) specifies the field types specified by the [&lt;field type list&gt;](#_bookmark3013) that it immediately contains.
2. Every [&lt;field type list&gt;](#_bookmark3013) specifies the field types that are specified by the [&lt;field type&gt;](#_bookmark3328)s that it imme- diately contains.
3. The maximum number of [&lt;field type&gt;](#_bookmark3328)s immediately contained in a [&lt;field type list&gt;](#_bookmark3013) is the implemen- tation-defined [(IL015)](#_bookmark6176) maximum number of record fields.
4. The preferred name of dynamic union types is ANY.

NOTE 294 — See [Subclause 4.3.4, “Properties and supported property value types”](#_bookmark199), for the definitions of supported property value type and dynamic property value type.

specified by _CDUT_.

2. The nullability specified by a [&lt;component type list&gt;](#_bookmark3021) _CTL_ is defined as follows. If every [&lt;value type&gt;](#_bookmark2878) simply contained in _CTL_ specifies known not nullable, then _CTL_ specifies known not nullable; oth- erwise, _CTL_ specifies possibly nullable.
3. If the [&lt;component type list&gt;](#_bookmark3021) _CTL_ is specified, then _CTL_ specifies the set of value types specified by at least one of the [&lt;value type&gt;](#_bookmark2878)s simply contained in _CTL_.
4. If a [&lt;component type list&gt;](#_bookmark3021) _CTL_ is specified, then either every [&lt;value type&gt;](#_bookmark2878) simply contained in _CTL_ shall specify possibly nullable or every [&lt;value type&gt;](#_bookmark2878) simply contained in _CTL_ shall specify known not nullable.

# General Rules

1. If [&lt;boolean type&gt;](#_bookmark2887) is specified, then a Boolean data type descriptor is created for the specified Boolean type _BT_ that describes _BT_ and comprises:
    1. The declared name of the primary base type of all Boolean types (BOOLEAN DATA).

NOTE 297 — See [Subclause 4.16.1, “Introduction to predefined value types and related base types”](#_bookmark684).

- 1. The preferred name of _BT_.

**18.9** [**&lt;value type&gt;**](#_bookmark2878)

- 1. The indication of whether _BT_ includes the null value as determined by the nullability specified by the [&lt;boolean type&gt;](#_bookmark2887).

1. If [&lt;character string type&gt;](#_bookmark2889) is specified, then a character string data type descriptor is created for the specified character string type _CST_ that describes _CST_ and comprises:
    1. The declared name of the primary base type of all character string types (STRING DATA).

NOTE 298 — See [Subclause 4.16.1, “Introduction to predefined value types and related base types”](#_bookmark684).

- 1. The preferred name of _CST_.
  2. The minimum length in characters of _CST_.
  3. The maximum length in characters of _CST_.
  4. The indication that _CST_ includes the null value as determined by the nullability specified by the [&lt;character string type&gt;](#_bookmark2889).

1. If [&lt;byte string type&gt;](#_bookmark2893) is specified, then a byte string data type descriptor is created for the specified byte string type _BST_ that describes _BST_ and comprises:
    1. The declared name of the primary base type of all byte string types (BINARY DATA).

NOTE 299 — See [Subclause 4.16.1, “Introduction to predefined value types and related base types”](#_bookmark684).

- 1. The preferred name of _BST_.
  2. The minimum length in bytes of _BST_.
  3. The maximum length in bytes of _BST_.
  4. The indication of whether _BST_ includes the null value as determined by the nullability specified by the [&lt;byte string type&gt;](#_bookmark2893).

1. If [&lt;exact numeric type&gt;](#_bookmark2903) is specified, then a numeric data type descriptor is created for the specified exact numeric type _ENT_ that describes _ENT_ and comprises:
    1. The declared name of the primary base type of _ENT_ (EXACT NUMERIC DATA).

NOTE 300 — See [Subclause 4.16.1, “Introduction to predefined value types and related base types”](#_bookmark684).

- 1. The preferred name of _ENT_, which is the declared name of the normal form of _ENT_.
  2. The indication of whether exact numbers of _ENT_ are specified in binary or decimal terms.
  3. The precision of _ENT_.
  4. The scale of _ENT_.
  5. The indication of whether _ENT_ includes the null value as determined by the nullability specified by the [&lt;exact numeric type&gt;](#_bookmark2903).

1. If [&lt;approximate numeric type&gt;](#_bookmark2944) is specified, then a numeric data type descriptor is created for the specified approximate numeric type _ANT_ that describes _ANT_ and comprises:
    1. The declared name of the primary base type of _ANT_ (FLOAT NUMERIC DATA).

NOTE 301 — See [Subclause 4.16.1, “Introduction to predefined value types and related base types”](#_bookmark684).

- 1. The preferred name of _ANT_, which is the declared name of the normal form of _ANT_.
  2. The indication that approximate numbers of _ANT_ are specified in binary terms.
  3. The precision of _ANT_.

**18.9** [**&lt;value type&gt;**](#_bookmark2878)

- 1. The scale of _ANT_.
  2. The indication of whether _ANT_ includes the null value as determined by the nullability specified by the [&lt;approximate numeric type&gt;](#_bookmark2944).

1. If [&lt;temporal instant type&gt;](#_bookmark2955) is specified, then a temporal instant data type descriptor is created for the specified temporal instant type _TINT_ that describes _TINT_ and comprises:
    1. The declared name of the primary base type of all temporal instant types (TEMPORAL INSTANT DATA).

NOTE 302 — See [Subclause 4.16.1, “Introduction to predefined value types and related base types”](#_bookmark684).

- 1. The preferred name of _TINT_, which is the declared name of the normal form of _TINT_.
  2. The indication of whether values of _TINT_ capture the date.
  3. The indication of whether values of _TINT_ capture the time of day.
  4. The indication of whether values of _TINT_ include a time zone displacement.
  5. The indication of whether _TINT_ includes the null value as determined by the nullability specified by the [&lt;temporal instant type&gt;](#_bookmark2955).

1. If [&lt;temporal duration type&gt;](#_bookmark2969) is specified, then a temporal duration data type descriptor is created for the specified temporal duration type _TDURT_ that describes _TDURT_ and comprises:
    1. The declared name of the primary base type of all temporal duration types (TEMPORAL DURATION DATA).

NOTE 303 — See [Subclause 4.16.1, “Introduction to predefined value types and related base types”](#_bookmark684).

- 1. The temporal duration unit group of temporal durations of _TDURT_ as specified by the [<temporal](#_bookmark2971) [duration qualifier>](#_bookmark2971) simply contained in the [&lt;temporal duration type&gt;](#_bookmark2969).
  2. The indication of whether _TDURT_ includes the null value as determined by the nullability specified by the [&lt;temporal duration type&gt;](#_bookmark2969).

1. If [&lt;open graph reference value type&gt;](#_bookmark2984) is specified, then a graph reference value data type descriptor is created for the specified open graph reference value type _OGRVT_ that describes _OGRVT_ and

comprises:

  2. The object base type name of graph types (GRAPH DATA).

    1. The reference base type name of graph reference value types (GRAPH REFERENCE).
    2. The object base type name of graph types (GRAPH DATA).
    3. The preferred name, which is the preferred name of graph types.
    4. The specified constraining GQL-object type.

**18.9** [**&lt;value type&gt;**](#_bookmark2878)

- 1. The indication of whether _CGRVT_ includes the null value as determined by the nullability specified by the [&lt;closed graph reference value type&gt;](#_bookmark2982).

    1. The reference base type name of binding table reference value types (BINDING TABLE REF- ERENCE).
    2. The object base type name of binding table types (BINDING TABLE DATA).
    3. The preferred name, which is the preferred name of binding table types.

    1. The reference base type name, which is the implementation-defined [(ID090)](#_bookmark6151) preferred name of the base type of node reference value types (NODE REFERENCE or VERTEX REFERENCE).
    2. The object base type name, which is the implementation-defined [(ID090)](#_bookmark6151) preferred name of the base type of node types (NODE DATA or VERTEX DATA).
    3. The preferred name, which is the preferred name of node types.
    4. No constraining GQL-object type.
    5. The indication of whether _ONRVT_ includes the null value as determined by the nullability specified by the [&lt;open node reference value type&gt;](#_bookmark2992).
3. If [&lt;closed node reference value type&gt;](#_bookmark2990) is specified, then a node reference value data type descriptor is created for the specified closed node reference value type _CNRVT_ that describes _CNRVT_ and

comprises:

- 1. The reference base type name, which is the implementation-defined [(ID090)](#_bookmark6151) preferred name of the base type of node reference value types (NODE REFERENCE or VERTEX REFERENCE).
  2. The object base type name, which is the implementation-defined [(ID090)](#_bookmark6151) preferred name of the base type of node types (NODE DATA or VERTEX DATA).
  3. The preferred name, which is the preferred name of node types.
  4. The specified constraining GQL-object type.
  5. The indication of whether _CNRVT_ includes the null value as determined by the nullability specified by the [&lt;closed node reference value type&gt;](#_bookmark2990).

1. If [&lt;open edge reference value type&gt;](#_bookmark2997) is specified, then an edge reference value data type descriptor is created for the specified open edge reference value type _OERVT_ that describes _OERVT_ and com- prises:
    1. The reference base type name, which is the implementation-defined [(ID091)](#_bookmark6152) preferred name of the base type of edge reference value types (EDGE REFERENCE or RELATIONSHIP REFER- ENCE).

**18.9** [**&lt;value type&gt;**](#_bookmark2878)

- 1. The object base type name, which is the implementation-defined [(ID091)](#_bookmark6152) preferred name of the base type of edge types (EDGE DATA or RELATIONSHIP DATA).
  2. The preferred name, which is the preferred name of edge types.
  3. No constraining GQL-object type.
  4. The indication of whether _OERVT_ includes the null value as determined by the nullability specified by the [&lt;open edge reference value type&gt;](#_bookmark2997).

    1. The reference base type name, which is the implementation-defined [(ID091)](#_bookmark6152) preferred name of the base type of edge reference value types (EDGE REFERENCE or RELATIONSHIP REFER- ENCE).
    2. The object base type name, which is the implementation-defined [(ID091)](#_bookmark6152) preferred name of the base type of edge types (EDGE DATA or RELATIONSHIP DATA).
    3. The preferred name, which is the preferred name of edge types.
    4. The specified constraining GQL-object type.

    1. The declared name of the primary base type of all immaterial value types (NULL DATA).
    2. The preferred name of _IVT_.
    3. The indication of whether _IVT_ includes the null value as determined by the nullability specified by the [&lt;immaterial value type&gt;](#_bookmark2976).
3. If [&lt;path value type&gt;](#_bookmark3000) is specified, then let _PVT_ be the specified path value type and a path value data type descriptor is created for _PVT_ that describes _PVT_ and comprises:
    1. The declared name of the primary base type of all path value types (PATH VALUE DATA).

NOTE 304 — See [Subclause 4.15.1, “Introduction to constructed value types and related base types”](#_bookmark643).

- 1. The indication of whether _PVT_ includes the null value as determined by the nullability specified by the [&lt;path value type&gt;](#_bookmark3000).

1. If [&lt;list value type&gt;](#_bookmark3002) is specified, then a list value data type descriptor is created for _LVT_ that describes

_LVT_ and comprises:

- 1. The base type name of all list value types (LIST VALUE DATA).
  2. The preferred name _LNF_(_LVT_), which is the declared name of the normal form of the list value type.
  3. The specified list element type (_LET_).
  4. The specified group characteristic of the list value type.
  5. The specified maximum cardinality of the list value type.
  6. The indication of whether _LVT_ includes the null value as determined by the nullability specified by the [&lt;list value type&gt;](#_bookmark3002).

**18.9** [**&lt;value type&gt;**](#_bookmark2878)

1. If the specified list element type of a list value type _LVT_ is an open dynamic union type, then _LVT_ is open; otherwise, _LVT_ is closed.
2. If [&lt;record type&gt;](#_bookmark3009) is specified, then let _RT_ be the specified record type. Case:
    1. If _RT_ is a closed record type, then a record data type descriptor is created for _RT_ that describes

_RT_ and comprises:

- - 1. The base type name of all record types (RECORD DATA).
        2.  The indication that _RT_ is closed.
        3.  A field type descriptor for every [&lt;field type&gt;](#_bookmark3328) simply contained in the [&lt;record type&gt;](#_bookmark3009), according to the Syntax Rules and General Rules of [Subclause 18.10, “](#_bookmark3327)[<field](#_bookmark3328) [type>”](#_bookmark3327), applied to the [&lt;field type&gt;](#_bookmark3328)s in the order in which they were specified.
        4.  The indication of whether _RT_ includes the null value as determined by the nullability specified by the [&lt;record type&gt;](#_bookmark3009).

    1. Otherwise, _RT_ is the open record type and a record data type descriptor is created for _RT_ that describes _RT_ and comprises:
        1. The base type name of all record types (RECORD DATA).
        2. The indication that _RT_ is open.
        3. The indication of whether _RT_ includes the null value as determined by the nullability specified by the [&lt;record type&gt;](#_bookmark3009).

1. If [&lt;dynamic union type&gt;](#_bookmark3015) is specified, then let _DUT_ be the specified dynamic union type and a dynamic union data type descriptor is created for _DUT_ that describes _DUT_ and comprises:
    1. The declared name of the primary base type of all dynamic union types, which is the dynamic base type of all value types (ANY DATA).

NOTE 305 — See [Subclause 4.14.1, “Introduction to dynamic union types and the dynamic base](#_bookmark599) [type”](#_bookmark599).

- 1. The preferred name of _DUT_, which is the declared name of the normal form of _DUT_.
  2. The indication of whether _DUT_ is open or closed as determined by the [&lt;dynamic union type&gt;](#_bookmark3015).
  3. The component types of _DUT_ are defined as follows. Case:
        1. If _DUT_ specifies a closed dynamic union type, then the component types of _DUT_ are given by the set of all data types specified by the [&lt;component type list&gt;](#_bookmark3021) simply contained in the [&lt;dynamic union type&gt;](#_bookmark3015).
        2. Otherwise, _DUT_ specifies an open dynamic union type.
            1. Let _COMPTYPES_ be an implementation-defined [(IV014)](#_bookmark6189) set of nullable value types that includes at least one supertype of every static value type supported by the GQL-implementation.
            2. If the [&lt;dynamic union type&gt;](#_bookmark3015) specifies possibly nullable, then the component types of _DUT_ are _COMPTYPES_; otherwise, the component types of _DUT_ are given by the set of all material variants of value types from _COMPTYPES_.

**18.9** [**&lt;value type&gt;**](#_bookmark2878)

- 1. The indication of whether _DUT_ includes the null value as determined by the nullability specified by the [&lt;dynamic union type&gt;](#_bookmark3015).

1. A dynamic union type _DUT_ includes every material value of one of its component types _DUT_. If _DUT_

is nullable, then it additionally includes the null value. No other values are included in _DUT_.

# Conformance Rules

1. Conforming GQL language shall not specify a [&lt;list value type name&gt;](#_bookmark3005) that contains GROUP.

NOTE 306 — A [&lt;list value type name&gt;](#_bookmark3005) that contains GROUP is a specification device to indicate the group characteristic of a list value type in the syntactic representation of the type and is not syntax available to the user.

1. Without Feature GV02, “8 bit signed integer numbers”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [&lt;signed binary exact numeric type&gt;](#_bookmark2908) that contains SIGNED INTEGER8, INTEGER8, or INT8.
2. Without Feature GV18, “Small signed integer numbers”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [&lt;signed binary exact numeric type&gt;](#_bookmark2908) that contains SMALLINT.
3. Without Feature GV19, “Big signed integer numbers”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [&lt;signed binary exact numeric type&gt;](#_bookmark2908) that contains BIGINT.
4. Without Feature GV04, “16 bit signed integer numbers”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [&lt;signed binary exact numeric type&gt;](#_bookmark2908) that contains SIGNED INTEGER16, INTEGER16, or INT16.
5. Without Feature GV07, “32 bit signed integer numbers”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [&lt;signed binary exact numeric type&gt;](#_bookmark2908) that contains SIGNED INTEGER32, INTEGER32, or INT32.
6. Without Feature GV12, “64 bit signed integer numbers”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [&lt;signed binary exact numeric type&gt;](#_bookmark2908) that contains SIGNED INTEGER64, INTEGER64, or INT64.
7. Without Feature GV14, “128 bit signed integer numbers”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [&lt;signed binary exact numeric type&gt;](#_bookmark2908) that contains INT128, INTEGER128, or SIGNED INTEGER128.
8. Without Feature GV16, “256 bit signed integer numbers”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [&lt;signed binary exact numeric type&gt;](#_bookmark2908) that contains INT256, INTEGER256, or SIGNED INTEGER256.
9. Without Feature GV01, “8 bit unsigned integer numbers”, conforming GQL language shall not contain an [&lt;unsigned binary exact numeric type&gt;](#_bookmark2919) that contains UNSIGNED INTEGER8 or UINT8.
10. Without Feature GV03, “16 bit unsigned integer numbers”, conforming GQL language shall not contain an [&lt;unsigned binary exact numeric type&gt;](#_bookmark2919) that contains UNSIGNED INTEGER16 or UINT16.
11. Without Feature GV06, “32 bit unsigned integer numbers”, conforming GQL language shall not contain an [&lt;unsigned binary exact numeric type&gt;](#_bookmark2919) that contains UNSIGNED INTEGER32 or UINT32.
12. Without Feature GV11, “64 bit unsigned integer numbers”, conforming GQL language shall not contain an [&lt;unsigned binary exact numeric type&gt;](#_bookmark2919) that contains UNSIGNED INTEGER64 or UINT64.
13. Without Feature GV05, “Small unsigned integer numbers”, conforming GQL language shall not contain an [&lt;unsigned binary exact numeric type&gt;](#_bookmark2919) that contains USMALLINT.
14. Without Feature GV08, “Regular unsigned integer numbers”, conforming GQL language shall not contain an [&lt;unsigned binary exact numeric type&gt;](#_bookmark2919) that contains UINT.
15. Without Feature GV10, “Big unsigned integer numbers”, conforming GQL language shall not contain an [&lt;unsigned binary exact numeric type&gt;](#_bookmark2919) that contains UBIGINT.
16. Without Feature GV09, “Specified integer number precision”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [&lt;signed binary exact numeric type&gt;](#_bookmark2908) that contains a [&lt;precision&gt;](#_bookmark2941) or a [&lt;scale&gt;](#_bookmark2943).
    1. [**&lt;value type&gt;**](#_bookmark2878)
17. Without Feature GV13, “128 bit unsigned integer numbers”, conforming GQL language shall not contain an [&lt;unsigned binary exact numeric type&gt;](#_bookmark2919) that contains UINT128, or UNSIGNED INTEGER128.
18. Without Feature GV15, “256 bit unsigned integer numbers”, conforming GQL language shall not contain an [&lt;unsigned binary exact numeric type&gt;](#_bookmark2919) that contains UINT256, or UNSIGNED INTEGER256.
19. Without Feature GV20, “16 bit floating point numbers”, conforming GQL language shall not contain an [&lt;approximate numeric type&gt;](#_bookmark2944) that contains FLOAT16.
20. Without Feature GV21, “32 bit floating point numbers”, conforming GQL language shall not contain an [&lt;approximate numeric type&gt;](#_bookmark2944) that contains FLOAT32.
21. Without Feature GV24, “64 bit floating point numbers”, conforming GQL language shall not contain an [&lt;approximate numeric type&gt;](#_bookmark2944) that contains FLOAT64.
22. Without Feature GV25, “128 bit floating point numbers”, conforming GQL language shall not contain an [&lt;approximate numeric type&gt;](#_bookmark2944) that contains FLOAT128.
23. Without Feature GV26, “256 bit floating point numbers”, conforming GQL language shall not contain an [&lt;approximate numeric type&gt;](#_bookmark2944) that contains FLOAT256.

# [&lt;field type&gt;](#_bookmark3328) Function

Specify a field type.

# Format

&lt;field type&gt; ::=

[&lt;field name&gt;](#_bookmark4437) \[ [&lt;typed&gt;](#_bookmark2881) \] [&lt;value type&gt;](#_bookmark2878)

# Syntax Rules

1. Let _FTL_ be the [&lt;field type list&gt;](#_bookmark3013) that simply contains the [&lt;field type&gt;](#_bookmark3328) _FT_.
2. The [&lt;field name&gt;](#_bookmark4437) shall not be equivalent to the [&lt;field name&gt;](#_bookmark4437) of any other [&lt;field type&gt;](#_bookmark3328) simply con- tained in _FTL_.
3. The _name_ of _FT_ is the name specified by the [&lt;field name&gt;](#_bookmark4437) simply contained in _FT_.
4. The _value type_ of _FT_ is the value type specified by the [&lt;value type&gt;](#_bookmark2878) simply contained in _FT_.

# General Rules

1. A data type descriptor is created that describes the value type of the field type being defined.
2. A field type descriptor is created that describes the field type being defined. The field type descriptor includes the following:
    1. The name of the field type.
    2. The value type of the field type.

# Conformance Rules

1) Without Feature GV48, “Nested record types”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [<field](#_bookmark3328) [type>](#_bookmark3328) that simply contains a [&lt;record type&gt;](#_bookmark3009).

**Function**
