# Format

&lt;search condition&gt; ::=

[&lt;boolean value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3934)

# Syntax Rules

_None._

# General Rules

1. The result of the [&lt;search condition&gt;](#_bookmark3337) is the result of the [&lt;boolean value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3934).
2. A [&lt;search condition&gt;](#_bookmark3337) is said to be _satisfied_ if and only if the result of the [&lt;boolean value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3934) is _True_.

# Conformance Rules

_None._

- 1. [**&lt;exists predicate&gt;**](#_bookmark3394)

# [&lt;exists predicate&gt;](#_bookmark3394) Function

Specify an existential subquery.

# Format

&lt;exists predicate&gt; ::= EXISTS {

[&lt;left brace&gt;](#_bookmark5030) [&lt;graph pattern&gt;](#_bookmark1977) [&lt;right brace&gt;](#_bookmark5041)

| [&lt;left paren&gt;](#_bookmark5032) [&lt;graph pattern&gt;](#_bookmark1977) [&lt;right paren&gt;](#_bookmark5043)

| [&lt;left brace&gt;](#_bookmark5030) [&lt;match statement block&gt;](#_bookmark1614) [&lt;right brace&gt;](#_bookmark5041)

| [&lt;left paren&gt;](#_bookmark5032) [&lt;match statement block&gt;](#_bookmark1614) [&lt;right paren&gt;](#_bookmark5043)

| [&lt;nested query specification&gt;](#_bookmark1123)

}

# Syntax Rules

1. Let _EP_ be the [&lt;exists predicate&gt;](#_bookmark3394).
2. If _EP_ immediately contains the [&lt;graph pattern&gt;](#_bookmark1977) _GP_, then:
    1. Let _RIA_ be a new system-generated identifier.
    2. _EP_ is effectively replaced by:

EXISTS { MATCH _GP_ RETURN TRUE AS _RIA_ }

1. If _EP_ immediately contains the [&lt;match statement block&gt;](#_bookmark1614) _MSB_, then:
    1. Let _RIA2_ be a new system-generated identifier.
    2. _EP_ is effectively replaced by:

EXISTS { _MSB_ RETURN TRUE AS _RIA2_ }

1. Let _NQS_ be the [&lt;nested query specification&gt;](#_bookmark1123) immediately contained in _EP_.
2. The declared type of _NQS_ shall be a binding table type.

# General Rules

1. In a new child execution context:
    1. The General Rules of _NQS_ are applied.
    2. If the current execution result is a non-empty table, then the result of _EP_ is _True_; otherwise, the result of _EP_ is _False_.

# Conformance Rules

1) Without Feature GQ22, “EXISTS predicate: multiple MATCH statements”, in conforming GQL language, an [&lt;exists predicate&gt;](#_bookmark3394) shall not directly contain a [&lt;match statement block&gt;](#_bookmark1614)

# [&lt;null predicate&gt;](#_bookmark3403) Function

Specify a test for a null value.

# Format

&lt;null predicate&gt; ::=

[&lt;value expression primary&gt;](#_bookmark3507) [&lt;null predicate part 2&gt;](#_bookmark3405)

&lt;null predicate part 2&gt; ::= IS \[ NOT \] NULL

# Syntax Rules

_None._

# General Rules

1. Let _VEP_ be the [&lt;value expression primary&gt;](#_bookmark3507).
2. Let _VEPR_ be the result of _VEP_.
3. Case:
    1. If _VEPR_ is the null value, then “_VEP_ IS NULL” is _True_ and the result of “_VEP_ IS NOT NULL” is

_False_.

- 1. Otherwise, “_VEP_ IS NULL” is _False_ and the result of “_VEP_ IS NOT NULL” is _True_.

# Conformance Rules

_None._

&lt;value type predicate part 2&gt; ::= IS \[ NOT \] [&lt;typed&gt;](#_bookmark2881) [&lt;value type&gt;](#_bookmark2878)

# Syntax Rules

1. Let _VTP_ be the [&lt;value type predicate&gt;](#_bookmark3408).
2. Let _VE_ be the [&lt;value expression primary&gt;](#_bookmark3507) simply contained in _VTP_, and let _VT_ be the [&lt;value type&gt;](#_bookmark2878) simply contained in _VTP_.
3. The declared type of _VTP_ is the Boolean type.

# General Rules

1. Let _VALUE_ be the result of _VE_ and let _TYPE_ be the value type specified by _VT_.
2. The result of _VTP_ is defined as follows. Case:
    1. If _VALUE_ is of _TYPE_ and NOT is not specified, then the result of _VTP_ is _True_.
    2. If _VALUE_ is not of _TYPE_ and NOT is specified, then the result of _VTP_ is _True_.
    3. Otherwise, the result of _VTP_ is _False_.

# Conformance Rules

1) Without Feature GA06, “Value type predicate”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [<value](#_bookmark3408) [type predicate>](#_bookmark3408) or a [&lt;value type predicate part 2&gt;](#_bookmark3410).

# [&lt;normalized predicate&gt;](#_bookmark3414) Function

Determine whether a character string value is normalized.

# Format

&lt;normalized predicate&gt; ::=

[&lt;string value expression&gt;](#_bookmark4133) [&lt;normalized predicate part 2&gt;](#_bookmark3416)

&lt;normalized predicate part 2&gt; ::=

IS \[ NOT \] \[ [&lt;normal form&gt;](#_bookmark4184) \] NORMALIZED

# Syntax Rules

1. Let [&lt;string value expression&gt;](#_bookmark4133) be _SVE_.
2. Case:
    1. If [&lt;normal form&gt;](#_bookmark4184) is specified, then let _NF_ be [&lt;normal form&gt;](#_bookmark4184).
    2. Otherwise, let _NF_ be NFC.
3. The expression

_SVE_ IS NOT _NF_ NORMALIZED

is equivalent to:

NOT ( _SVE_ IS _NF_ NORMALIZED )

# General Rules

1. The result of _SVE_ IS _NF_ NORMALIZED is Case:
    1. If the result of _SVE_ is the null value, then _Unknown_.
    2. If the result of _SVE_ is in the normalization form specified by _NF_, in accordance with [Unicode](#_bookmark12) [Standard Annex #15](#_bookmark12), then _True_.
    3. Otherwise, _False_.

# Conformance Rules

_None._

# [&lt;directed predicate&gt;](#_bookmark3420) Function

Determine whether an edge variable is bound to a directed edge.

&lt;directed predicate&gt; ::=

[&lt;element variable reference&gt;](#_bookmark2381) [&lt;directed predicate part 2&gt;](#_bookmark3422)

&lt;directed predicate part 2&gt; ::= IS \[ NOT \] DIRECTED

# Syntax Rules

1. Let _DP_ be the [&lt;directed predicate&gt;](#_bookmark3420).
2. Let _EVR_ be the [&lt;element variable reference&gt;](#_bookmark2381) simply contained in _DP_. _EVR_ shall have singleton degree of reference.
3. The declared type of _EVR_ shall be an edge reference value type.
4. If NOT is specified, then the [&lt;directed predicate&gt;](#_bookmark3420) is equivalent to:

NOT ( _EVR_ IS DIRECTED )

# General Rules

1. Let _GE_ be the result of _EVR_.
2. The result of _DP_ is defined as follows. Case:
    1. If _GE_ is the null value, then the result of _DP_ is _Unknown_.
    2. If _GE_ is a reference value whose referent is a directed edge, then the result of _DP_ is _True_.
    3. Otherwise, _GE_ is a reference value whose referent is an undirected edge and the result of _DP_

is _False_.

# Conformance Rules

1) Without Feature G110, “IS DIRECTED predicate”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a

[&lt;directed predicate&gt;](#_bookmark3420) or a [&lt;directed predicate part 2&gt;](#_bookmark3422).

&lt;labeled predicate&gt; ::=

[&lt;is labeled or colon&gt;](#_bookmark3430) [&lt;label expression&gt;](#_bookmark2355)

&lt;is labeled or colon&gt; ::= IS \[ NOT \] LABELED

3. Let _LE_ be the [&lt;label expression&gt;](#_bookmark2355) simply contained in _LP_.
4. If NOT is specified, then _LP_ is effectively replaced by:

NOT ( _EVR_ IS LABELED _LE_ )

1. If _LP_ simply contains an [&lt;is labeled or colon&gt;](#_bookmark3430) _ILOC_ that is [&lt;colon&gt;](#_bookmark5021), then _ILOC_ is effectively replaced by IS LABELED.

# General Rules

1. Let _GE_ be the result of _EVR_.
2. The result of _LP_ is defined as follows. Case:

- 1. [**&lt;source/destination predicate&gt;**](#_bookmark3436)

# [&lt;source/destination predicate&gt;](#_bookmark3436) Function

Determine whether a node is the source or destination of an edge.

# Format

&lt;source/destination predicate&gt; ::=

[&lt;node reference&gt;](#_bookmark3437) [&lt;source predicate part 2&gt;](#_bookmark3439)

| [&lt;node reference&gt;](#_bookmark3437) [&lt;destination predicate part 2&gt;](#_bookmark3441)

&lt;node reference&gt; ::=

[&lt;element variable reference&gt;](#_bookmark2381)

&lt;source predicate part 2&gt; ::=

IS \[ NOT \] SOURCE OF [&lt;edge reference&gt;](#_bookmark3443)

&lt;destination predicate part 2&gt; ::=

IS \[ NOT \] DESTINATION OF [&lt;edge reference&gt;](#_bookmark3443)

&lt;edge reference&gt; ::=

[&lt;element variable reference&gt;](#_bookmark2381)

# Syntax Rules

1. Let _SDP_ be the [&lt;source/destination predicate&gt;](#_bookmark3436).
2. Let _NR_ be the [&lt;element variable reference&gt;](#_bookmark2381) immediately contained in the [&lt;node reference&gt;](#_bookmark3437) simply contained in _SDP_. _NR_ shall have singleton degree of reference. The declared type of _NR_ shall be a node reference value type.
3. Let _ER_ be the [&lt;element variable reference&gt;](#_bookmark2381) immediately contained in the [&lt;edge reference&gt;](#_bookmark3443) simply contained in _SDP_. _ER_ shall have singleton degree of reference. The declared type of _ER_ shall be an edge reference value type.
4. Let _SOD_ be the keyword SOURCE or DESTINATION simply contained in the [<source/destination](#_bookmark3436) [predicate>](#_bookmark3436).
5. If NOT is specified, then the [&lt;source/destination predicate&gt;](#_bookmark3436) is equivalent to:

NOT ( _NR_ IS _SOD_ OF _ER_ )

# General Rules

1. Let _GEN_ be the result of _NR_ and let _GEE_ be the result of _ER_.
2. The result of _SDP_ is defined as follows. Case:
    1. If _GEN_ is the null value or _GEE_ is the null value, then the result of _SDP_ is _Unknown_.
    2. If the referent of _GEE_ is an undirected edge, then the result of _SDP_ is _False_.
    3. If _SOD_ is SOURCE and the referent of _GEN_ is the source node of the referent of _GEE_, then the result of _SDP_ is _True_.
    4. [**&lt;source/destination predicate&gt;**](#_bookmark3436)
    5. If _SOD_ is DESTINATION and the referent of _GEN_ is the destination node of the referent of _GEE_, then the result of _SDP_ is _True_.
    6. Otherwise, the result of _SDP_ is _False_.

# Conformance Rules

1) Without Feature G112, “IS SOURCE and IS DESTINATION predicate”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [&lt;source/destination predicate&gt;](#_bookmark3436), a [&lt;source predicate part 2&gt;](#_bookmark3439), or a [<destination](#_bookmark3441) [predicate part 2>](#_bookmark3441).

# [&lt;all_different predicate&gt;](#_bookmark3448) Function

Determine whether all graph elements bound to a list of element references are pairwise different from one another.

# Format

&lt;all_different predicate&gt; ::= ALL_DIFFERENT [&lt;left paren&gt;](#_bookmark5032)

[&lt;element variable reference&gt;](#_bookmark2381) [&lt;comma&gt;](#_bookmark5022) [&lt;element variable reference&gt;](#_bookmark2381) \[ { [&lt;comma&gt;](#_bookmark5022) [&lt;element variable reference&gt;](#_bookmark2381) }... \]

[&lt;right paren&gt;](#_bookmark5043)

# Syntax Rules

1. Let _ADP_ be the [&lt;all_different predicate&gt;](#_bookmark3448).
2. Every [&lt;element variable reference&gt;](#_bookmark2381) simply contained in _ADP_ shall have singleton degree of reference.

# General Rules

1. Let _N_ be the number of [&lt;element variable reference&gt;](#_bookmark2381)s simply contained in _ADP_, let _EVR_1, ..., _EVRN_ be an enumeration of those [&lt;element variable reference&gt;](#_bookmark2381)s, and for every _i_, 1 (one) ≤ _i_ ≤ _N_, let _GEi_ be the result of _EVRi_.
2. The result of _ADP_ is defined as follows. Case:
    1. If there exists _i_, 1 (one) ≤ _i_ ≤ _N_, such that _GEi_ is the null value, then an exception condition is

raised: _data exception — null value not allowed (22004)_.

- 1. If there exists _i_, 1 (one) ≤ _i_ < _N_, and _j_, _i_ < _j_ ≤ _N_ such that _GEi_ and _GEj_ are not comparable values, then an exception condition is raised: _data exception — values not comparable (22G04)_.
  2. If there exist _j_ and _k_, 1 (one) ≤ _j_ < _k_ ≤ _N_, such that _GEj_ and _GEk_ reference the same graph element, then the result of _ADP_ is _False_.
  3. Otherwise, the result of _ADP_ is _True_.

# Conformance Rules

1) Without Feature G113, “ALL_DIFFERENT predicate”, conforming GQL language shall not contain an [&lt;all_different predicate&gt;](#_bookmark3448).

2. Every [&lt;element variable reference&gt;](#_bookmark2381) simply contained in _SDP_ shall have singleton degree of reference.

# General Rules

1. Let _N_ be the number of [&lt;element variable reference&gt;](#_bookmark2381)s simply contained in _SDP_, let _EVR_1, ..., _EVRN_ be an enumeration of those [&lt;element variable reference&gt;](#_bookmark2381)s, and for every _i_, 1 (one) ≤ _i_ ≤ _N_, let _GEi_ be the result of _EVRi_.
2. The result of _SDP_ is defined as follows. Case:

  2. If every _GEi_, 1 (one) ≤ _i_ ≤ _N_, references the same graph element, then the result of _SDP_ is _True_.

NOTE 310 — A record type with a field type whose value type is the empty type is unconstructable, i.e., comprises no records. Hence, a binding table whose declared type is a binding table type with such a record type has no records. The exception regarding [&lt;return item&gt;](#_bookmark1729)s stated by this Syntax Rules enables renaming of columns of such binding tables since iteration is guaranteed to not occur in a [<select state-](#_bookmark1758) [ment>](#_bookmark1758) or a [&lt;return statement&gt;](#_bookmark1722) based on this reasoning.

_None._

# General Rules

1. A [&lt;value specification&gt;](#_bookmark3529), [&lt;unsigned value specification&gt;](#_bookmark3531), or [&lt;non-negative integer specification&gt;](#_bookmark3533) specifies a value that is not matched from a graph or selected from a binding table.

_data exception — invalid value type (22G03)_.

# [&lt;let value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3551) Function

# Syntax Rules

1. Let _LVE_ be the [&lt;let value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3551) and let _WRT_ be the declared type of the incoming working record of _LVE_.
2. Let _LVDL_ be the [&lt;let variable definition list&gt;](#_bookmark1645). Let _N_ be the number of elements of _LVDL_. For _i_, 1 (one)

≤ _i_ ≤ _N_, let _LVDi_ be the _i_\-th element of _LVDL_.

1. For _i_, 1 (one) ≤ _i_ ≤ _N_:
    1. Let _FNi_ be the name specified by the [&lt;binding variable&gt;](#_bookmark4447) contained in _LVDi_ without an inter- vening instance of [&lt;value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3470).
    2. _FNi_ shall not identify a field type of _WRT_.
    3. Let _FEi_ be the [&lt;value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3470) simply contained in _LVDi_.
2. For all pairs of _i_, _j_ such that 1 (one) ≤ _i_ < _j_ ≤ _N_: _FNi_ shall not be equal to _FNj_.
3. Let _NRT_ be a record types whose field types are defined as follows. For _i_, 1 (one) ≤ _i_ ≤ _N_, the field type whose name is _FNi_ and whose value type is the declared type of _FEi_ is included in _NRT_.
4. Let _RHS_ be the [&lt;value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3470) immediately contained in _LVE_.
5. The declared type of the incoming working record of _RHS_ is _WRT_ amended with _NRT_.
6. The declared type of _LVE_ is the declared type of _RHS_.

# General Rules

1. Let _NR_ be a record whose fields are defined as follows. For _i_, 1 (one) ≤ _i_ ≤ _N_, the field whose name is _FNi_ and whose value type is the result of _FEi_ is included in _NR_.
2. In a new child execution context amended with _NR_, let _RESULT_ be the result of _RHS_.
3. The result of _LVE_ is _RESULT_.

# Conformance Rules

1. Without Feature GE03, “Let-binding of variables in expressions”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [&lt;let value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3551).
    1. [**&lt;value query expression&gt;**](#_bookmark3557)

# [&lt;value query expression&gt;](#_bookmark3557) Function

Specify a scalar value derived from a [&lt;nested query specification&gt;](#_bookmark1123).

# Format

&lt;value query expression&gt; ::=

VALUE [&lt;nested query specification&gt;](#_bookmark1123)

# Syntax Rules

1. Let _VQE_ be the [&lt;value query expression&gt;](#_bookmark3557).
2. Let _NQS_ be the [&lt;nested query specification&gt;](#_bookmark1123) simply contained in _VQE_.
3. The declared type of _NQS_ shall be a binding table type with a single column _SC_.
4. The _immediately emitting statement_ of a [&lt;nested query specification&gt;](#_bookmark1123) _NQSXX_ is the last [&lt;statement&gt;](#_bookmark1145) simply contained in _NQSXX_.
5. The _emitting result statement_ of a [&lt;nested query specification&gt;](#_bookmark1123) _NQSX_ is defined as follows:
    1. The immediately emitting statement of _NQSX_ shall be a [&lt;linear query statement&gt;](#_bookmark1584).
    2. Case:
        1. If the immediately emitting statement of _NQSX_ implicitly or explicitly simply contains a [&lt;primitive result statement&gt;](#_bookmark1690) _PRSX_, then the emitting result statement of _NQSX_ is _PRSX_.
        2. If the immediately emitting statement of _NQSX_ is a [&lt;focused nested query specification&gt;](#_bookmark1592) or an [&lt;ambient linear query statement&gt;](#_bookmark1594) that immediately contains a [<nested query](#_bookmark1123)

[specification>](#_bookmark1123) _NNQSX_ and the emitting result statement of _NNQSX_ is defined, then the emitting result statement of _NQSX_ is the emitting result statement of _NNQSX_.

- - 1. Otherwise, the emitting result statement of _NQSX_ is “omitted”.

NOTE 312 — This is a recursive definition.

1. The emitting result statement of _NQS_ shall not be “omitted”.
2. Let _PRS_ be the emitting result statement of _NQS_.
3. _PRS_ shall implicitly or explicitly simply contain the [&lt;return statement&gt;](#_bookmark1722) _RS_.

NOTE 313 — The emitting statement of _NQS_ can be a [&lt;select statement&gt;](#_bookmark1758) as long as the syntax transform- ation specified in [Subclause 14.12, “](#_bookmark1757)[<select](#_bookmark1758) [statement>”](#_bookmark1757) yields a [&lt;linear query statement&gt;](#_bookmark1584) that fulfills

the Syntax Rules of this Subclause if it is taken as the emitting statement of _NQS_.

1. Let _RI_ be the only [&lt;return item&gt;](#_bookmark1729) simply contained in _RS_.

NOTE 314 — To fulfill [Syntax Rule 3)](#_bookmark3559), _RS_ can only contain a single [&lt;return item&gt;](#_bookmark1729).

1. One of the following shall be true:
    1. _PRS_ shall contain an [&lt;order by and page statement&gt;](#_bookmark1683) that simply contains a [&lt;limit clause&gt;](#_bookmark2561) LIMIT 1.
    2. [**&lt;value query expression&gt;**](#_bookmark3557)
    3. _PRS_ shall not simply contain a [&lt;group by clause&gt;](#_bookmark2513) and _RI_ shall directly contain an [<aggregate](#_bookmark3731) [function>](#_bookmark3731).
2. The declared type of the incoming working record of _NQS_ is the declared type of the incoming working record of _VQE_.
3. The declared type of the incoming working table of _NQS_ is the material unit binding table type.
4. The declared type of _VQE_ is the column type of the column _SC_.

NOTE 315 — To fulfill [Syntax Rule 3)](#_bookmark3559), the declared type of _NQS_ is a binding table type with a single column

_SC_.

# General Rules

1. In a new child execution context: The General Rules of [Subclause 9.2, “](#_bookmark1136)[<pr](#_bookmark1137)[ocedure body>”](#_bookmark1136) are applied; let _RNQS_ be the result of the application of these rules.
2. Case:
    1. If _RNQS_ is an empty binding table, then the result of _VQE_ is the null value.
    2. Otherwise, _RNQS_ is a binding table comprising a single record with a single field _F_ and the result of _VQE_ is the value of _F_.

# Conformance Rules

1) Without Feature GQ18, “Scalar subqueries”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [<value](#_bookmark3557) [query expression>](#_bookmark3557).

&lt;case expression&gt; ::=

NULLIF [&lt;left paren&gt;](#_bookmark5032) [&lt;value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3470) [&lt;comma&gt;](#_bookmark5022) [&lt;value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3470) [&lt;right paren&gt;](#_bookmark5043)

| COALESCE [&lt;left paren&gt;](#_bookmark5032) [&lt;value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3470)

{ [&lt;comma&gt;](#_bookmark5022) [&lt;value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3470) }... [&lt;right paren&gt;](#_bookmark5043)

# Syntax Rules

1. If a [&lt;case expression&gt;](#_bookmark3574) specifies a [&lt;case abbreviation&gt;](#_bookmark3575), then:
    1. Let _NV_ be the number of [&lt;value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3470)s directly contained in the [&lt;case abbreviation&gt;](#_bookmark3575) and let _Vi_, 1 (one) ≤ _i_ ≤ _NV_, be the _i_\-th such [&lt;value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3470).
    2. NULLIF (_V_1, _V_2) is equivalent to the following [&lt;case specification&gt;](#_bookmark3578):

CASE WHEN _V_1=_V_2 THEN NULL ELSE _V_1 END

- 1. COALESCE (_V_1, _V_2) is equivalent to the following [&lt;case specification&gt;](#_bookmark3578):

CASE

WHEN NOT _V_1 IS NULL THEN _V_1

ELSE _V_2

END

- 1. For any number _n_ ≥ 3 of [&lt;value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3470)s, COALESCE (_V_1, _V_2, ..., _Vn_) is equivalent to the following [&lt;case specification&gt;](#_bookmark3578):

CASE

WHEN NOT _V_1 IS NULL THEN _V_1

ELSE COALESCE (_V_2, ..., _Vn_) END

NOTE 316 — This is a recursive definition.

1. If a [&lt;case specification&gt;](#_bookmark3578) specifies a [&lt;simple case&gt;](#_bookmark3579), then let _CO_ be the [&lt;case operand&gt;](#_bookmark3588).
    1. If any [&lt;when operand&gt;](#_bookmark3592) is [&lt;directed predicate part 2&gt;](#_bookmark3422), [&lt;labeled predicate part 2&gt;](#_bookmark3429), [<source](#_bookmark3439) [predicate part 2>](#_bookmark3439) or [&lt;destination predicate part 2&gt;](#_bookmark3441), then _CO_ shall be [<element variable refer-](#_bookmark2381) [ence>](#_bookmark2381) and every [&lt;when operand&gt;](#_bookmark3592) shall be [&lt;directed predicate part 2&gt;](#_bookmark3422), [<labeled predicate](#_bookmark3429)

[part 2>](#_bookmark3429), [&lt;source predicate part 2&gt;](#_bookmark3439) or [&lt;destination predicate part 2&gt;](#_bookmark3441); otherwise, _CO_ shall not be [&lt;element variable reference&gt;](#_bookmark2381) and no [&lt;when operand&gt;](#_bookmark3592) shall be [<directed predicate part](#_bookmark3422) [2>](#_bookmark3422), [&lt;labeled predicate part 2&gt;](#_bookmark3429), [&lt;source predicate part 2&gt;](#_bookmark3439) or [&lt;destination predicate part 2&gt;](#_bookmark3441).

- 1. Let _N_ be the number of [&lt;simple when clause&gt;](#_bookmark3582)s.
  2. For _i_, 1 (one) ≤ _i_ ≤ _N_:
        1. Let _WOLi_ be the [&lt;when operand list&gt;](#_bookmark3590) of the _i_\-th [&lt;simple when clause&gt;](#_bookmark3582).
        2. Let _Ri_ be the [&lt;result&gt;](#_bookmark3601) of the _i_\-th [&lt;simple when clause&gt;](#_bookmark3582).
        3. Let _M_(_i_) be the number of [&lt;when operand&gt;](#_bookmark3592)s simply contained in _WOLi_.
        4. For _j_, 1 (one) ≤ _j_ ≤ _M_(_i_):
            1. let _WOi_,_j_ be the _j_\-th [&lt;when operand&gt;](#_bookmark3592) simply contained in _WOLi_.
            2. Case:
                1. If _WOi_,_j_ is a [&lt;non-parenthesized value expression primary&gt;](#_bookmark3510), then let _EWOi_,_j_

be:

\= _WOi_,_j_

- 1. [**&lt;case expression&gt;**](#_bookmark3574)
        - - 1. Otherwise, let _EWOi_,_j_ be _WOi_,_j_.
  2. If [&lt;else clause&gt;](#_bookmark3586) is specified, then let _CEEC_ be that [&lt;else clause&gt;](#_bookmark3586); otherwise, let _CEEC_ be the zero-length character string.
  3. The [&lt;simple case&gt;](#_bookmark3579) is equivalent to a [&lt;searched case&gt;](#_bookmark3581) in which the _i_\-th [&lt;searched when clause&gt;](#_bookmark3584) takes the form:

WHEN ( _CO EWO__i_,1 ) OR

... OR

( _CO EWOi_,_M_(_i_) )

THEN _Ri_

- 1. The [&lt;else clause&gt;](#_bookmark3586) of the equivalent [&lt;searched case&gt;](#_bookmark3581) takes the form:

_CEEC_

- 1. The Conformance Rules of the Subclauses of [Clause 19, “Predicates”](#_bookmark3334), are applied to the result of this syntactic transformation.

NOTE 317 — The specific Subclauses of [Clause 19, “Predicates”](#_bookmark3334), are determined by the predicates that are created as a result of the syntactic transformation.

1. At least one [&lt;result&gt;](#_bookmark3601) in a [&lt;case specification&gt;](#_bookmark3578) shall specify a [&lt;result expression&gt;](#_bookmark3603).
2. If an [&lt;else clause&gt;](#_bookmark3586) is not specified, then ELSE NULL is implicit.
3. The Syntax Rules of [Subclause 22.18, “General combination of value types”](#_bookmark5291), are applied with the

set of declared types of all [&lt;result expression&gt;](#_bookmark3603)s in the [&lt;case specification&gt;](#_bookmark3578) as [_DTSET_](#_bookmark5292); let _DT_ be the [_RESTYPE_](#_bookmark5293) returned from the application of those Syntax Rules. The declared type of the [<case spe-](#_bookmark3578) [cification>](#_bookmark3578) is _DT_.

# General Rules

1. Case:
    1. If a [&lt;result&gt;](#_bookmark3601) specifies NULL, then its value is the null value.
    2. Otherwise, a [&lt;result&gt;](#_bookmark3601) specifies a [&lt;value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3470) and its value is the result of that [<value](#_bookmark3470) [expression>](#_bookmark3470).
2. Case:
    1. If the result of the [&lt;search condition&gt;](#_bookmark3337) of some [&lt;searched when clause&gt;](#_bookmark3584) in a [&lt;case specification&gt;](#_bookmark3578) is _True_, then the result of the [&lt;case expression&gt;](#_bookmark3574) is the result of the [&lt;result&gt;](#_bookmark3601) of the first (left- most) [&lt;searched when clause&gt;](#_bookmark3584) whose [&lt;search condition&gt;](#_bookmark3337) evaluates to _True_, cast as the declared type of the [&lt;case specification&gt;](#_bookmark3578).
    2. Otherwise, no [&lt;search condition&gt;](#_bookmark3337) in a [&lt;case specification&gt;](#_bookmark3578) evaluates to _True_ and the result of the [&lt;case expression&gt;](#_bookmark3574) is the result of the [&lt;result&gt;](#_bookmark3601) of the explicit or implicit [&lt;else clause&gt;](#_bookmark3586), cast as the declared type of the [&lt;case specification&gt;](#_bookmark3578).

# Conformance Rules

_None._

# [&lt;cast specification&gt;](#_bookmark3630) Function

Specify a data conversion.

# Format

&lt;cast specification&gt; ::=

CAST [&lt;left paren&gt;](#_bookmark5032) [&lt;cast operand&gt;](#_bookmark3632) AS [&lt;cast target&gt;](#_bookmark3635) [&lt;right paren&gt;](#_bookmark5043)

&lt;cast operand&gt; ::=

[&lt;value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3470)

| [&lt;null literal&gt;](#_bookmark4595)

&lt;cast target&gt; ::=

[&lt;value type&gt;](#_bookmark2878)

# Syntax Rules

1. Let _CS_ be the [&lt;cast specification&gt;](#_bookmark3630).
2. Let _CO_ be the [&lt;cast operand&gt;](#_bookmark3632).
3. Let _TD_ be the data type identified by [&lt;value type&gt;](#_bookmark2878).
4. _TD_ shall not specify an immaterial value type.
5. If _CO_ specifies NULL, then _TD_ shall be nullable, the declared type of _CS_ is _TD_ and no further Syntax Rules of this Subclause are applied; otherwise, _TD_ shall not be an immaterial value type.
6. The declared type of _CS_ is _TD_.
7. If _CO_ is a [&lt;value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3470), then let _SD_ be the declared type of the [&lt;value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3470).
8. If _CO_ is a [&lt;value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3470), then the valid combinations of _TD_ and _SD_ in _CS_ are given in [Table 4,](#_bookmark3638) [“Valid combinations of source and target and types”](#_bookmark3638). “Y” indicates that the combination is syntactically valid without restriction; “M” indicates that the combination is valid subject to other Syntax Rules in this Subclause being satisfied; and “N” indicates that the combination is invalid. The combination of _TD_ and _SD_ shall not be invalid according to this classification.

_SCT_ of _SD_ such that

where _VALUE_ is a [&lt;value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3470) whose declared type is _SCT_, shall be a valid [&lt;cast specification&gt;](#_bookmark3630).

    1. If _SD_ is a regular list value type, then _TD_ shall be a regular list value type.
    2. Let _ESD_ be the list element type of _SD_.
    3. Let _ETD_ be the list element type of _TD_.

CAST ( _VALUE_ AS _ETD_ )

where _VALUE_ is a [&lt;value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3470) of declared type _ESD_, shall be a valid [&lt;cast specification&gt;](#_bookmark3630).

1. If _SD_ is a closed record type and _TD_ is a closed record type, then:
    1. Let _TFNS_ be the set of field type names of _TD_.
    2. The set of field type names of _SD_ shall include _TFNS_.
    3. For every name _FN_ in _TFNS_:
        1. Let _SFVT_ be the value type of the field type with name _FN_ in _SD_.
        2. Let _TFVT_ be the value type of the field type with name _FN_ in _TD_.
        3. The [&lt;cast specification&gt;](#_bookmark3630):

CAST ( _VALUE_ AS _TFVT_ )

where _VALUE_ is a [&lt;value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3470) of declared type _SFVT_, shall be a valid [<cast](#_bookmark3630) [specification>](#_bookmark3630).

# General Rules

1. If _CO_ is a [&lt;value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3470) _VE_, then let _SV_ be the result of _VE_.
2. Case:
    1. If _CO_ is NULL, then the result of _CS_ is the null value and no further General Rules of this Sub- clause are applied.
    2. If _SV_ is the null value, then Case:
        1. If _TD_ is nullable, then the result of _CS_ is the null value and no further General Rules of this Subclause are applied.
        2. Otherwise, _TD_ is material and the following exception condition is raised: _data exception_
            - _invalid value type (22G03)_.
3. Let _STZ_ be the current time zone displacement.
4. Let _TV_ be defined as follows. Case:
    1. If _TD_ is a dynamic union type, then _TV_ is _SV_.
    2. If _SD_ is a dynamic union type and _TD_ is a static value type, then:

Specify a value computed from a collection of records.

COUNT [&lt;left paren&gt;](#_bookmark5032) [&lt;asterisk&gt;](#_bookmark5020) [&lt;right paren&gt;](#_bookmark5043)

1. Let _AF_ be the [&lt;aggregate function&gt;](#_bookmark3731).
2. If _AF_ immediately contains a [&lt;general set function&gt;](#_bookmark3733) that does not specify the [&lt;set quantifier&gt;](#_bookmark3745), then ALL is implicit.
3. _AF_ shall not contain a [&lt;procedure body&gt;](#_bookmark1137).
4. _AF_ shall not simply contain an [&lt;aggregate function&gt;](#_bookmark3731).
5. Let the [&lt;value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3470) or the [&lt;dependent value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3751) _VE_ be defined as follows. Case:
    1. [**&lt;aggregate function&gt;**](#_bookmark3731)
    2. If _AF_ immediately contains a [&lt;general set function&gt;](#_bookmark3733) _GSF_, then _VE_ is the [&lt;value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3470) immediately contained in _GSF_.
    3. If _AF_ immediately contains a [&lt;binary set function&gt;](#_bookmark3735) _BSF_, then _VE_ is the [<dependent value](#_bookmark3751) [expression>](#_bookmark3751) immediately contained in _BSF_.
    4. Otherwise, _VE_ is the [&lt;value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3470) or the [&lt;dependent value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3751) immediately contained in _AF_.
6. Let _DT_ be the declared type of _VE_.
7. If _AF_ immediately contains COUNT, then:
    1. If _AF_ immediately contains [&lt;asterisk&gt;](#_bookmark5020), then _AF_ shall be directly contained in an [<aggregating](#_bookmark3488) [value expression>](#_bookmark3488).
    2. The declared type of the result is an implementation-defined [(ID059)](#_bookmark6133) exact numeric type with scale 0 (zero).
8. If _AF_ immediately contains a [&lt;general set function&gt;](#_bookmark3733), then:
    1. If _AF_ specifies a [&lt;general set function&gt;](#_bookmark3733) whose [&lt;set quantifier&gt;](#_bookmark3745) is DISTINCT, then _VE_ is an operand of a grouping operation.     2. If _AF_ specifies a [&lt;general set function type&gt;](#_bookmark3737) that is MAX or MIN, then _VE_ is an operand of an ordering operation. The Syntax Rules and Conformance Rules of [Subclause 22.14, “Ordering](#_bookmark5263) [operations”](#_bookmark5263), apply.
    3. If MAX or MIN is specified, then the declared type of the result is _DT_.
    4. If SUM or AVG is specified, then:
        1. _DT_ shall be a numeric type.
        2. If SUM is specified and _DT_ is exact numeric with scale _S_, then the declared type of the result is an implementation-defined [(ID095)](#_bookmark6153) exact numeric type with scale _S_.

    4. Let _IVE_ be the [&lt;independent value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3752) simply contained in _AF_.

# [&lt;element_id function&gt;](#_bookmark3808) Function

Generate a unique identifier for a graph element.

# Format

&lt;element_id function&gt; ::=

ELEMENT_ID [&lt;left paren&gt;](#_bookmark5032) [&lt;element variable reference&gt;](#_bookmark2381) [&lt;right paren&gt;](#_bookmark5043)

# Syntax Rules

1. Let _EIF_ be the [&lt;element_id function&gt;](#_bookmark3808).
2. Let _EVR_ be the [&lt;element variable reference&gt;](#_bookmark2381) simply contained in _EIF_. _EIF_ shall have singleton degree of reference.
3. The declared type of [&lt;element_id function&gt;](#_bookmark3808) is an implementation-defined [(ID076)](#_bookmark6146) type that is

permitted as the declared type of an operand of an equality operation according to the Syntax Rules of [Subclause 22.13, “Equality operations”](#_bookmark5252).

# General Rules

1. Let _GRV_ be the result of _EVR_.
2. The result of _EIF_ is defined as follows. Case:
    1. If _GRV_ is the null value, then the result of _EIF_ is the null value.
    2. Otherwise, the result of _EIF_ is an implementation-dependent [(UV004)](#_bookmark6232) value that encapsulates the identity of the referent of _GRV_ for the duration of the currently executing GQL-request.

NOTE 319 — The result of _EIF_ can be but is not guaranteed to be the global object identifier of the referent of _GRV_.

The referenced binding variable of a [&lt;binding variable reference&gt;](#_bookmark3823) declared by a [&lt;graph pattern&gt;](#_bookmark1977) is bound in the [Subclause 22.6, “Application of bindings to evaluate an expression”](#_bookmark5194).

    1. Let _NV_ be the result of the [&lt;numeric value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3965).
    2. If _NV_ is the null value, then the result is the null value and no further General Rules of this Subclause are applied.
    3. If _NV_ is less than 0 (zero), then an exception condition is raised: _data exception — list element error (22G0C)_.
    4. Let _AV_ be the result of the [&lt;list value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3879).
    5. If _AV_ is the null value, then the result is the null value and no further General Rules of this Subclause are applied.
    6. Let _AC_ be the cardinality of _AV_.
    7. If _NV_ is greater than _AC_, then an exception condition is raised: _data exception — list element error (22G0C)_.
    8. Let _N_ be _AC_ − _NV_.
    9. Case:
        1. If _N_ \= 0 (zero), then the result is a list whose cardinality is 0 (zero).
    10. [**&lt;list value function&gt;**](#_bookmark3890)
        1. Otherwise, the result is a list of _N_ elements such that, for _i_, 1 (one) ≤ _i_ ≤ _N_, the value of the _i_\-th element of the result is the value of the _i_\-th element of _AV_.
2. The result of [&lt;elements function&gt;](#_bookmark3893) _EF_ is defined as follows.
    1. Let _PV_ be the result of the [&lt;path value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3854).
    2. If _PV_ is the null value, then the result of _EF_ is the null value; otherwise, the result of _EF_ is the path element list of _PV_.

1. If NOT is specified in a [&lt;boolean test&gt;](#_bookmark3941), then let _BP_ be the contained [&lt;boolean primary&gt;](#_bookmark3946) and let _TV_

- 1. [**&lt;boolean value expression&gt;**](#_bookmark3934)

# General Rules

1. The result is derived by the application of the specified Boolean operators (“AND”, “OR”, “NOT”, and “IS”) to the results derived from each [&lt;boolean primary&gt;](#_bookmark3946). If Boolean operators are not specified, then the result of the [&lt;boolean value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3934) is the result of the specified [&lt;boolean primary&gt;](#_bookmark3946).
2. NOT (_True_) is _False_, NOT (_False_) is _True_, and NOT (_Unknown_) is _Unknown_.
3. [Table 5, “Truth table for the AND Boolean operator”](#_bookmark3956), [Table 6, “Truth table for the OR Boolean](#_bookmark3957) [operator”](#_bookmark3957), and [Table 7, “Truth table for the IS Boolean operator”](#_bookmark3958), specify the semantics of AND, OR, and IS, respectively.

**Table 5 — Truth table for the AND Boolean operator**

| **AND** | **_True_** | **_False_** | **_Unknown_** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **_True_** | _True_ | _False_ | _Unknown_ |
| **_False_** | _False_ | _False_ | _False_ |
| **_Unknown_** | _Unknown_ | _False_ | _Unknown_ |

**Table 6 — Truth table for the OR Boolean operator**

| **OR** | **_True_** | **_False_** | **_Unknown_** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **_True_** | _True_ | _True_ | _True_ |
| **_False_** | _True_ | _False_ | _Unknown_ |
| **_Unkno_****_wn_** | _True_ | _Unkno__wn_ | _Unknown_ |

**Table 7 — Truth table for the IS Boolean operator**

| **IS** | **TRUE** | **FALSE** | **UNKNOWN** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **_True_** | _True_ | _False_ | _False_ |
| **_False_** | _False_ | _True_ | _False_ |
| **_Unknown_** | _False_ | _False_ | _True_ |

# Conformance Rules

1. Without Feature GE07, “Boolean XOR”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [<boolean value](#_bookmark3934) [expression>](#_bookmark3934) that immediately contains XOR.

# Syntax Rules

1. Case:
    1. If the declared type of either operand of a dyadic arithmetic operator is approximate numeric, then the declared type of the result is an implementation-defined [(ID063)](#_bookmark6136) approximate numeric type.
    2. Otherwise, the declared type of both operands of a dyadic arithmetic operator is exact numeric and the declared type of the result is an implementation-defined [(ID064)](#_bookmark6137) exact numeric type, with precision and scale defined as follows:
        1. Let _S1_ and _S2_ be the scale of the first and second operands respectively.
        2. The precision of the result of addition and subtraction is [implementation-defined](#_bookmark6138) [(ID065)](#_bookmark6138), and the scale is the maximum of _S1_ and _S2_.
        3. The precision of the result of multiplication is implementation-defined [(ID066)](#_bookmark6139), and the scale is _S1_ \+ _S2_.
        4. The precision and scale of the result of division are implementation-defined [(ID067)](#_bookmark6140).
2. The declared type of a [&lt;factor&gt;](#_bookmark3971) is that of the immediately contained [&lt;numeric primary&gt;](#_bookmark3973).
3. The declared type of a [&lt;numeric primary&gt;](#_bookmark3973) shall be numeric.
4. If a [&lt;numeric value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3965) immediately contains a [&lt;minus sign&gt;](#_bookmark5034) _NMS_ and immediately contains a [&lt;term&gt;](#_bookmark3968) that is a [&lt;factor&gt;](#_bookmark3971) that immediately contains a [&lt;sign&gt;](#_bookmark4533) that is a [&lt;minus sign&gt;](#_bookmark5034) _FMS_, then there shall be a [&lt;separator&gt;](#_bookmark4906) between _NMS_ and _FMS_.

# General Rules

1. If the result of any [&lt;numeric primary&gt;](#_bookmark3973) simply contained in a [&lt;numeric value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3965) is the null value, then the result of the [&lt;numeric value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3965) is the null value.
2. If the [&lt;numeric value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3965) contains only a [&lt;numeric primary&gt;](#_bookmark3973), then the result of the [<numeric](#_bookmark3965) [value expression>](#_bookmark3965) is the result of the specified [&lt;numeric primary&gt;](#_bookmark3973).
3. The monadic arithmetic operators [&lt;plus sign&gt;](#_bookmark5037) and [&lt;minus sign&gt;](#_bookmark5034) (+ and −, respectively) specify

monadic plus and monadic minus, respectively. Monadic plus does not change its operand. Monadic minus reverses the sign of its operand.

1. The dyadic arithmetic operators [&lt;plus sign&gt;](#_bookmark5037), [&lt;minus sign&gt;](#_bookmark5034), [&lt;asterisk&gt;](#_bookmark5020), and [&lt;solidus&gt;](#_bookmark5044) (+, −, \*, and

/, respectively) specify addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division, respectively. If the value of a divisor is zero, then

Case:

- 1. If a GQL-implementation supports Feature GA01, “IEEE 754 floating point operations”, then the result shall be a value as defined by [IEEE Std 754:2019](#_bookmark8).
  2. Otherwise, an exception condition is raised: _data exception — division by zero (22012)_.

1. If the result of an arithmetic operation is an exact number, then Case:
    1. If the operator is not division and the mathematical result of the operation is not exactly representable with the precision and scale of the declared type of the result, then an exception condition is raised: _data exception — numeric value out of range (22003)_.
    2. If the operator is division and the approximate mathematical result of the operation repres- ented with the precision and scale of the declared type of the result loses one or more leading significant digits after rounding or truncating if necessary, then an exception condition is

raised: _data exception — numeric value out of range (22003)_. The choice of whether to round or truncate is implementation-defined [(IA011)](#_bookmark6100).

1. If the result of an arithmetic operation is an approximate number and the exponent of the approx- imate mathematical result of the operation is not within the implementation-defined [(IL023)](#_bookmark6179)

exponent range for the declared type of the result, then Case:

- 1. If a GQL-implementation supports Feature GA01, “IEEE 754 floating point operations”, then the result shall be a value as defined by [IEEE Std 754:2019](#_bookmark8).
  2. Otherwise, an exception condition is raised: _data exception — numeric value out of range (22003)_.

# Syntax Rules

1. The declared type of the result of [&lt;length expression&gt;](#_bookmark4001) is the implementation-defined [(ID068)](#_bookmark6141) nullable exact numeric type with scale 0 (zero).
2. If a [&lt;cardinality expression&gt;](#_bookmark4002) _CE_ is specified that immediately contains SIZE and the [<list value](#_bookmark3879) [expression>](#_bookmark3879) _LVE_, then _CE_ is effectively replaced by:

CARDINALITY(_LVE_)

1. The declared type _DT_ of the result of a [&lt;cardinality expression&gt;](#_bookmark4002) _CE_ that immediately contains a

[&lt;cardinality expression argument&gt;](#_bookmark4005) _CEA_ is defined as follows:

- 1. Let _DTA_ be the declared type of _CEA_.
  2. _DT_ is the implementation-defined [(ID070)](#_bookmark6143) exact numeric type with scale 0 (zero) to whose nullability the nullability of _DTA_ is assignment-aligned.

**20.22** [**&lt;numeric value function&gt;**](#_bookmark3991)

1. The declared type of the result of [&lt;absolute value expression&gt;](#_bookmark4017) the declared type of the immediately contained [&lt;numeric value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3965).
2. The declared type of the result of [&lt;modulus expression&gt;](#_bookmark4019) is the declared type of the immediately contained [&lt;numeric value expression divisor&gt;](#_bookmark4022).
3. The declared type of the result of [&lt;trigonometric function&gt;](#_bookmark4023) is an implementation-defined [(ID069)](#_bookmark6142) approximate numeric type.
4. The declared type of the result of [&lt;general logarithm function&gt;](#_bookmark4027) is an [implementation-defined](#_bookmark6142) [(ID069)](#_bookmark6142) approximate numeric type.
5. The declared type of the result of [&lt;natural logarithm&gt;](#_bookmark4033) is an implementation-defined [(ID069)](#_bookmark6142) approximate numeric type.
6. The declared type of the result of [&lt;exponential function&gt;](#_bookmark4035) is an implementation-defined [(ID069)](#_bookmark6142) approximate numeric type.
7. The declared type of the result of [&lt;power function&gt;](#_bookmark4037) is an implementation-defined [(ID069)](#_bookmark6142) approximate numeric type.
8. If [&lt;floor function&gt;](#_bookmark4043) or [&lt;ceiling function&gt;](#_bookmark4044) is specified, then Case:
    1. If the declared type of the immediately contained [&lt;numeric value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3965) _NVE_ is exact numeric, then the declared type of the result is exact numeric with [implementation-defined](#_bookmark6144) [(ID074)](#_bookmark6144) precision, with the radix of _NVE_, and with scale 0 (zero).
    2. Otherwise, an approximate numeric with implementation-defined [(ID075)](#_bookmark6145) precision.
9. If [&lt;common logarithm&gt;](#_bookmark4031) is specified, then let _NVE_ be the simply contained [<numeric value expres-](#_bookmark3965) [sion>](#_bookmark3965). The [&lt;common logarithm&gt;](#_bookmark4031) is equivalent to:

LOG (10, _NVE_)

1. If [&lt;square root&gt;](#_bookmark4041) is specified, then let _NVE_ be the simply contained [&lt;numeric value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3965). The [&lt;square root&gt;](#_bookmark4041) is equivalent to:

POWER (_NVE_, 0.5)

# General Rules

1. If the [&lt;char length expression&gt;](#_bookmark4008) _CLX_ is specified, then let the character string _CSV_ be the result of the [&lt;character string value expression&gt;](#_bookmark4134) immediately contained in _CLX_.

Case:

- 1. If _CSV_ is material, then the result of _CLX_ is the (character string) length of _CSV_.

NOTE 331 — The (character string) length of _CSV_ is defined in [Subclause 4.16.3, “Character string](#_bookmark744) [types”](#_bookmark744) as the number of characters in the sequence of characters comprising _CSV_.

- 1. Otherwise, the result of _CLX_ is the null value.

1. If the [&lt;byte length expression&gt;](#_bookmark4012) _BLX_ is specified, then let the byte string _BSV_ be the result of the

[&lt;byte string value expression&gt;](#_bookmark4140) immediately contained in _BLX_. Case:

- 1. If _BSV_ is material, then the result of _BLX_ is the (byte string) length of _BSV_.
  2. [**&lt;numeric value function&gt;**](#_bookmark3991)

NOTE 332 — The (byte string) length of _BSV_ is defined in [Subclause 4.16.4, “Byte string types”](#_bookmark765) as the number of bytes in the sequence of bytes comprising _BSV_.

- 1. Otherwise, the result of _BLX_ is the null value.

1. If the [&lt;path length expression&gt;](#_bookmark4015) _PLX_ is specified, then let the path value _PSV_ be the result of the

[&lt;path value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3854) immediately contained in _PLX_. Case:

- 1. If _PSV_ is material, then the result of _PLX_ is the (path value) length of _PSV_.

NOTE 333 — The (path value) length of _PSV_ is defined in [Subclause 4.15.2, “Path value types”](#_bookmark655) as the number of edge reference values in the path element list _PEL_ of _PSV_, if _PEL_ contains at least one node reference value; otherwise, the null value.

- 1. Otherwise, the result of _PLX_ is the null value.

1. If the [&lt;cardinality expression&gt;](#_bookmark4002) _CE_ is specified, then let _CER_ be the result of the [<cardinality](#_bookmark4005) [expression argument>](#_bookmark4005) immediately contained in _CE_ and the result of _CE_ is defined as follows.

Case:

- 1. If _CER_ is a binding table reference value whose referent is _BT_, then the result of _CE_ is the car- dinality of _BT_.
  2. If _CER_ is a path value _PV_, then the result of _CE_ is the cardinality of _PV_.
  3. If _CER_ is a list value _LV_, then the result of _CE_ is the cardinality of _LV_.
  4. If _CER_ is a record _REC_, then the result of _CE_ is the cardinality of _REC_.
  5. Otherwise, _CER_ is the null value and the result of _CE_ is the null value.

1. If [&lt;absolute value expression&gt;](#_bookmark4017) is specified, then let _N_ be the result of the immediately contained

[&lt;numeric value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3965). Case:

- 1. If _N_ is the null value, then the result is the null value.
  2. If _N_ ≥ 0, then the result is _N_.
  3. Otherwise, the result is −1 \* _N_. If −1 \* _N_ is not representable by the declared type of the result, then an exception condition is raised: _data exception — numeric value out of range (22003)_.

1. If [&lt;modulus expression&gt;](#_bookmark4019) is specified, then let _N_ be the result of the immediately contained [<numeric](#_bookmark4021) [v](#_bookmark4021)alue expression dividend> and let _M_ be the result of the immediately contained [<numeric value](#_bookmark4022) [expression divisor>](#_bookmark4022).

Case:

- 1. If at least one of _N_ and _M_ is the null value, then the result is the null value.
  2. If _M_ is zero, then an exception condition is raised: _data exception — division by zero (22012)_.
  3. Otherwise, the result is the unique exact numeric value _R_ with scale 0 (zero) such that all of the following are true:
        1. _R_ has the same sign as _N_.
        2. The absolute value of _R_ is less than the absolute value of _M_.
        3. For some exact numeric value _K_ with scale 0 (zero), _N_ \= _M_ \* _K_ \+ _R_.
  4. [**&lt;numeric value function&gt;**](#_bookmark3991)

1. If [&lt;trigonometric function&gt;](#_bookmark4023) is specified, then let _V_ be the result of the immediately contained

[&lt;numeric value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3965) that represents an angle expressed in radians. Case:

- 1. If _V_ is the null value, then the result is the null value.
  2. Otherwise, let _OP_ be the [&lt;trigonometric function name&gt;](#_bookmark4025). Case:
        1. If _OP_ is ACOS, then Case:
            1. If _V_ is less than −1 (negative one) or _V_ is greater than 1 (one), then an exception condition is raised: _data exception — numeric value out of range (22003)_.
            2. Otherwise, the result of the [&lt;trigonometric function&gt;](#_bookmark4023) is the inverse cosine of _V_.
        2. If _OP_ is ASIN, then Case:
            1. If _V_ is less than −1 (negative one) or _V_ is greater than 1 (one), then an exception condition is raised: _data exception — numeric value out of range (22003)_.
            2. Otherwise, the result of the [&lt;trigonometric function&gt;](#_bookmark4023) is the inverse sine of _V_.
        3. If _OP_ is ATAN, then the result is the inverse tangent of _V_.
        4. If _OP_ is COS, then the result is the cosine of _V_.
        5. If _OP_ is COSH, then the result is the hyperbolic cosine of _V_.
        6. If _OP_ is SIN, then the result is the sine of _V_.
        7. If _OP_ is SINH, then the result is the hyperbolic sine of _V_.
        8. If _OP_ is TAN, then the result is the tangent of _V_.
        9. If _OP_ is TANH, then the result is the hyperbolic tangent of _V_.
        10. If _OP_ is COT, then the result is the cotangent of _V_.
        11. If _OP_ is DEGREES, then the result is the value of _V_, taken to be in radians, expressed as degrees.
        12. If _OP_ is RADIANS, then the result is the value of _V_, taken to be in degrees, expressed as radians.

1. If [&lt;general logarithm function&gt;](#_bookmark4027) is specified, then let _VB_ be the result of the [&lt;general logarithm base&gt;](#_bookmark4029) and let _VA_ be the result of the [&lt;general logarithm argument&gt;](#_bookmark4030).

Case:

- 1. If at least one of _VA_ and _VB_ is the null value, then the result is the null value.
  2. If _VA_ is negative or 0 (zero), then an exception condition is raised: _data exception — numeric value out of range (22003)_.
  3. If _VB_ is negative, 0 (zero), or 1 (one), then an exception condition is raised: _data exception — numeric value out of range (22003)_.
  4. Otherwise, the result is the logarithm with base _VB_ of _VA_.
  5. [**&lt;numeric value function&gt;**](#_bookmark3991)

1. If [&lt;natural logarithm&gt;](#_bookmark4033) is specified, then let _V_ be the result of the immediately contained [<numeric](#_bookmark3965) [value expression>](#_bookmark3965).

Case:

- 1. If _V_ is the null value, then the result is the null value.
  2. If _V_ is 0 (zero) or negative, then an exception condition is raised: _data exception — invalid argument for natural logarithm (2201E)_.
  3. Otherwise, the result is the natural logarithm of _V_.

1. If [&lt;exponential function&gt;](#_bookmark4035) is specified, then let _V_ be the result of the immediately contained [<numeric](#_bookmark3965) [value expression>](#_bookmark3965).

Case:

- 1. If _V_ is the null value, then the result is the null value.
  2. Otherwise, the result is _e_ (the base of natural logarithms) raised to the power _V_. If the result is not representable in the declared type of the result, then an exception condition is raised: _data exception — numeric value out of range (22003)_.

1. If [&lt;power function&gt;](#_bookmark4037) is specified, then let _NVEB_ be the [&lt;numeric value expression base&gt;](#_bookmark4039), then let _VB_ be the result of _NVEB_, let _NVEE_ be the [&lt;numeric value expression exponent&gt;](#_bookmark4040), and let _VE_ be the result of _NVEE_.

Case:

- 1. If at least one of _VB_ and _VE_ is the null value, then the result is the null value.
  2. If _VB_ is 0 (zero) and _VE_ is negative, then an exception condition is raised: _data exception — invalid argument for power function (2201F)_.
  3. If _VB_ is 0 (zero) and _VE_ is 0 (zero), then the result is 1 (one).
  4. If _VB_ is 0 (zero) and _VE_ is positive, then the result is 0 (zero).
  5. If _VB_ is negative and _VE_ is not equal to an exact numeric value with scale 0 (zero), then an exception condition is raised: _data exception — invalid argument for power function (2201F)_.
  6. If _VB_ is negative and _VE_ is equal to an exact numeric value with scale 0 (zero) that is an even number, then the result is the result of

EXP(_NVEE_\*LN(−_NVEB_))

- 1. If _VB_ is negative and _VE_ is equal to an exact numeric value with scale 0 (zero) that is an odd number, then the result is the result of

−EXP(_NVEE_\*LN(−_NVEB_))

- 1. Otherwise, the result is the result of

EXP(_NVEE_\*LN(_NVEB_))

1. If [&lt;floor function&gt;](#_bookmark4043) is specified, then let _V_ be the result of the immediately contained [<numeric value](#_bookmark3965) [expression>](#_bookmark3965) _NVE_.

Case:

- 1. If _V_ is the null value, then the result is the null value.
  2. Otherwise,
  3. [**&lt;numeric value function&gt;**](#_bookmark3991)

Case:

- - 1. If the declared type of _NVE_ is exact numeric, then the result is the greatest exact numeric value with scale 0 (zero) that is less than or equal to _V_. If this result is not representable by the declared type of the result, then an exception condition is raised: _data exception_

_— numeric value out of range (22003)_.

- - 1. Otherwise, the result is the greatest whole number that is less than or equal to _V_. If this result is not representable by the declared type of the result, then an exception condition is raised: _data exception — numeric value out of range (22003)_.

1. If [&lt;ceiling function&gt;](#_bookmark4044) is specified, then let _V_ be the result of the immediately contained [<numeric](#_bookmark3965) [value expression>](#_bookmark3965) _NVE_.

Case:

- 1. If _V_ is the null value, then the result is the null value.
  2. Otherwise, Case:
        1. If the declared type of _NVE_ is exact numeric, then the result is the least exact numeric value with scale 0 (zero) that is greater than or equal to _V_. If this result is not repres- entable by the declared type of the result, then an exception condition is raised: _data exception — numeric value out of range (22003)_.
        2. Otherwise, the result is the least whole number that is greater than or equal to _V_. If this result is not representable by the declared type of the result, then an exception condition is raised: _data exception — numeric value out of range (22003)_.

# Conformance Rules

1. Without Feature GF01, “Enhanced numeric functions”, conforming GQL language shall not contain an [&lt;absolute value expression&gt;](#_bookmark4017), a [&lt;modulus expression&gt;](#_bookmark4019), a [&lt;floor function&gt;](#_bookmark4043), a [&lt;ceiling function&gt;](#_bookmark4044), or a [&lt;square root&gt;](#_bookmark4041).
2. Without Feature GF02, “Trigonometric functions”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a

[&lt;trigonometric function&gt;](#_bookmark4023).

1. Without Feature GF03, “Logarithmic functions”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a

[&lt;general logarithm function&gt;](#_bookmark4027), a [&lt;common logarithm&gt;](#_bookmark4031), a [&lt;natural logarithm&gt;](#_bookmark4033), an [<exponential](#_bookmark4035) [function>](#_bookmark4035), or a [&lt;power function&gt;](#_bookmark4037).

1. Without Feature GV35, “Byte string types”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [<byte](#_bookmark4012) [length expression>](#_bookmark4012).
2. Without Feature GF04, “Enhanced path functions”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a

[&lt;path length expression&gt;](#_bookmark4015).

1. Without Feature GF12, “CARDINALITY function”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a

[&lt;cardinality expression&gt;](#_bookmark4002) that immediately contains CARDINALITY.

1. Without Feature GF13, “SIZE function”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [<cardinality](#_bookmark4002) [expression>](#_bookmark4002) that immediately contains SIZE.

            4. If [&lt;trim character string&gt;](#_bookmark4181) is not specified, then [&lt;space&gt;](#_bookmark5018) is implicit.
        2. Otherwise, let _SRC_ be [&lt;trim source&gt;](#_bookmark4176). TRIM ( _SRC_ ) is equivalent to:

1. If the [&lt;multi-character trim function&gt;](#_bookmark4172) _MCTF_ is specified, then:
    1. The declared type of the result is the declared type of the [&lt;trim source&gt;](#_bookmark4176) _TS_ immediately con- tained in _MCTF_.

# Syntax Rules

1. If the declared type of the simply contained [&lt;datetime primary&gt;](#_bookmark4268) is a zoned datetime type, then the declared type of [&lt;datetime value expression&gt;](#_bookmark4264) is the zoned datetime type; otherwise, the declared type of [&lt;datetime value expression&gt;](#_bookmark4264) is the local datetime type.

# General Rules

1. If the result of a [&lt;datetime primary&gt;](#_bookmark4268) is not a temporal instant, then an exception condition is raised:

_data exception — invalid value type (22G03)_.

1. If the result of any [&lt;datetime primary&gt;](#_bookmark4268), [&lt;duration value expression&gt;](#_bookmark4339), [&lt;datetime value expression&gt;](#_bookmark4264), or [&lt;duration term&gt;](#_bookmark4348) simply contained in a [&lt;datetime value expression&gt;](#_bookmark4264) is the null value, then the result of the [&lt;datetime value expression&gt;](#_bookmark4264) is the null value.
2. The result of a [&lt;datetime primary&gt;](#_bookmark4268) is the result of the immediately contained [<value expression](#_bookmark3507) [primary>](#_bookmark3507) or [&lt;datetime value function&gt;](#_bookmark4279).
3. If a [&lt;datetime value expression&gt;](#_bookmark4264) immediately contains the operator [&lt;plus sign&gt;](#_bookmark5037) or [&lt;minus sign&gt;](#_bookmark5034), then the result is evaluated as specified in [ISO 8601-2:2019](#_bookmark5), 14, “Date and time arithmetic”.

# Conformance Rules

[function>](#_bookmark4291) or a [&lt;localtime function&gt;](#_bookmark4286).

# Format

&lt;datetime value function&gt; ::=

[&lt;date function&gt;](#_bookmark4280)

&lt;time function&gt; ::= CURRENT_TIME

LOCAL_TIME \[ [&lt;left paren&gt;](#_bookmark5032) \[ [&lt;time function parameters&gt;](#_bookmark4297) \] [&lt;right paren&gt;](#_bookmark5043) \]

[&lt;date string&gt;](#_bookmark4568)

# Syntax Rules

1. CURRENT_DATE is equivalent to:

DATE()

1. CURRENT_TIME is equivalent to:

ZONED_TIME()

1. LOCAL_TIME is equivalent to:

LOCAL_TIME()

- 1. [**&lt;datetime value function&gt;**](#_bookmark4279)

1. CURRENT_TIMESTAMP is equivalent to:

ZONED_DATETIME()

1. LOCAL_TIMESTAMP is equivalent to:

LOCAL_DATETIME()

1. The declared type of a [&lt;date function&gt;](#_bookmark4280) is the date type.
2. The declared type of a [&lt;time function&gt;](#_bookmark4282) is the zoned time type.
3. The declared type of a [&lt;datetime function&gt;](#_bookmark4288) is the zoned datetime type.
4. The declared type of a [&lt;localtime function&gt;](#_bookmark4286) is the local time type.
5. The declared type of a [&lt;localdatetime function&gt;](#_bookmark4291) is the local datetime type.

# General Rules

1. If the current request timestamp is “not set”, then the current request timestamp is set to the current date and time at an implementation-dependent [(US009)](#_bookmark6227) point in time before the evaluation of a

[&lt;datetime value function&gt;](#_bookmark4279).

NOTE 334 — This can happen at any implementation-dependent [(US009)](#_bookmark6227) point in time after the setting of the request timestamp to “not set”; the determination of the request timestamp need not wait for evaluation of a [&lt;datetime value function&gt;](#_bookmark4279).

1. If the set of [&lt;field name&gt;](#_bookmark4437)s simply contained in a [&lt;date function parameters&gt;](#_bookmark4294) is not one of:
    1. 'year'
    2. 'year' and 'month'
    3. 'year', 'month', and 'day'

then an exception is raised: _data exception — invalid date, time, or datetime function field name (22G05)_.

1. If the set of [&lt;field name&gt;](#_bookmark4437)s simply contained in a [&lt;time function parameters&gt;](#_bookmark4297) is not one of:
    1. 'hour'
    2. 'hour' and 'minute'
    3. 'hour', 'minute', and 'second'
    4. 'hour', 'minute', 'second' and one of 'millisecond', 'microsecond', and 'nanosecond'.
    5. 'timezone', if [&lt;time function parameters&gt;](#_bookmark4297) is simply contained in a [&lt;time function&gt;](#_bookmark4282).

then an exception is raised: _data exception — invalid date, time, or datetime function field name (22G05)_.

1. If the set of [&lt;field name&gt;](#_bookmark4437)s contained in a [&lt;datetime function parameters&gt;](#_bookmark4299) is not one of:
    1. 'year', 'month', 'day', and any of the set of [&lt;field name&gt;](#_bookmark4437)s permitted in a [<time function para-](#_bookmark4297) [meters>](#_bookmark4297).
    2. 'timezone', if [&lt;datetime function parameters&gt;](#_bookmark4299) is simply contained in a [&lt;datetime function&gt;](#_bookmark4288).

then an exception is raised: _data exception — invalid date, time, or datetime function field name (22G05)_.

# Conformance Rules

1) Without Feature GV41, “Temporal types: duration support”, conforming GQL language shall not contain a [&lt;duration value expression&gt;](#_bookmark4339).

- 1. [**&lt;duration value function&gt;**](#_bookmark4395)

# [&lt;duration value function&gt;](#_bookmark4395) Function

Specify a function yielding a value of a temporal duration type.

# Format

&lt;duration value function&gt; ::=

[&lt;duration function&gt;](#_bookmark4396)

| [&lt;duration absolute value function&gt;](#_bookmark4400)

&lt;duration function&gt; ::=

DURATION [&lt;left paren&gt;](#_bookmark5032) [&lt;duration function parameters&gt;](#_bookmark4398) [&lt;right paren&gt;](#_bookmark5043)

&lt;duration function parameters&gt; ::=

[&lt;duration string&gt;](#_bookmark4578)

| [&lt;record constructor&gt;](#_bookmark3915)

&lt;duration absolute value function&gt; ::=

ABS [&lt;left paren&gt;](#_bookmark5032) [&lt;duration value expression&gt;](#_bookmark4339) [&lt;right paren&gt;](#_bookmark5043)

# Syntax Rules

_None._

# General Rules

1. If [&lt;duration function parameters&gt;](#_bookmark4398) immediately contains a [&lt;duration string&gt;](#_bookmark4578) _DS_, then Case:
    1. If _DS_ conforms to the Format of [&lt;iso8601 years and months&gt;](#_bookmark4580) without a [&lt;separator&gt;](#_bookmark4906) between the fields, then the declared type of the [&lt;duration function&gt;](#_bookmark4396) is the year and month-based duration type.
    2. If _DS_ conforms to the Format of [&lt;iso8601 days and time&gt;](#_bookmark4585) without a [&lt;separator&gt;](#_bookmark4906) between the fields, then the declared type of the [&lt;duration function&gt;](#_bookmark4396) is the day and time-based duration type.
    3. Otherwise, an exception condition is raised: _data exception — invalid duration format (22G0H)_.
2. If [&lt;duration function parameters&gt;](#_bookmark4398) immediately contains a [&lt;record constructor&gt;](#_bookmark3915) _RVS_, then Case:
    1. If the declared type of _RVS_ specifies the fields 'years' or 'months', then the declared type of the [&lt;duration function&gt;](#_bookmark4396) is the year and month-based duration type.
    2. If the declared type of _RVS_ specifies the fields 'days', 'hours', 'minutes', 'seconds', 'milliseconds', 'microseconds', or 'nanoseconds', then the declared type of the [&lt;duration function&gt;](#_bookmark4396) is the day and time-based duration type.
    3. Otherwise, an exception condition is raised: _data exception — invalid duration function field name (22G07)_.
    4. [**&lt;duration value function&gt;**](#_bookmark4395)
3. If [&lt;duration function parameters&gt;](#_bookmark4398) immediately contains a [&lt;record constructor&gt;](#_bookmark3915), then the record is transformed into an equivalent [&lt;duration string&gt;](#_bookmark4578) as follows:
    1. If _RVS_ specifies the fields 'years' or 'months', then:
        1. Let _YYS_ be defined as follows:
            1. Let _YY_ be defined as follows. If _RVS_ does not specify the 'years' field, then _YY_ is 0 (zero); otherwise, _YY_ is the result of the [&lt;value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3470) in the 'years' field of _RVS_.
            2. _YYS_ is the result of:

CAST(_YY_ AS STRING)

- - 1. Let _MMS_ be defined as follows:
            1.  Let _MM_ be defined as follows. If _RVS_ does not specify the 'month' field, then _MM_ is 0 (zero); otherwise, _MM_ is the result of the [&lt;value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3470) in the 'months' field of _RVS_.
            2.  _MMS_ is the result of:

CAST(_MM_ AS STRING)

- - 1. Let _DS_ be the result of:

'P' || _YYS_ || 'Y' || _MMS_ || 'M'

- 1. Otherwise,
        1. Let _DDS_ be defined as follows:
            1. Let _DD_ be defined as follows. If _RVS_ does not specify the 'days' field, then _DD_ is 0 (zero); otherwise, _DD_ is the result of the [&lt;value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3470) in the 'days' field of _RVS_.
            2. _DDS_ is the result of:

CAST(_DD_ AS STRING)

- - 1. Let _HRS_ be defined as follows:
            1.  Let _HR_ be defined as follows. If _RVS_ does not specify the 'hours' field, then _HR_ is 0 (zero); otherwise, _HR_ is the result of the [&lt;value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3470) in the 'hours' field of _RVS_.
            2.  _HRS_ is the result of:

CAST(_HR_ AS STRING)

- - 1. Let _MINS_ be defined as follows:
            1.  Let _MIN_ be defined as follows. If _RVS_ does not specify the 'minutes' field, then _MIN_ is 0 (zero); otherwise, _MIN_ is the result of the [&lt;value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3470) in the 'minutes' field of _RVS_.
            2.  _MINS_ is the result of:

CAST(_MIN_ AS STRING)

- - 1. Let _SECS_ be defined as follows:

    1. [**&lt;duration value function&gt;**](#_bookmark4395)
        - 1. Let _SEC_ be defined as follows. If _RVS_ does not specify the 'seconds' field, then _SEC_ is 0 (zero); otherwise, _SEC_ is the result of the [&lt;value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3470) in the 'seconds' field of _RVS_.
          2. _SECS_ is the result of:

CAST(_SEC_ AS STRING)

- - 1. Let _SUBSECS_ be defined as follows. Case:
            1.  If _RVS_ specifies the 'milliseconds' field, then:
                1.  Let _MISEC_ be the result of the [&lt;value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3470) in the 'milliseconds' field of _RVS_.
                2.  Let _MISECC_ be the result of:

CAST(_MISEC_ AS STRING)

- - - - 1. If CHAR_LENGTH(_MISECC_) < 3, then _SUBSECS_ is _MISECC_ prepended with 0’s (zeroes) to a length of 3; otherwise, _SUBSECS_ is _MISECC_.

            1. If _RVS_ specifies the 'microseconds' field, then:
                1. Let _MYSEC_ be the result of the [&lt;value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3470) in the 'microseconds' field of _RVS_.
                2. Let _MYSECC_ be the result of:

CAST(_MYSEC_ AS STRING)

- - - - 1. If CHAR_LENGTH(_MYSECC_) < 6, then _SUBSECS_ is _MYSECC_ prepended with 0’s (zeroes) to a length of 6; otherwise, _SUBSECS_ is _MYSECC_.

            1. If _RVS_ specifies the 'nanoseconds' field, then:
                1. Let _NASEC_ be the result of the [&lt;value expression&gt;](#_bookmark3470) in the 'nanoseconds' field of _RVS_.
                2. Let _NASECC_ be the result of:

CAST(_NASEC_ AS STRING)

- - - - 1. If CHAR_LENGTH(_NASECC_) < 9, then _SUBSECS_ is _NASECC_ prepended with 0’s (zeroes) to a length of 9; otherwise, _SUBSECS_ is _NASECC_.

            1. Otherwise, _SUBSECS_ is '000'.

        1. Let _SECSNSUBSECS_ be the result of:

_SECS_ || '.' || _SUBSECS_ || 'S'

without intervening whitespace.

- - 1. _DS_ is the result of:

'P' || _DDS_ || 'DT' || _HRS_ || 'H' || _MINS_ || 'M' || _SECSNSUBSECS_

without intervening whitespace.

- 1. [**&lt;duration value function&gt;**](#_bookmark4395)

1. The result of the [&lt;duration function&gt;](#_bookmark4396) is the duration represented by the immediately contained

[&lt;duration string&gt;](#_bookmark4578), as defined in [ISO 8601-1:2019](#_bookmark4), 5.5.2, “Duration” as extended by [ISO 8601-2:2019](#_bookmark5), 4.3, “Additional explicit forms” and [ISO 8601-2:2019](#_bookmark5), 4.4, “Numerical extensions”.

1. If [&lt;duration absolute value function&gt;](#_bookmark4400) is specified, then let _N_ be the result of the [<duration value](#_bookmark4339) [expression>](#_bookmark4339).

Case:

- 1. If _N_ is the null value, then the result is the null value.
  2. If _N_ ≥ 0 (zero), then the result is _N_.
  3. Otherwise, the result is −1 \* _N_.

# Syntax Rules

1. The [&lt;identifier&gt;](#_bookmark4744)s that are valid [&lt;authorization identifier&gt;](#_bookmark4419)s are implementation-defined [(IV015)](#_bookmark6190).
2. The _name_ specified by a [&lt;delimited identifier&gt;](#_bookmark4749) or a [&lt;non-delimited identifier&gt;](#_bookmark4746) _DIONDI_ is the canonical name form of _DIONDI_.

NOTE 335 — See [Syntax Rule 24)](#_bookmark4964) of [Subclause 21.3, “](#_bookmark4737)[<t](#_bookmark4738)[oken>,](#_bookmark4737) [<separ](#_bookmark4906)[ator>, and](#_bookmark4737) [&lt;identifier&gt;](#_bookmark4744)[”](#_bookmark4737) for the definition of canonical name form.

1. A _system-generated name_ is the canonical name form of a system-generated identifier.

# General Rules

1. An [&lt;authorization identifier&gt;](#_bookmark4419) identifies a principal and a set of privileges for that principal.
2. An [&lt;object name&gt;](#_bookmark4421) identifies a GQL-object.
3. An [&lt;object name or binding variable&gt;](#_bookmark4422) identifies a GQL-object or a binding variable.
4. A [&lt;directory name&gt;](#_bookmark4424) identifies a GQL-directory.
5. A [&lt;schema name&gt;](#_bookmark4425) identifies a GQL-schema.
6. A [&lt;graph name&gt;](#_bookmark4426) identifies a graph.
7. A [&lt;delimited graph name&gt;](#_bookmark4427) identifies a graph.
8. A [&lt;graph type name&gt;](#_bookmark4429) identifies a graph type.
9. A [&lt;node type name&gt;](#_bookmark4430) identifies a node type.
10. An [&lt;edge type name&gt;](#_bookmark4431) identifies an edge type.
11. A [&lt;binding table name&gt;](#_bookmark4432) identifies a binding table.
12. A [&lt;delimited binding table name&gt;](#_bookmark4433) identifies a binding table.
    1. **Names and variables**
13. A [&lt;procedure name&gt;](#_bookmark4434) identifies a procedure.
14. A [&lt;label name&gt;](#_bookmark4435) identifies a label.
15. A [&lt;property name&gt;](#_bookmark4436) identifies a property of a GQL-object.
16. A [&lt;field name&gt;](#_bookmark4437) identifies a field of a record, a field type of a record, or a column of a binding table.
17. A [&lt;parameter name&gt;](#_bookmark4439) identifies a parameter.
18. A variable is a graph variable, a graph pattern variable, a binding table variable, a value variable, or a binding variable.
19. A [&lt;graph pattern variable&gt;](#_bookmark4441) identifies a graph pattern variable. A graph pattern variable is an element variable, a path variable, or a subpath variable.
20. A [&lt;path or subpath variable&gt;](#_bookmark4442) identifies a path variable or a subpath variable.
21. An [&lt;element variable&gt;](#_bookmark4443) identifies an element variable.
22. A [&lt;path variable&gt;](#_bookmark4444) identifies a path variable. Path variables are binding variables.
23. A [&lt;subpath variable&gt;](#_bookmark4445) identifies a subpath variable.
24. A [&lt;binding variable&gt;](#_bookmark4447) identifies a binding variable.
